title: [Tracking][Spec Decode] Adaptive DSpark Bring-Up Tracker
body: Tracking issue to organize the adaptive verification support for DSpark speculative decoding ## Backend Support Adaptive verification has a firm requirement that the attention backend must not use the CPU-side query lengths as a source-of-truth, instead using the gpu tensors (so that we can run the confidence-based assignment on the GPU without synchronizing the CPU). Additionally, kernels must be able to support decode batches where requests have different query lengths per request. Currently, the following backends are known to support variable lengths: - FLASH_ATTN - DSV4 Attention **TODO**: - Hybrid / Linear attention (requires significant effort) - - Mamba (for NVIDIA Nemotron models) - - GDN (for Qwen3.x models) - - Kimi KDA (for Kimi K3) - DSV3-style MLA - FlashInfer GQA: - - TRTLLM kernel support exists, just needs to be plugged into vLLM. Minor change. - - CUTLASS backend of FlashInfer may need additional support to avoid the cpu query lengths ## Online Profiling The initial version does profiling at startup to estimate the verification step time by replaying the recorded CUDA graphs. This is known to have some drift: We want to extend this to fully online profiling in the future. However, there are some challenges that make this tricky: - Online profiling may lead to "dead spots": one-time latency spikes make a certain batch size appear unattractive, leading to the adaptive verifier to never select that batch size, which leads to negative feedback and stale data limiting our range of profiled values. Generally there is an "exploration vs exploitation" problem here, as well as a requirement for some way to detect and eliminate outliers (such as those caused by JIT compilation) - Variable sequence lengths make it hard to measure a single reliable estimate of execution time for a given number of tokens. In practice we will want some way to account for this: either tracking measured points in 2D (num_tokens, max_seq_len or mean_seq_len), or estimating the overhead added per-token of KV reads ## Tuning Confidence Scores The confidence scores are not always perfectly calibrated. In particular, it seems like the deeper positions have higher variance and some bias in their expectation. The DSpark paper suggests [Sequential Temperature Scaling (STS)](https://arxiv.org/html/2607.05147v1) as an online solution to calibrating these estimates. I did not see much benefit when adding this feature, but we should experiment more thoroughly and assess the potential benefit of improved confidence estimates. Here are the results from one run with DSV4-Flash-0731: ## First-Class Observability ### Exposing Timings and Adaptive-SD Metrics Now that we are profiling different phases of the worker execution (model runner, proposer), and tracking the step time by batch size, we will want to expose these to the user for observability. This will help with performance tuning and development, as well as for monitoring of production deployments at scale. We will want to propagate the metrics to both the prometheus / frontend, as well as to the iteration-level logging feature. We will also want some way to report our other metrics for adaptive verification: confidence success rate (mismatch between "expected" AL and "achieved" AL), performance model reliability (difference between "expected" step time and "actual" step time), etc. ### Benchmarking Compatibility Adaptive speculative decoding will change what it means for speculative decoding to have high acceptance rate. AL is no longer a "golden" metric for success. As a start, this PR enables detailed, per-request and per-step speculative decoding metrics to be exposed in the OpenAI response. This can be used to report exact speculative decoding statistics and aggregated on the client to fit the use-case. https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48915 ## Feature Compatibility - [ ] Logprob extraction support ([see here](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47808#discussion_r3723768178))

title: [Bug]: [ROCm] DeepSeek-V4 sparse indexer is a dead end on non-MI3xx GPUs, though working torch fallbacks exist in-tree
body:
### Your current environment

<details>
<summary>Abridged environment (key versions; 2-node cluster)</summary>

```text
vLLM:    0.26.1.dev0+g568afb3a1.d20260808
PyTorch: 2.12.0+rocm7.14.0
Python:  3.14.4
ROCm:    7.14, RCCL 2.30.4
GPU:     2x AMD Radeon 8060S (Strix Halo APU, gfx1151), 1 GPU per node
Nodes:   2-node Ray cluster, TP=2, Thunderbolt interconnect (RCCL NET/Socket)
Model:   DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 (quantization=deepseek_v4_fp8, fp8_ds_mla KV cache)
AITER:   built from source (ROCm/aiter @ main, PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH=gfx1151); imports and JITs fine
```

Serve command:

```bash
vllm serve /models/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 \
  --max-model-len 8192 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.8 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
  --distributed-executor-backend ray
```

</details>

### 🐛 Describe the bug

Three interacting gates currently make DeepSeek-V4 (and presumably any model using the DSA sparse indexer with `fp8_ds_mla`) impossible to run on ROCm GPUs other than MI3xx — while torch reference fallbacks for exactly this situation already exist in-tree, are wired with correct arguments, and work when made reachable (verified on a 2× gfx1151 cluster, now serving).

**Gate 1 — the indexer requires AITER.** During the profiling forward pass, `sparse_attn_indexer.py::forward_hip` raises:

```
Sparse attention indexer ROCm path is only supported on AITER.
Please enable aiter with VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1
```

**Gate 2 — the advice in that error cannot work.** `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1` is silently ignored on non-MI3xx because `vllm/_aiter_ops.py` hard-gates on platform:

```python
def is_aiter_found_and_supported() -> bool:
    ...
    if current_platform.is_rocm() and IS_AITER_FOUND:
        from vllm.platforms.rocm import on_mi3xx
        return on_mi3xx()
    return False
```

So the user is sent in a loop: the error demands an env var that the platform gate then discards, even with AITER installed and importable.

**Gate 3 — the in-tree fallbacks are unreachable.** `vllm/v1/attention/ops/rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py` contains `fp8_paged_mqa_logits_torch` and `fp8_mqa_logits_torch`, and both dispatchers (`rocm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits`, `rocm_fp8_mqa_logits`) already call them in their `else` branches when the AITER Triton module is unavailable. But reaching the dispatchers requires AITER enabled (gates 1–2), and with AITER enabled the module lookup always succeeds, so the AITER Triton kernels are always selected.

On RDNA3/3.5 those AITER Triton kernels cannot compile regardless (no fp8 WMMA), so whitelisting the arch in gate 2 just moves the failure into Triton:

```
triton.compiler.errors.CompilationError
  o = tl.dot(q, k.T)
      ^
Unsupported lhs dtype fp8e4nv
(aiter/ops/triton/attention/pa_mqa_logits.py, deepgemm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits_stage1)
```

i.e. every path on this hardware terminates in an error one step before working fallback code.

### Reproduction

1. 2× gfx1151, DeepSeek-V4-Flash, serve command in the environment section → gate 1 error.
2. Add `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1` → identical error (gate 2).
3. Whitelist gfx1151 in `is_aiter_found_and_supported()` → Triton `fp8e4nv` CompilationError in the AITER paged-MQA kernel (gate 3).

### Tested fix (cluster is serving with this)

**a) `vllm/_aiter_ops.py`** — accept gfx1151 as AITER-capable:

```diff
-        from vllm.platforms.rocm import on_mi3xx
-
-        return on_mi3xx()
+        from vllm.platforms.rocm import on_mi3xx, on_gfx1151
+
+        return on_mi3xx() or on_gfx1151()
```

**b) `vllm/v1/attention/ops/rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py`** — skip the AITER Triton module lookup on gfx1151 so the existing torch fallbacks run (same change in both dispatchers):

```diff
-    if rocm_aiter_ops.is_enabled():
+    from vllm.platforms.rocm import on_gfx1151
+
+    # gfx1151: Triton cannot compile tl.dot with fp8e4nv inputs; skip the
+    # AITER Triton kernels so the torch reference fallback below is used.
+    if rocm_aiter_ops.is_enabled() and not on_gfx1151():
         aiter_paged_mqa_logits_module = paged_mqa_logits_module()
```

```diff
+    from vllm.platforms.rocm import on_gfx1151
+
     aiter_mqa_logits_module = None
-    if rocm_aiter_ops.is_enabled():
+    if rocm_aiter_ops.is_enabled() and not on_gfx1151():
         aiter_mqa_logits_module = mqa_logits_module()
```

The prefill dispatcher (`rocm_fp8_mqa_logits`) needs the same gate: its AITER kernel performs the same fp8 `tl.dot` and fails identically on the first real prefill if only the paged path is patched.

A cleaner resolution than piling onto the arch whitelist is probably per-kernel capability gating: dispatchers select the AITER Triton kernel only on archs where it is known to compile (mi3xx / gfx942 / gfx950 — the gfx942 special case already exists in `rocm_fp8_mqa_logits`), else torch fallback — and gate 1's error message should not recommend an env var that gate 2 ignores. Happy to turn this into a PR if maintainers agree on the preferred shape.

Note: the sparse-attention Triton kernels in the same file are unaffected — they dequantize fp8→bf16 in-kernel before `tl.dot` and compile fine on gfx1151.

### Secondary finding: torch fallback vs FULL cudagraph capture

Once reachable, `fp8_paged_mqa_logits_torch` is not capture-safe (`.item()` / data-dependent host loops), but `@eager_break_during_capture` intentionally runs ops inline when `forward_context.cudagraph_runtime_mode == CUDAGraphMode.FULL` (`compilation/breakable_cudagraph.py`), so FULL capture crashes:

```
File ".../rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py", line 290, in fp8_paged_mqa_logits_torch
    seq_len = int(context_lens[i].item())
torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: operation not permitted when stream is capturing
(hipErrorStreamCaptureUnsupported)
```

If the fallbacks become officially reachable, the op should be treated as non-capturable when the torch path is active (or cudagraph disabled for it). We run with `--enforce-eager` (also required on this cluster: piecewise capture deadlocked in RCCL NET/Socket collectives; related to #32180).

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Bug]: MFU/MBU bills linear-attention layers of hybrid models as full attention; reported bandwidth exceeds the GPU's peak
body:
### Your current environment

RTX 4090 24 GB (spec 1,008 GB/s; memory clock 10,501 MHz per `nvidia-smi -q`), driver 590.48.01 (CUDA 13.1), Ubuntu 24.04, vLLM `0.30.1rc1.dev80+g26f49e336` (nightly cu130 wheel), torch 2.13.0+cu130, transformers 5.17.0. The rented machine is gone, so I do not have `collect_env.py` output; `vllm/v1/metrics/` is unchanged between `26f49e336` and current `main` (`8b84e150`, 2026-09-24).

### 🐛 Describe the bug

`AttentionMetrics` bills full attention (QKV/O weights, KV-cache reads, attention FLOPs) for every one of `num_hidden_layers`. Hybrid models with linear-attention layers only have full attention in a fraction of them: Qwen3.5 and Qwen3-Next use 3 Gated DeltaNet layers for every full-attention layer (`layer_types`, `full_attention_interval: 4`). #55624 handles sliding-window/full alternation but not linear-attention or Mamba layers, so the reported MBU for these models is not physically possible.

Config-only check (no GPU):

```python
from tests.v1.metrics.test_perf_metrics import create_mock_vllm_config
from vllm.transformers_utils.config import get_config
from vllm.v1.metrics.perf import ModelMetrics

mm = ModelMetrics(create_mock_vllm_config(get_config("Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B", trust_remote_code=False)))
print({m.component_type(): getattr(m, "num_hidden_layers", None) for m in mm.metrics})
# {'attn': 32, 'ffn': 32, 'unembed': None}; layer_types has 8 "full_attention" and 24 "linear_attention"
```

Measured with `vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B --enable-mfu-metrics` (`VLLM_LOG_STATS_INTERVAL=2`) and `vllm bench serve` (random prompts, 512 output tokens, `--ignore-eos`, 3 × batch requests per cell). The table only uses 2-second log intervals inside the benchmark's wall time that have no prefill in them (`Avg prompt throughput: 0.0`), so it is pure decode:

| batch × context | reported GB/s, median (run 1 / run 2) | intervals above 1,008 GB/s | same cells, layer count corrected (see below) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8 × 8k | 1,164 / 1,165 | 8/8, 8/8 | 602, 0/9 above |
| 8 × 16k | 1,538 / 1,536 | 10/10, 11/11 | 652, 0/11 above |
| 32 × 8k | 1,821 / 1,831 | 10/10, 10/10 | 645, 0/13 above |

- A device-to-device copy on the same card reaches 918 GB/s (read + write, 3 trials), so the reported numbers are not physically possible.
- Control: Qwen3-4B (dense, same size, same script, same machine) never exceeds the peak: 0 of 32 decode intervals, max 881 GB/s.
- Intervention: counting only the 8 full-attention layers (a small parser reading `layer_types` / `layers_block_type`) removes every over-peak interval on the same cells.

The corrected column is not the right answer either. Dropping the 24 linear-attention layers from attention without billing them as anything leaves out their weights (1,011 M parameters for Qwen3.5-4B, counted from the safetensors headers) and their recurrent state, so the estimate becomes about 0.75× of the bytes actually moved. A correct fix needs a linear-attention component: weights, the per-request recurrent and conv state read and written every step, and nothing that grows with context. Hand accounting of what the model actually reads shows the current code over-bills bytes per decode step by about 1.43× at 8 × 8k and about 2× at 32 × 8k, and under-bills slightly at 1 × 1k.

A smaller related gap: the Qwen3.5 / Qwen3-Next attention has an output gate (`attn_output_gate: true`; `q_proj` is `[8192, 2560]`, twice the query width), which `qkv_weight` / `qkv_proj` do not include.

Limits of this report: one GPU and one hybrid model measured; Qwen3-Next, Jamba, Falcon-H1 only checked at config level. `ncu` DRAM counters were not available in the container, so "bytes actually moved" comes from the parameter and state accounting above, not a hardware counter.

Not a duplicate as far as I can tell: no open or closed issue or PR covers MFU/MBU for linear-attention or Mamba layers (searched 2026-09-25). The two open PRs touching `perf.py` (#55474, #54228) do not touch layer counting.

I'd like to work on the fix (linear-attention component plus layer-type parsing, with tests) if that direction sounds right to the maintainers of this area.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to write the scripts, drive the measurements on my rented GPU and draft this report. I reviewed the logs and the results.

title: [Perf]: turboquant_k8v4 decode penalty scales with context length (-2.8% at 3k, -31% at 55k) on Ampere SM86, no speculative decoding
body:
### Summary

On a hybrid GDN + full-attention model, `--kv-cache-dtype turboquant_k8v4` costs almost nothing at short context but roughly a third of decode throughput at 55k prompt tokens, compared to `fp8_e4m3` with everything else identical. Speculative decoding is **off** in both arms, so this is separate from #53180 / #52475 / #53406 / #53410.

The KV-cache saving is real and large (+37% pool on the same GPUs), but on our hardware the throughput loss lands exactly on the long-context requests the bigger pool is meant to serve, which makes the feature unusable for us today.

### Environment

- vLLM **0.27.1**, stock (pip, no local patches)
- 2x RTX 3090 (**Ampere, SM 8.6**), TP=2, 250 W each
- Model: Qwen3.8-27B, hybrid GDN + full attention, own mixed W8/W4 GPTQ weight quant, `dtype=bfloat16`
  - 64 layers, `full_attention_interval=4` -> 16 full-attention layers (engine log: `TQ hybrid: full-attention layers [3, 7, 11, ..., 63]`)
  - `head_dim=256`, 24 query heads / 4 KV heads (**GQA group size 6**)

### Reproduction

Two servers, launched from the same script; the **only** difference in `non-default args` is `kv_cache_dtype`. Both without `speculative_config`.

```
vllm serve <model> \
  --dtype bfloat16 --tensor-parallel-size 2 --disable-custom-all-reduce \
  --max-model-len 156000 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.86 \
  --kv-cache-dtype turboquant_k8v4 \
  --enable-prefix-caching --prefix-match-unit 16 \
  --mamba-cache-mode align \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --max-num-seqs 4 \
  --long-prefill-token-threshold 2048 --enable-chunked-prefill
```

Arm C is the same line with `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`.

Load: single stream, no concurrency, warm (same prompt run twice back to back), 800 output tokens per run, server-side sampling override (`temperature=1.0, top_p=0.95, top_k=20, presence_penalty=1.0`). Two prompt sizes: **3,216** and **55,344** prompt tokens.

### Measurements

| | `fp8_e4m3` | `turboquant_k8v4` | delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| KV cache pool (engine log) | 357,622 tokens | 491,111 tokens | **+37.3%** |
| Max concurrency @156k | 2.29x | 3.15x | |
| Decode, 3,216 prompt tokens | 53.33 / 53.32 t/s | 51.83 / 51.82 t/s | **-2.8%** |
| Decode, 55,344 prompt tokens | 50.18 / 50.20 t/s | 34.58 / 34.58 t/s | **-31.1%** |

(Two runs per cell, both listed; run-to-run spread is <0.1 t/s.)

Engine log lines:

```
GPU KV cache size: 357,622 tokens | Maximum concurrency for 156,000 tokens per request: 2.29x   # fp8_e4m3
GPU KV cache size: 491,111 tokens | Maximum concurrency for 156,000 tokens per request: 3.15x   # turboquant_k8v4
```

Secondary observation (same runs, not isolated from prefix-cache state, so weaker evidence): TTFT on the warm 55k prompt was 1.05 s with TurboQuant vs 0.56 s with fp8, and 0.69 s vs 0.09 s on the warm 3k prompt.

Output quality with TurboQuant and no speculative decoding was clean: 0 degenerate responses across 8 probes plus a 42-item internal eval run.

### What we think is happening

The penalty is near-zero at 3k and ~31% at 55k, i.e. it tracks the number of quantized KV positions read back per decode step rather than a fixed per-step overhead. That is consistent with the dequant/rotation work sitting in the per-position read path of the Triton decode kernel, but we have not profiled it — this is an observation, not a diagnosis.

### Questions

1. Is a context-length-scaling decode penalty of this size expected for the current Triton decode kernels, or does it indicate a missed fast path for this geometry?
2. Our config (`k8v4`, GQA group size 6, `head_dim` 256) falls outside the dispatch gates of #53060 (K4V4-NC only) and #48235 (GQA group size 4). #40792 targets exactly `k8v4` GQA grouping and reports +16.5–27.2% on A100/H100 — would it be expected to change the *slope* here, or only the constant?
3. #40069 lists "CUDA/cutedsl kernels to replace the triton kernels" under Performance. Is that the tracking item for this, and is there a benchmark shape you would like measured on SM86? We can run more points on this hardware.

### Expected

Either the decode penalty stays roughly constant with context length, or the context-scaling behaviour is documented so the compression/throughput trade-off can be evaluated before deployment.

*This issue was researched and written by Ren, an AI agent operated by karls0r, with his review.*

title: [Bug][Perf][DSpark] #54674 stacked context WKV regresses TTFT ~3.3% on 2-node DGX Spark (GB10, TP=2), with no decode gain
body:
## Summary

[#54674](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54674) ("[Perf][DSpark] Stack DeepSeek V4 context WKV projections", merged 2026-09-17) is a **TTFT regression of ~3.2-3.3%** on 2-node DGX Spark (GB10 / SM121, TP=2) serving DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 NVFP4. It also costs ~1.5% of the KV pool. We measured no compensating decode or acceptance-rate gain.

Since the PR targets the context/prefill path, a TTFT regression is the opposite of its intended effect, so we are reporting it rather than just dropping the patch locally.

## Why the usual A/B is not enough here, and what we did instead

Throughput metrics on this platform have a large boot-to-boot spread, so a single A-vs-B comparison cannot resolve a few percent. We ran **A-B-A** (three full engine restarts) and used the two A runs to calibrate the noise floor:

| metric | A1 (without #54674) | B (with #54674) | A2 (without #54674) | A1↔A2 spread |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| greedy 32K decode tok/s | 65.62 | 64.57 | 60.92 | **7.2%** |
| temp0.6 8K decode tok/s (mean of 3) | 61.54 | 65.70 | 65.23 | **6.0%** |
| temp0.6 acceptance rate | 0.6539 | 0.7016 | 0.6961 | **6.5%** |
| **TTFT 8K (s)** | **2.502** | **2.589** | **2.512** | **0.4%** |
| **TTFT 32K (s)** | **10.191** | **10.551** | **10.221** | **0.3%** |

Decode throughput and DSpark acceptance rate swing 6-7% between two boots of the *same* build, so every apparent "gain" for B in those rows is inside the noise band. TTFT, by contrast, is stable to 0.3-0.4% across the two A runs — and B is consistently **+3.2%** (8K) and **+3.3%** (32K) relative to the A mean, which is roughly an order of magnitude outside that spread.

A 128K-prefill probe agrees in direction: 62.6 s with the patch vs 61.9 / 62.1 s without.

Secondary cost: GPU KV cache pool drops from **1,655,061** to **1,630,430** tokens (-1.5%), and reported max concurrency at 1M context from 1.58x to 1.55x.

## Hypothesis

With `--max-num-seqs 6` on a 2-node TP=2 GB10 pair, the stacked WKV projection does not have enough concurrent context work to amortize its extra setup, so the stacking overhead lands directly on TTFT. Configurations with larger batch or more GPUs may still benefit — we are not claiming the PR is wrong in general, only that it is a net loss in this shape.

## Reproduction

Serve command (2 nodes, one GB10 each, RoCE):

```
vllm serve nvidia/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-NVFP4 \
  --revision f1caa71142bd0be02f728c79f75042ac1e461579 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 --nnodes 2 --distributed-executor-backend mp \
  --trust-remote-code --max-num-seqs 6 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
  --max-model-len 1048576 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla --block-size 256 \
  --enable-chunked-prefill --quantization deepseek_v4_fp8 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.825 \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser deepseek_v4 \
  --compilation-config '{"mode":0,"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","disable_eagle_block_drop":true}' \
  --no-async-scheduling --enable-flashinfer-autotune
```

Measure TTFT at 8K and 32K prompt with 384 output tokens, greedy. **Restart the engine between arms and run A-B-A**; a single A/B will not separate a 3% TTFT effect from the decode noise if you look at throughput, and will look like a *win* if you look at `temp0.6` decode or acceptance rate.

## Environment

- 2x DGX Spark (GB10, SM121, 48 SMs, driver 580.173.02), TP=2 over RoCE, unified 128 GB/node
- vLLM nightly `2671fedf` + the merged `#54674` diff applied as a source overlay (byte-identical to the merged version apart from the `diff --git`/`index` headers)
- flashinfer 0.6.18.post1 with the #4802 SM120 sparse-MLA sources overlaid (+#5048, +#5097)
- DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 NVFP4, `fp8_ds_mla` KV, DSpark k=5
- Benchmarks run on an idle cluster with periodic synthetic load disabled

Happy to re-run with different `--max-num-seqs` or on a larger batch shape if that would help locate the crossover.

title: Speculative-decoding draft model (EAGLE/MTP head) compile cache key flips between two values with byte-identical startup args — shared `VllmConfig` mutated in-place during main-model full-compile startup (v0.27.1; deterministic on 0.29)
body:
## Summary

On vLLM 0.27.1 with speculative decoding (MTP head, k=1), the **draft model's** torch.compile cache identity deterministically flips between exactly two values across restarts with **byte-identical argv and environment**. The flip factor is not the command line — it is whether the **main model compiles (cold start) or loads from cache (warm start)** on that startup.

Forensics on `cache_key_factors.json` (which records the actual hash factors) show the draft's `config_hash` differs between the two generations while env/compiler factors are identical: the shared `VllmConfig` object is **mutated in-place during the main model's warmup/CUDA-graph-capture phase**, after the backbone compiles with a clean hash but before the eagle head compiles. On a 0.29 development build (commit `g38537331d`, the same build referenced in #58653) the same forensics show `eagle_head config_hash == backbone config_hash` in **9/9 compile-era startups** across two independent deployments — i.e. 0.29 appears immune.

## Environment

- vLLM **0.27.1** (stable release), single GPU, single rank
- Model: Qwen3.8-27B (W4A16 quantized), hybrid attention (linear/GDN + full), MTP module
- Speculative decoding: MTP k=1; CUDA graph `PIECEWISE`; fp8 KV cache
- 0.27.1 evidence from deployment A; 0.29 control (dev build `g38537331d`, 2026-09-19) from deployment A's current build and deployment B

## Symptom

- The draft model's AOT/compile cache directory alternates between two values (`40a960c…` ↔ `81aa37e7…`) across **17 same-signature restarts** observed during one incident window, all with identical startup args.
- Every flip costs a full draft recompile (~196 s) at the next startup whose expected generation doesn't match — the draft cache hit rate is determined by the *previous startup's shape*, not by config.

## Forensics: `cache_key_factors.json`

vLLM writes `torch_compile_cache/<short_hash>/rank_0_0/<backbone|eagle_head>/cache_key_factors.json` recording the real hash factors. Comparing the **eagle head** across the two generations:

| factor | generation 1 (main compiled) | generation 2 (main loaded) | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| env_hash (231 keys) | `2e9cfbbedb14f457` | same | SAME |
| compiler_hash | `8e33489fd9` | same | SAME |
| **config_hash** | **`06b5820a50`** | **`b398c1fc03`** | **DIFF — the flip factor** |
| code_hash | `2b706e49…` | `91b0ecb5…` | DIFF (dynamo compile-counter side effect) |

Key observation: in generation 2 (clean), the eagle head's `config_hash` **equals the backbone's** (`b398c1fc03`) — the draft derives from the main config without changing hash factors. In generation 1, eagle ≠ backbone for the same process, i.e. between the backbone's compile and the eagle's compile, **something changed the config that feeds `compute_hash()`**.

## Why "same cache dir, diverging jsons"

- `compilation/backends.py:1053` (0.27.1): `if not self.compilation_config.cache_dir:` — the **shared** `CompilationConfig.cache_dir` is set by the backbone's compile; the eagle head then **reuses the backbone's cache dir** instead of deriving its own from its (now-dirty) factors.
- But each `cache_key_factors.json`'s `config_hash` is recomputed fresh at `__call__` entry (`backends.py:1034`, no caching).
- Result: both roles land in one directory while their jsons record diverging config hashes — the forensic signature that led us here.

## Startup-shape bisection (timeline, UTC)

| startup | main model | warmup+capture window | eagle config_hash | draft AOT saved as |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-09-17 00:09–00:12 | full compile | **present, 67.6 s** | `06b5820a50` (dirty) | `81aa37e7` |
| 2026-09-17 00:37 | direct load | absent | `b398c1fc03` (clean) | `40a960c` |
| 2026-09-20 04:09 | full compile | present | dirty | `81aa37e7` |
| 2026-09-22 19:35 | direct load | absent | clean | `40a960c` |

The warmup+capture phase exists **only** on full-compile startups, and it runs **between** backbone compile and eagle compile — exactly where the mutation must occur. **Flip factor = whether the main model compiles on that startup.**

## Mechanism chain

1. Backbone `__call__` computes `config_hash` fresh (clean).
2. Main-model warmup + CUDA-graph capture runs (full-compile startups only) — **this phase mutates the shared `VllmConfig` in-place** (exact field not yet isolated).
3. Eagle head `__call__` recomputes `config_hash` from the now-mutated config → different value.
4. Draft AOT save dir (derived from `[env_hash, config_hash, code_hash, compiler_hash]`) flips; the torch_compile_cache dir does not (reuse) → diverging-jsons signature.

## Ruled out (all with file:line in 0.27.1)

- `traced_files` / `cache_dir` / `local_cache_dir`: in `CompilationConfig` ignored_factors (`compilation/config.py:792-800`)
- `num_gpu_blocks` / `num_gpu_blocks_override`: in `CacheConfig` ignored_factors
- `cudagraph_mode`: byte-identical CUDAGraphMode traces in both generations' draft AOT pickles (both `PIECEWISE`); the resolve-time downgrade warning fires **after** each draft compile in both startups
- `adjust_cudagraph_sizes_for_spec_decode`: write-back happens at `resolve()`, outside the window
- Engine-phase speculative-config mutation: `SpeculativeConfig.compute_hash` for MTP is constant `[False]`; `update_arch_*` all in `__post_init__` (construction time, identical both generations)
- `CudaGraphManager` internals (`cudagraph_utils.py:122`): own attributes, no config write points
- "0.29 caches the hash" hypothesis: 0.29's `backends.py` computes `config_hash` fresh, code isomorphic to 0.27.1 — immunity is behavioral, not a caching change

## Cross-version control (0.29 immune)

- Deployment B (0.29 dev build `g38537331d`): **9/9** compile-era startups have `eagle_head config_hash == backbone config_hash` (json forensics, same method).
- Deployment A's 0.29 build: two generations (2026-09-23, 2026-09-24 windows), likewise `backbone == draft config_hash`.
- ⇒ On 0.29 the in-window mutation either no longer happens or no longer feeds hash factors. **0.27.1 affected; 0.29 (dev) appears immune.**

> **Note — candidate explanations for the immunity (testable).** (a) 0.29's `compute_hash` factor set changed, so whatever mutates in the window no longer feeds any hash factor; (b) 0.29's warmup path no longer mutates `VllmConfig` in place; (c) both. One measured datum supports (a): the recorded `cache_key_factors` env-key set grew from **231 keys (0.27.1) to 238 (0.29)** across our two deployments — 26 added feature-flag knobs (new decoder kernels, data/context parallelism, XPU and CPU-offload switches, hardware-agnostic keys, etc.) and 19 removed legacy keys. Pinning the immunity to (a), (b), or (c) requires the field-diff instrumentation outlined below.

## Impact

- The draft compile cache is effectively **startup-history-dependent**: identical configs produce different cache identities depending on whether the main model compiles. Warm-start fleets see surprise recompiles (~196 s per flip; 17 same-signature restarts in one incident window here).
- More generally: **any in-place mutation of `VllmConfig` between the first and last compile of a single startup silently changes derived cache keys** — a reproducibility hazard for torch.compile caching beyond speculative decoding.

## Isolating the field (planned)

Static analysis is exhausted (12+ write points audited). The only leak-free method is instrumenting a real 0.27.1 engine: monkeypatch `VllmConfig.compute_hash` and dump every sub-config's `get_hash_factors()` at backbone vs eagle `__call__`, then field-diff. We plan to run this and will comment with the exact field(s).

> **Note.** Offline worker-derive attempts (calling `VllmConfig.compute_hash` from a separate probe process) produce a `config_hash` different from the in-engine value; all forensic claims in this issue therefore rely exclusively on the on-disk `cache_key_factors.json` snapshots as the source of record.

## Notes

- Authored anonymously by maintainers of two independent production deployments (same as #58653).
- Anonymized forensic snapshots (`cache_key_factors.json` diffs, four-point timeline) available on request.
- Reproduction was performed on 0.27.1 stable; the 0.29 control is a development build — verification on 0.29 stable is pending and will be posted as a comment.

### Describe the bug On Model Runner V1 with speculative decoding, a `thinking_token_budget` that forces a multi-token `reasoning_end_str` often emits the end sequence wrong: end tokens go missing with one of the model's own tokens in their place, and some reasoning sections never close. On main `9f07d023d07f`, 17 of 32 budget-forced ends were corrupted. The same arm on Model Runner V2 was 0 of 32. The cause is in `ThinkingBudgetStateHolder._update_think_state` (`vllm/v1/sample/thinking_budget_state.py`, added with #34668). While forcing, it advances through the end sequence on the step's draft tokens rather than on accepted tokens, and forces only one position per step. V2 forces every position of the verification window. The fix is in #52677 (`df93fe6c67`), because that PR forces the same end sequence through the same state machine. #### Reproduction One GB10 (sm_121), main `9f07d023d07f` (precompiled wheel `0.30.1rc1.dev20+g9f07d023d`), torch 2.13.0+cu130, driver 580.173.02, Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 with its MTP head. ``` VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0 vllm serve Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 \ --speculative-config '{"method":"qwen3_5_mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3,"max_model_len":262144}' \ --reasoning-parser qwen3 \ --reasoning-config '{"reasoning_end_str":"I have to give the solution based on the reasoning directly now."}' \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.6 --max-num-seqs 32 --max-model-len 262144 \ --enable-prefix-caching --mamba-cache-mode align \ --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --long-prefill-token-threshold 7840 ``` (plus YaRN `hf-overrides`, the `qwen3_coder` tool parser, and `enable_thinking: false` in the default chat template kwargs) Client: `/v1/chat/completions`, `temperature` 0.7, `reasoning_effort` "xhigh", `thinking_token_budget` 256, `max_tokens` 2048. Two prompts that make the model reason at length (write a fixed line 150 or 250 times in its reasoning, then answer "done" or "prime"), 16 requests each at concurrency 16. `reasoning_end_str` is 14 tokens. The budget fired on all 32. | end sequence | reasoning closed | final answer followed | requests | |---|---|---|---| | intact | yes | yes | 14 | | intact | yes | no, the answer re-entered the loop | 1 | | corrupted | yes | yes | 7 | | corrupted | yes | no, the answer re-entered the loop | 5 | | corrupted | no, reasoning ran to `max_tokens` | no | 5 | | **total** | 27 of 32 closed | 21 of 32 answered | 15 intact, **17 corrupted** | "Intact" means the reasoning ends with the phrase exactly once. What the corrupted ones look like: ``` ...I have the solution based on the reasoning directly now. ...I have to give final based on the analysis now. ...I have to give final based on this directly now. ...I need give the solution based on the reasoning directly now. ...I have considered the solution based on the reasoning directly now. ...I have already the solution based on the reasoning directly now. ``` Same host, model, flags, prompts, budget and client: | run | budget fired | intact | corrupted | closed | final answer | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | main `9f07d023d07f`, V1 | 32 | 15 | **17** | 27 | 21 | | main `9f07d023d07f`, V2 (`Using V2 Model Runner` in the log) | 32 | 32 | 0 | 32 | 25 | | #52677 `df93fe6c67`, V1 | 32 | 32 | 0 | 32 | 26 | Fisher two-sided p = 8.2e-7 for corrupted, main V1 against #52677. The #52677 row is that PR's tree on its own wheel (base `f944491db9`), so it differs from main in more than this fix; the V2 row is main itself. The requests without a final answer in the two clean rows closed intact and then repeated the prompt's line in the answer, which is the prompt doing its job. #### Mechanism (main `9f07d023d07f`) When the budget runs out, lines 422-445 force the first end token at one position (`force_index = [remaining_budget]`, `[0]` or `[spec_len]`). On later steps, lines 447-478 walk `spec_token_ids`: a draft equal to the next end token advances `end_count` and its position is left unforced, and only the first non-matching position (or the bonus slot) is forced. At a matching position the target decides on its own logits. If it samples something else, the matching draft is rejected and the target's token is committed, but `end_count` has already moved past it, so the next step forces from a later index: ``` accepted so far END[0..3] drafts [END[4], x, y] -> end_count 3 -> 5; force position 1 := END[5] position 0 not forced; the target samples T instead of END[4]; T is committed next step forcing resumes at END[6]; END[4] and END[5] are never emitted ``` That is the "I have to give final based on ..." shape above: " final" where " the solution" belongs. Two more cases come from the same walk: - when the drafts reach the last end token, `in_end` is cleared before any of them is verified; - when the transition forces the first end token part-way through the window and the draft there matches it, the positions after it go unforced. #### Unit tests `tests/v1/sample/test_thinking_forced_end_spec.py` (in #52677) drives the holder in the order V1 calls it (bonus pass in `Sampler`, target pass in `RejectionSampler`) with greedy verification, CPU only. Against the unfixed code, 5 of its 6 cases fail: | case | unfixed | fixed | |---|---|---| | thinking budget, target rejects a matching draft | FAIL, emits `[40, 41, 42, 77, 200]` for `[40, 41, 42, 43, 44, 200]` | pass | | thinking budget, forcing starts inside the draft window | FAIL, emits `[40, 77, 41, ...]` | pass | | loop break (#52677), target rejects a matching draft | FAIL, same shape | pass | | loop break (#52677), ramp release runs out | FAIL, same shape | pass | | loop break (#52677), drafts reach the last end token | FAIL, the sequence restarts at token 0 | pass | | control, no draft ever matches | pass | pass | #### The fix in #52677 - progress through the end sequence comes from the accepted output; - every position of the verification window, drafts and bonus, is forced to its own end token; - that includes forcing that starts part-way through a window: the budget transition, the loop-break fire, and the ramp release running out. One runtime file, `vllm/v1/sample/thinking_budget_state.py`, plus the test file. Through #52677's loop breaking, which forces the same end sequence when it detects a repeating reasoning loop (same settings except loop breaking on at 128/4/4 with a 256-token floor, `thinking_token_budget` 32768 so only the loop breaker fires, `max_tokens` 4096): | V1 unless stated | host | code | forced ends | corrupted | never closed | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | without the fix, two runs | spark-6 | `351f7b2c5e` | 51 | 23 | 8 | | an earlier version of the fix | spark-6 | on `351f7b2c5e` | 24 | 0 | 0 | | without the fix | spark-5 | `a650585283` | 25 | 6 | 2 | | with the fix | spark-5 | `df93fe6c67` | 25 | 0 | 0 | | with the fix, V2 | spark-5 | `df93fe6c67` | 24 | 0 | 0 | On spark-5 the two V1 rows are one commit apart: 6 of 25 against 0 of 25, Fisher p = 0.022. Matching fires by the scheduler log's request ID instead of by the phrase gives 7 of 26 against 0 of 25 (p = 0.0098), because one unfixed request lost the phrase's tail too. The unfixed rate differs between the hosts (23 of 51 against 6 of 25) at different commits with one or two runs each, so I would not read anything into that gap. #### Limits - V1 only. V2 is the default runner from v0.29.0 (#53183), and main on V2 was clean in the same arm. - One model, one phrase, one GPU type, n = 32 per row. A forced end is corrupted only when the model disagrees with a correct draft inside the end sequence, so the rate depends on the model, the phrase and the temperature. At temperature 0 on the same model, a separate run saw no corruption in 297 such positions. - In spec mode, when a batch has no drafts at all and V1 uses the plain sampler, the holder's row layout gives each request zero rows. That predates this and is not addressed here. #### Related, and why this is not a duplicate - #39697, with open fixes #43210 and #53572: the holder misses a natural reasoning end when `reasoning_end_str` carries a transition phrase, and forces the phrase into the answer. Same file, different defect. Neither diff touches the draft walk at lines 447-478. - #58231: `thinking_token_budget` with speculative decoding and `top_p < 1` emits token id 0 instead of the forced end. Same configuration, different cause (split-row top-p masking in `topk_topp_triton.py`). The corruption here is real vocabulary, never token 0. Searched open and closed issues and PRs for `_update_think_state`, `ThinkingBudgetStateHolder`, `reasoning_end_str`, and "thinking budget" with speculative decoding / MTP / spec decode.

title: [RFC]: Attention Backend Refactor
body:
*Follow-up to [RFC 42082](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/42082) (Standardize KV-cache Layouts). The KV layout standardization can proceed independently (we should complete this first to avoid excessive thrash; this RFC proposes a more aggressive refactor of the attention backend and KV cache manager interfaces.*

### Motivation.

Each attention backend today requires **four interlinked classes** (~750–1000 lines per backend):

| Class | Instances | Role |
|:------|:------------|:-----|
| `AttentionBackend` | (none) static | capability queries, factory methods |
| `AttentionMetadataBuilder` | 1 per group |  builds `AttentionMetadata` each step |
| `AttentionMetadata` | 1 per group per step | backend-specific batch state |
| `AttentionImpl` | 1 per layer | per-layer config; calls kernel in `forward()` |

Problems:
1. **High boilerplate.** Writing a new backend means implementing 4 classes . Adding fields `AttentionMetadata` requires  modifications to `AttentionMetadataBuilder`, `AttentionMetadata` and `AttentionImpl`
2. **Global manager registry.** A hardcoded `spec_manager_map` (679–686 in `single_type_kv_cache_manager.py`) decides which manager handles each spec type. Adding a new spec type or a model-specific eviction policy requires patching this shared map plus extending the `is_uniform_type()` isinstance chain.
3. **Coupled concerns in `KVCacheSpec`.** Block allocation policy (how many blocks, when to recycle) and tensor layout (head dims, dtype, page layout) are bundled in one object. Layers that share allocation behavior but differ in tensor layout can't share a block table without the `UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs` wrapper.



### Proposed Change.

Two independent changes:

#### 1. Single `AttentionBackend` Class

Collapse the four classes into one. The backend manages its own state — no separate metadata type.

```python
class AttentionBackend(ABC):

    def get_cache_config(self) -> tuple[
        type[SingleTypeKVCacheManager],
        ManagerConfig,
        KVCacheTensorSpec,
    ]:
        """Return the manager class, its config, and the tensor spec
        this backend needs. Layers with equal (cls, config) share a
        block table."""
        ...

    def bind_kv_caches(self, kv_caches: dict[str, Tensor],
                       block_table_map: dict[str, int]) -> None:
        """Bind allocated KV cache tensors and block-table mapping.
        block_table_map: layer_name → kv_cache_group_id."""
        ...

    def prep_forward(self, common_attn_metadata: CommonAttentionMetadata,
                     block_tables: dict[int, Tensor],
                     for_cudagraph_capture: bool = False) -> None:
        """Build backend-specific state once per step.
        block_tables: kv_cache_group_id → block table tensor.
        Replaces the MetadataBuilder + Metadata pair."""
        ...

    def forward(self, layer_config: LayerConfig,
                output: Tensor, query: Tensor, key: Tensor,
                value: Tensor, **kwargs) -> Tensor:
        """Execute attention for one layer. Per-layer differences
        (scale, sliding_window, num_heads) come via LayerConfig.
        KV cache is already bound via bind_kv_caches."""
        ...
```

##### Simplified Runner Loop

Today the runner iterates a nested 2D structure (KV cache groups × attention groups) and delegates to a complex `_build_attn_group_metadata` path that handles builder state management, metadata caching, and type translation:

```python
# Current (~1289–1401 in gpu_model_runner.py): nested loop
for kv_cache_group_id, kv_cache_group_spec in enumerate(...):
    # ... build CommonAttentionMetadata ...
    for attn_group in self.attn_groups[kv_cache_group_id]:
        builder = attn_group.get_metadata_builder()
        attn_metadata_i = builder.build(
            common_prefix_len=...,
            common_attn_metadata=common_attn_metadata,
        )
        for layer_name in attn_group.layer_names:
            attn_metadata[layer_name] = attn_metadata_i
```

With backends managing their own state via `prep_forward`, the runner flattens to a single loop over attention groups. Each group can span multiple KV cache groups — relevant block tables are passed as a dict:

```python
# Proposed: flat loop
for attn_group in self.attn_groups:
    attn_group.backend.prep_forward(
        common_metadata,
        block_tables={gid: block_tables[gid]
                      for gid in attn_group.kv_cache_group_ids},
    )
```

The metadata builder abstraction, metadata caching layer, and the `attn_metadata` dict that maps layer names to per-step metadata objects all go away.

##### Migration

A `LegacyBackendAdapter` wraps existing 4-class backends, forwarding `prep_forward` → builder + build and `forward` → impl.forward. Backends migrate incrementally.

#### 2. Backends Declare Manager + Tensor Spec

Today `KVCacheSpec` conflates block allocation and tensor layout. Because they're bundled, the `UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs` wrapper exists solely to group layers with matching allocation policy but different page sizes — and `is_uniform_type()` must be extended with a new isinstance branch for every new spec type.

Instead, **each backend returns the manager it needs**:

```python
(manager_cls, manager_config, kv_cache_tensor_spec)
```

- **`manager_cls` + `manager_config`** — block allocation policy. Layers with equal `(manager_cls, manager_config)` share a block table. This replaces `spec_manager_map`, `UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs`, and `is_uniform_type()`.
- **`kv_cache_tensor_spec`** — physical tensor layout (the `KVCacheTensorSpec` from [RFC 42082](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/42082)). Stays on the worker, never crosses to the scheduler.

##### Manager Configs

Each manager defines a frozen `Config` dataclass carrying only allocation-policy fields. `block_size` and `num_blocks` are constructor parameters (global values determined by the worker), not part of the config.

```python
class FullAttentionManager(SingleTypeKVCacheManager):
    @dataclass(frozen=True)
    class Config:
        pass

class SlidingWindowManager(SingleTypeKVCacheManager):
    @dataclass(frozen=True)
    class Config:
        sliding_window: int

class MambaManager(SingleTypeKVCacheManager):
    @dataclass(frozen=True)
    class Config:
        mamba_cache_mode: str
        num_speculative_blocks: int
```

Models can supply custom managers (e.g. a model-specific eviction policy) by returning a different `manager_cls` from `get_cache_config()` — no patching of shared registries.

##### Worker-Driven Allocation

The worker has the model, the backends, and the GPU. It owns grouping and tensor allocation — the engine only needs allocation policy and a block budget:

```
Worker:           collect (manager_cls, manager_config, tensor_spec) per backend
Worker:           group by (manager_cls, manager_config) equality
Worker:           compute block_size, kernel_block_size, num_blocks
Worker → Engine:  SchedulerKVCacheConfig { num_blocks, block_size, groups }
Engine:           min(num_blocks) across workers → broadcast agreed value
Worker:           allocate tensors locally with agreed num_blocks
```

The scheduler never sees `KVCacheTensorSpec`. Tensor layout plans no longer cross the process boundary.

### What Disappears

| Today | After |
|:------|:------|
| `spec_manager_map` (global dict) | Gone — `manager_cls` returned by backend |
| `UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs` + `is_uniform_type()` isinstance chain | Gone — `(cls, config)` equality |
| `KVCacheTensor` layout plan crossing to engine | Gone — worker allocates locally |
| 4-class backend structure (Backend + Builder + Metadata + Impl) | Gone — single `AttentionBackend` |
| `get_kv_cache_shape()` / `get_kv_cache_stride_order()` on backend | Gone — lives on `KVCacheTensorSpec` ([RFC 42082](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/42082)) |
| Per-layer `AttentionImpl` instances | Gone — Layer specifics passed to `forward()` |

### Trade-offs

- **Model definitions must manage backend sharing.** Today the runner creates one `AttentionImpl` per layer automatically. With the unified backend, the model is responsible for ensuring layers that should share a backend actually reference the same instance. This is more explicit but slightly more work for model authors.
- **`LegacyBackendAdapter` is needed during migration.** All existing backends continue working behind the adapter, but the adapter adds one indirection layer until each backend is ported natively.



### Feedback Period.

_No response_

### CC List.

@MatthewBonanni @WoosukKwon @heheda12345 

### Worktracking

TODO: start work following https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/42082
TODO: develop follow-up RFC for plugins @MatthewBonanni

title: [Bug] MiMoV2 load_weights: fused qkv_proj path uses naive chunk(tp,dim=0)[rank], misplaces Q values into K/V slots
body:
## Summary

`vllm/model_executor/models/mimo_v2.py:load_weights` has a code path for fused-`qkv_proj` checkpoints (MiMo-V2 Pro variants) that does

```python
if "qkv_proj" in name:
    if name in params_dict:
        param = params_dict[name]
        loaded_weight = loaded_weight.chunk(tp_size, dim=0)[tp_rank]
        default_weight_loader(param, loaded_weight)
    continue
```

For a checkpoint where the fused tensor is laid out `[Q | K | V]` along dim 0 — which is the case for at least `festr2/MiMo-V2.5-Pro-NVFP4-MXFP8-attn-TP8` — a naive `chunk(tp_size, dim=0)[tp_rank]` gives 7 of 8 ranks (at TP=8) rows that fall entirely inside the Q region. Those ranks' `QKVParallelLinear` parameter slots for K and V end up filled with Q values; only the last rank gets any real K/V data. Attention is therefore severely broken on 7 of 8 ranks.

The proper loader (`QKVParallelLinear.weight_loader` with `shard_id="q"/"k"/"v"`) handles the TP split per-section correctly. It's already used by the `stacked_params_mapping` path for checkpoints that store Q/K/V as separate tensors; the fused path just doesn't reach it.

## Repro

Model: `festr2/MiMo-V2.5-Pro-NVFP4-MXFP8-attn-TP8` (the only Pro-format quant I'm aware of that hits the fused branch; the Flash variant stores split q_proj/k_proj/v_proj and goes through `stacked_params_mapping`, which is correct).

Cluster: 8-node DGX Spark (GB10, sm_121), TP=8, Ray distributed executor. With other patches in place (MXFP8 dispatch wired into `modelopt_mixed`, `weight_scale_inv` -> `weight_scale` rename for the modelopt MXFP8 scale parameter), the model reaches Application startup and serves requests, but inference returns degenerate token loops (`*\0` / `Müslü` / `the` style — varies with prompt but never coherent).

## Empirical evidence the layout is `Q→K→V` (not per-rank pre-sharded)

For layer 0 `model.layers.0.self_attn.qkv_proj.weight_scale_inv` (shape `[27136, 192]`, uint8 E8M0):

| Region (dim-0 slice) | Rows | Mean byte | Interpretation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Q section `[0:24576]` | 24576 | **114.55** | 24576 = 128 Q heads × 192 head_dim |
| K section `[24576:26112]` | 1536 | **115.99** | 1536 = 8 KV heads × 192 head_dim |
| V section `[26112:27136]` | 1024 | **113.27** | 1024 = 8 KV heads × 128 v_head_dim |

The three sections have distinguishable scale-byte distributions (note V is systematically smaller-magnitude, consistent with `attention_value_scale=0.612` applied to V before attention). If the tensor were per-rank pre-sharded (8 chunks of `[Q|K|V]` concatenated), every chunk would have the same internal structure and the per-rank means would be identical; instead they're flat ~114 for the first 7 chunks (all-Q) and a weighted mix for chunk 7 (which spans the Q/K/V boundaries).

## Fix

Split the fused tensor by `(q_size, k_size, v_size)` using config dims (distinguishing full vs. SWA layers via `hybrid_layer_pattern`), then call the existing `QKVParallelLinear.weight_loader` three times with `shard_id` `"q"`, `"k"`, `"v"`. Each call lets the proper loader take this rank's TP-slice of that section, identical to the existing stacked path.

Proposed patch against `vllm/model_executor/models/mimo_v2.py` (replacing the `if "qkv_proj" in name:` block):

```python
if "qkv_proj" in name:
    if name in params_dict:
        param = params_dict[name]
        try:
            _li = int(name.split(".layers.")[1].split(".")[0])
        except (IndexError, ValueError):
            _li = -1
        _is_swa = (
            _li >= 0
            and hasattr(self.config, "hybrid_layer_pattern")
            and self.config.hybrid_layer_pattern[_li] == 1
        )
        if _is_swa:
            _nh = self.config.swa_num_attention_heads
            _nkv = self.config.swa_num_key_value_heads
            _hd = self.config.swa_head_dim
            _vhd = getattr(self.config, "swa_v_head_dim", _hd)
        else:
            _nh = self.config.num_attention_heads
            _nkv = self.config.num_key_value_heads
            _hd = self.config.head_dim
            _vhd = getattr(self.config, "v_head_dim", _hd)
        _qs = _nh * _hd
        _ks = _nkv * _hd
        _vs = _nkv * _vhd
        if loaded_weight.shape[0] == _qs + _ks + _vs:
            _q = loaded_weight[:_qs]
            _k = loaded_weight[_qs : _qs + _ks]
            _v = loaded_weight[_qs + _ks : _qs + _ks + _vs]
            _wl = getattr(param, "weight_loader", default_weight_loader)
            _wl(param, _q, "q")
            _wl(param, _k, "k")
            _wl(param, _v, "v")
            loaded_params.add(name)
        else:
            # Unexpected shape — keep old behavior.
            loaded_weight = loaded_weight.chunk(tp_size, dim=0)[tp_rank]
            default_weight_loader(param, loaded_weight)
    continue
```

I have this running on a TP=8 cluster; with the patch, the same model produces coherent output for chat and completion prompts (`12 × 7` → `84`, `def fibonacci(n):` → proper Python recursion, etc.). Without the patch, the same configuration produces the degenerate token loops described above.

The patch handles both full and SWA layers (MiMo-V2 has full attention layers at positions where `hybrid_layer_pattern[layer] == 0` and SWA layers elsewhere). It applies to both the FP8 weight tensor and the uint8 E8M0 scale tensor (`weight_scale_inv`) because both share the `qkv_proj` name prefix.

## Why this also affects users who don't see the symptom

The Flash-format MiMo-V2 checkpoints (separate `q_proj`/`k_proj`/`v_proj`) go through the `stacked_params_mapping` path before hitting this branch, so they're fine. Only fused-`qkv_proj` Pro checkpoints reach the buggy path. To my knowledge today that's `festr2/MiMo-V2.5-Pro-NVFP4-MXFP8-attn-TP8` and the BF16 source `XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.5-Pro` (if anyone tries to serve it directly).

## Related

- vllm#41797 (DiffKV Triton attention for MiMo) — gets the model past the attention-backend selection blocker; the load-path bug is independent.
- NVIDIA/cutlass#3096, flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#2776 — the wider sm_121/NVFP4 conversation. For this specific checkpoint the garbage signature `あるい/Müslü` was *not* a CUTLASS Sm120 ArchTag symptom; the same garbage class shows up across MXFP8 attention kernels (Marlin / Emulation / FlashInferCutlass) and NVFP4 MoE backends (Marlin / CUTLASS / Emulation) — only the load-side fix above clears it.

Happy to open a PR with the patch + a small test. Wanted to file the diagnosis first so the analysis isn't buried.

Working repo with patches + recipe: https://github.com/idonati/spark-vllm-docker-festr2

title: [Hybrid SSM] Investigate accuracy divergence between `mamba_chunk_scan` and `selective_state_update` kernels
body:
## Context

PR #43186 lowered the gsm8k accuracy threshold for `ibm-granite/granite-4.0-h-tiny` under NIXL PD disagg after #42430 rerouted the D-side 1-token recompute from `mamba_chunk_scan_combined_varlen` to `selective_state_update` (SSU).

The two kernels produce different bf16 outputs due (supposedly) different reduction orders:
- `mamba_chunk_scan_combined_varlen` goes through bf16 matmul with intermediate bf16 casts (`tl.dot`)
- `selective_state_update` keeps the SSM step in fp32 throughout

As noted in [this comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43186#issuecomment-2893988543), this seems like a large accuracy drop for something meant to be algebraically equivalent.

## Goal

Investigate the kernel-level numerical divergence **in isolation** to:
1. **Quantify the magnitude**: Run both kernels on identical inputs for a single prompt (prefill + decode) and measure the output divergence (max abs diff, relative error distribution).
2. **Determine hardware dependence**: Test on at least **Ampere (A100)** and **Hopper (H100)** to see if the divergence magnitude or direction is architecture-dependent.
3. **Recommend a fix or acceptable tolerance**: Based on findings, either align the kernels' numeric behavior or document the expected tolerance.

## Reproduction Plan

- Isolate the two kernels (`mamba_chunk_scan_combined_varlen` and `selective_state_update`) with a single-prompt workload (1 prefill + N decode steps).
- Compare outputs element-wise against each other and against an fp64 reference.
- Run on Ampere (A100) and Hopper (H100) hardware.

## References

- PR that lowered threshold: #43186
- PR that rerouted to SSU: #42430

title: [Bug]: test_mla_rope_kvcache_cat_fusion fails with FlashAttnMLA + fp8 KV cache (NotImplementedError)
body:
### Your current environment

- vllm `0.23.0` (PyPI release) and `vllm-project/vllm@main` (also reproduced on a downstream fork at the same upstream sha)
- transformers: verified on both `4.57.1` and `5.12.1` (latest stable, released 2026-06-15) — same failure
- 1 × NVIDIA H20, CUDA 13.0, torch `2.11.0+cu130`

### 🐛 Describe the bug

`tests/compile/passes/test_mla_rope_kvcache_cat_fusion.py::test_mla_rope_kvcache_cat_fusion` parametrizes over `kv_cache_dtype=["auto", "fp8"]` × `MLA_BACKENDS = [TRITON_MLA, FLASH_ATTN_MLA, ROCM_AITER_MLA]`. On Hopper (where `flash_attn_supports_mla()` is True) two combinations are collected and both fail at backend construction:

```
test_mla_rope_kvcache_cat_fusion[fp8-dtype0-True-16-512-1536-128-64-128-16-True-AttentionBackendEnum.FLASH_ATTN_MLA]
test_mla_rope_kvcache_cat_fusion[fp8-dtype0-False-16-512-1536-128-64-128-16-True-AttentionBackendEnum.FLASH_ATTN_MLA]
```

Stack:
```
E   NotImplementedError: FlashAttnMLA V1 with FP8 KV cache not yet supported
```

raised by `vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/flashattn_mla.py` when constructing the backend.

### Reproducer

```bash
pytest -v tests/compile/passes/test_mla_rope_kvcache_cat_fusion.py \
       -k "FLASH_ATTN_MLA and fp8"
```

Expected: 2 collected, both either pass or be cleanly skipped.
Actual: 2 failed (after pytest-rerunfailures retries them).

### Where it came from

`tests/compile/passes/test_mla_rope_kvcache_cat_fusion.py` was added in #40392 (merged 2026-05-11) and has not been touched since (only one commit on the file). The parametrize matrix unconditionally crosses `kv_cache_dtype=["auto", "fp8"]` with all `MLA_BACKENDS`. There is no `skipif` for the `(FLASH_ATTN_MLA, fp8)` cell, even though `FlashAttnMLA` explicitly raises `NotImplementedError` for FP8 KV cache.

### Suggested options (no preference, just listing)

1. Implement FP8 KV cache support in `FlashAttnMLA` so the parametrize matrix can stand.
2. Add a `pytest.skip(...)` runtime check in `test_mla_rope_kvcache_cat_fusion` for `(attn_backend == FLASH_ATTN_MLA and kv_cache_dtype == "fp8")`, mirroring the `flashattn_mla.py` capability gate.
3. Filter `MLA_BACKENDS` to drop `FLASH_ATTN_MLA` when `kv_cache_dtype == "fp8"` at test collection time.

Filing this only as a report — happy to put up a PR for any of the three if a maintainer indicates the preferred direction.

title: [Bug]: No clamp-capable batched NVFP4 fused-MoE backend → DeepEP / wide-EP unusable for MiniMax-M3 NVFP4
body:
### Environment

vLLM mainline with the NVFP4 MiniMax-M3 MoE path (the standard `vllm/vllm-openai:minimax-m3`
build + the NVFP4 MoE support from PR #46380), on Blackwell sm_100, NVLink-only (no InfiniBand),
with `deep_ep` and `nvshmem` available.

### What's wrong

NVFP4 MiniMax-M3 serves fine with normal expert parallelism. But the moment you turn on
**DeepEP** for wide-EP on the decode workers (e.g. `data-parallel-size: 16` +
`all2all-backend: deepep_low_latency`), it dies at startup:

```
NotImplementedError: No NvFp4 MoE backend supports the deployment configuration.
  (vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/oracle/nvfp4.py, select_nvfp4_moe_backend)
```

DeepEP itself comes up fine first — you can see `Using DeepEPLLAll2AllManager` and the EP rank
map being built — so this isn't a DeepEP or NVSHMEM problem. It's that none of the NVFP4 MoE
kernels can handle DeepEP's batched layout **and** MiniMax-M3's SwiGLU clamp at the same time.

### Why it happens

MiniMax-M3's experts use SwiGLU-OAI with a clamp (`swiglu_limit`). Two requirements collide:

- **The clamp** is only implemented by one NVFP4 backend, `FLASHINFER_TRTLLM`. When
  `swiglu_limit` is set, the backend picker (`NVFP4_BACKENDS_WITH_CLAMP`) narrows the choices
  down to TRTLLM only.
- **DeepEP** needs the *batched* activation format, and the only NVFP4 backend that provides it,
  `FLASHINFER_CUTEDSL_BATCHED`, does SILU only — no SwiGLU, no clamp.

So "I need the clamp" forces TRTLLM (which is standard-layout only), and "I need DeepEP" forces
the batched kernel (which has no clamp). No single backend does both:

| backend | applies SwiGLU clamp? | supports batched (DeepEP) layout? | activations |
|---|---|---|---|
| `FLASHINFER_TRTLLM` | ✅ (the only one) | ❌ standard only | SILU, RELU2, GELU(_TANH), SWIGLUOAI, SWIGLUOAI_UNINTERLEAVE |
| `FLASHINFER_CUTEDSL_BATCHED` | ❌ | ✅ (the only one) | SILU only |
| `FLASHINFER_CUTLASS` | ❌ | ❌ | SILU, GELU_TANH, RELU2, SWIGLUOAI |

Forcing the batched backend by hand doesn't get around it either — you just hit a guard:
`ValueError: Model sets swiglu_limit=..., but the requested moe_backend does not apply the SwiGLU clamp.`

### A separate snag on NVLink-only systems

If you reach for `deepep_high_throughput` instead, it fails even earlier, while DeepEP is
setting up its buffers:

```
deep_ep/buffer.py ... RuntimeError: CUDA error 'invalid resource handle'
```

High-throughput mode expects InfiniBand RDMA between nodes. On NVLink-only multi-node systems
there's no IB, so it can't start. `deepep_low_latency` + `VLLM_DEEPEP_LOW_LATENCY_USE_MNNVL=1`
is the right transport there, and it *does* start — it just then runs into the backend gap above.

### How to tell it's activation-specific, not a clamp bug

A SiLU-activated NVFP4 MoE (`hidden_act="silu"` + clamp) works fine, because SILU is supported by
both TRTLLM (clamp, standard layout) and CUTEDSL_BATCHED. The gap is specifically the
**SwiGLU-OAI + clamp** combination on a **batched** NVFP4 kernel.

### What would fix it

Teach a *batched* NVFP4 MoE backend to do SwiGLU-OAI (uninterleaved) with the clamp, and add it
to `NVFP4_BACKENDS_WITH_CLAMP`. Two plausible routes:

1. Add a **masked**-layout version of the cute-DSL swiglu-fusion kernel that already exists for
   the contiguous layout (`flashinfer/.../blockscaled_contiguous_gather_grouped_gemm_swiglu_fusion`).
   The DeepEP/batched path uses the masked grouped GEMM, which currently has no swiglu fusion.
2. Or add a `swigluoai_clamp_scaled_nvfp4_experts_quantize` op (like the existing SILU-only
   `silu_and_mul_scaled_nvfp4_experts_quantize`) and wire it into `FLASHINFER_CUTEDSL_BATCHED`.

This is basically the batched counterpart of #45624, which added the same activation + clamp to
the standard-layout TRTLLM backend. Until something like it lands, NVFP4 MiniMax-M3 is limited to
standard EP and can't use DeepEP wide-EP.

title: [Bug]: /v1/realtime audio sessions can retain KV cache indefinitely when clients stay connected without final=True
body:
### Your current environment

## Environment

- vLLM V1
- `/v1/realtime`
- Realtime audio transcription, e.g. Voxtral realtime models

### 🐛 Describe the bug

## Summary

In the `/v1/realtime` audio WebSocket API, a client can keep a realtime session alive indefinitely by leaving the WebSocket connection open and never sending `input_audio_buffer.commit` with `final: true`.

For V1 realtime streaming requests, normal non-final commits keep the request resumable and extend the session context. KV blocks are only released when the request is actually finalized, aborted, or the WebSocket connection is closed. If the client remains connected but stops sending audio/final, the server has no application-layer idle timeout to force cleanup.

## Impact

This can cause KV cache usage to grow or remain pinned for stale realtime sessions. In production, stale clients can eventually push KV cache usage to 100%, requiring manual intervention such as closing client connections or restarting pods.

## Current Behavior

A realtime audio session is cleaned up when:

- The client sends `input_audio_buffer.commit` with `final: true`
- The WebSocket disconnects
- The server detects the connection is gone and cleanup runs

However, if the WebSocket stays open and the client stops sending valid audio or never sends `final: true`, the realtime session can continue occupying engine-side resources.

Repeated non-final commits also do not represent actual new audio input, but they can keep the application-level session alive.

## Expected Behavior

Realtime audio WebSocket sessions should have a server-side idle policy. If no valid audio input is received for a configurable timeout, the server should gracefully finalize or close the session so the underlying engine request can unwind and release KV cache.

## Proposed Fix

Add an application-layer idle watchdog to `RealtimeConnection`:

- Default timeout: 30 seconds
- Configurable via an environment variable
- Reset the watchdog on valid `input_audio_buffer.append`
- Reset on non-final `commit` only when it actually starts generation
- Do not let repeated no-op commits keep the session alive
- On timeout, enqueue the final audio sentinel to gracefully finish the streaming request
- If graceful finalization does not complete within a short grace period, cancel the generation task and close the WebSocket

This gives operators a practical safety valve for stale realtime clients while preserving explicit `final=True` behavior for well-behaved clients.

title: [Bug] TPU: State leak in FP8 MoE shared_experts after AOT compilation fails with prefix caching
body:
### Your current environment

1. Environment: TPU v6e-8
2. Image: `vllm/vllm-tpu:nightly-20260626-c539adc-cc79815`


### 🐛 Describe the bug

### Description
When running an FP8 MoE model (`Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8`) on TPU v6e with `--enable-prefix-caching` enabled, the engine crashes during the warmup phase with an `AssertionError` in `shared_experts.py`. 

The root cause appears to be a state leak in the FP8 `shared_experts` module triggered by a failed AOT compilation attempt. 

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Environment: TPU v6e-8
2. Image: `vllm/vllm-tpu:nightly-20260626-c539adc-cc79815`
3. Command:
```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --data-parallel-size 1 \
  --max-model-len 131072 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
  --max-num-seqs 64 \
  --enable-prefix-caching \
  --trust-remote-code
```  

### Relevant Log Output
```(EngineCore pid=602) INFO 06-26 17:58:38 [compilation_manager.py:133] Precompile worker0 backbone --> {'num_tokens': 2048, 'num_reqs': 64}
(EngineCore pid=602) INFO 06-26 17:58:39 [compilation_manager.py:156] AOT lower skipped for worker0 backbone (ValueError('Invalid shape for `swap`... ')); will compile in warmup.
...
(EngineCore pid=602) ERROR 06-26 17:58:42 [core.py:1231]   File "/workspace/vllm/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/runner/shared_experts.py", line 165, in forward
(EngineCore pid=602) ERROR 06-26 17:58:42 [core.py:1231]     assert self._output[self._output_idx] is None
(EngineCore pid=602) ERROR 06-26 17:58:42 [core.py:1231] AssertionError
``` 

### Root Cause Analysis
1.) The engine attempts AOT compilation for various input shapes. It succeeds up to num_tokens=1024.
2.) When attempting to compile num_tokens=2048, AOT lowering fails due to a shape mismatch in the prefix caching swap logic:
```AOT lower skipped for worker0 backbone (ValueError('Invalid shape for swap. Ref shape: (2, 0, 2048). Expected shape: (0, 32). Value shape: (1, 32)... ')); will compile in warmup.```

3.) The State Leak: The FP8 shared_experts module does not clear its internal state after this aborted AOT pass.

4.) When the engine immediately moves to the warmup phase and attempts to trace the model, it hits the uncleared state and crashes here:
assert self._output[self._output_idx] is None -> AssertionError

### Additional Context
1.) This bug is a regression. The identical configuration runs successfully on an older image (vllm/vllm-tpu:nightly-20260612-c0c56aa-8a91228).

2.) The crash requires the combination of FP8 MoE (requantizing to float8_e4m3fn), AOT compilation, and --enable-prefix-caching.

title: [Bug][Metrics] `get_metrics_snapshot()` raises on unknown metric types, crashing LLM.get_metrics() and the ORCA header path
body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

`vllm/v1/metrics/reader.py::get_metrics_snapshot()` dispatches over
`metric.type` for every `vllm:`-prefixed entry in
`prometheus_client.REGISTRY`, but its dispatch is closed over
`{gauge, counter, histogram}`. The trailing `else` branch raises:

```python
else:
    raise AssertionError(f"Unknown metric type {metric.type}")
```

(`vllm/v1/metrics/reader.py:141` on current `main`.)

### Impact

`prometheus_client` ships `Summary`, `Info`, `Stateset`, and `untyped`
as first-class metric types, and OTel's `gen_ai.server.request.duration`
semantic convention is conventionally exported as `Summary`. The day
anyone adds a `Summary`-typed metric (or any custom collector that
returns `metric.type == \"untyped\"`) prefixed `vllm:`, two live code
paths crash:

1. **`vllm/v1/engine/llm_engine.py:380` → public `LLM.get_metrics()`**
   offline library API. Every offline caller reading in-memory metrics
   would crash.
2. **`vllm/entrypoints/serve/utils/orca_metrics.py:90` → `metrics_header()`**
   on `/v1/chat/completions` requests that opt into the
   `endpoint-load-metrics` ORCA header. Every such requests returns
   HTTP 500.

### Root cause

The available prometheus_client family of metric types is wider than
the three the reader handles, and the trailing branch fails loudly
instead of degrading gracefully.

### Suggested fix

Replace the `raise AssertionError(...)` with a graceful
`logger.debug(\"Skipping unknown metric type %s for metric %s\", ...)`
+ `continue`, matching the existing unknown-type handling pattern
already used elsewhere in the codebase (e.g.
`vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/offloading/metrics.py:189`,
`:216`, `:451`).

### Relationship to existing work

- [PR #35649](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/35649)
  \"Replace bare AssertionError with specific exception types\" touches
  the same line and proposes `raise ValueError(...)`. That keeps the
  production hazard: the reader still crashes both live consumers; it
  just does so with a different exception class. The behaviour this
  issue proposes (skip, not raise) is materially different: it
  prioritises availability for the library/header consumers, which were
  never in a position to read a metric type they have no dataclass for
  anyway.

### Environment

Found while auditing the V1 metrics subsystem on `main` at
`867fd5e8ed6b0bfcf84b24f82658c9fb698a6d35` (2026-06-27). The bug is
not environment-specific: it reproduces whenever any future
`vllm:`-prefixed metric uses a type outside `{gauge, counter, histogram}`.

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] I searched for relevant existing issues (no existing report
  found for the crash; #35649 is a related refactor with a materially
  different behaviour proposal).

---
*The fix and analysis above were investigated with AI assistance
(Claude); the underlying source locations and reasoning were reviewed
by me before filing.*

title: [Bug][ROCm]: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 cannot load on ROCm, the AMD Qwen4ExpNGramEmbedding has no FP8 weight_scale
body:
### Your current environment

- vLLM v0.30.0, image `docker.io/vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:v0.30.0` (amd64 `sha256:2e7da1ad1c66836802072588adea75f9f4991da5f9545b4318e91d422c22ce6a`) with fastokens 0.3.1 added, nothing else changed
- 8x AMD Instinct MI325X (gfx942), ROCm driver 6.19.14
- Kubernetes, TP 4 on four of the eight cards
- The same failure on v0.29.0


### 🐛 Describe the bug

`Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8` at revision `236dfdf285828023ca3bcd3f37366c58a3469b13` fails in weight loading on ROCm. Every worker dies with the same error:

```
ValueError: There is no module or parameter named 'ngram_embedding.weight_scale' in Qwen4ExpNGramEmbedding. The available parameters belonging to ngram_embedding (PLEVocabParallelEmbedding) are: {'ngram_embedding.weight'}
```

Command, run inside the image:

```
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 \
  --revision 236dfdf285828023ca3bcd3f37366c58a3469b13 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --max-model-len 262144 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85
```

The checkpoint is `quant_method: fp8` with `weight_block_size: [128, 128]` and dynamic activations. Its n-gram embedding table is F8_E4M3 with one BF16 global scale stored as `ngram_embedding.weight_scale`.

**Why it still fails after #54722 and #54882.** Both PRs are in v0.30.0, and both fix the FP8 PLE scale in the NVIDIA model path only (`vllm/models/qwen4_exp/nvidia/`). The ROCm build takes `vllm/models/qwen4_exp/amd/ple_layer.py`, which defines its own `Qwen4ExpNGramEmbedding` with no FP8 method and no `weight_scale` parameter. The scale tensor has nowhere to land on AMD. This is still true on main after #57497. #54765 is the NVIDIA report of the same error.

**What works.** `--enable-expert-parallel` gets the checkpoint past the block-quant check that stops plain TP 4 and TP 8 (expert width 640 against a 128 block gives 160 or 80 per rank). With EP the workers reach weight loading and fail only on the scale above. The bf16 checkpoint `Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next` serves on the same box and image.

**Ask.** Port the FP8 PLE weight-scale handling into the AMD `Qwen4ExpNGramEmbedding`, or share one embedding method between the two paths. Until then the FP8 checkpoint cannot be served on ROCm at any TP, on MI325X or MI355X.

I can test a fix on MI325X.

title: [Bug]: MTP fails to load dense BF16 MTP head on compressed-tensors pack-quantized checkpoints (no module or parameter named 'fc.weight')
body:
## Bug Description

`--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp",...}'` crashes at weight-load time when the target checkpoint is **compressed-tensors pack-quantized** and ships its MTP head as **dense BF16** in a separate shard. The MTP predictor's Linear layers are built from the *target's* quant config, so the loader expects packed parameter names (`weight_packed`) while the checkpoint provides dense `mtp.*.weight` tensors.

## Environment

- vLLM v0.30.0, official docker image `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.30.0` (stock, no patches)
- Model: [`ukisai/Swift-1.5-Qwen3.8-27b-W4A16-AWQ`](https://huggingface.co/ukisai/Swift-1.5-Qwen3.8-27b-W4A16-AWQ) (dense 27B, `Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration`, hybrid GDN + full attention, vision preserved)
- Flags: `vllm serve ukisai/Swift-1.5-Qwen3.8-27b-W4A16-AWQ --tensor-parallel-size 2 --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'` (+ kv fp8; the crash is at load, the rest is irrelevant)

## Crash

```
ValueError: There is no module or parameter named 'fc.weight' in Qwen3_5MultiTokenPredictor
```

Raised from the weight-map walk in `vllm/model_executor/models/utils.py` (`_load_module`, the "no module or parameter named" branch), reached via `Qwen3_5MultiTokenPredictor.load_weights` (`vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_5_mtp.py`). The engine never reaches runtime — deterministic at boot.

## Root Cause

`Qwen3_5MultiTokenPredictor.__init__` builds its `fc` (`ColumnParallelLinear`) and decoder layers from `vllm_config.quant_config` — the **target's** config. The file already contains two workarounds for the dense-draft-on-quantized-target family:

1. `modelopt_fp4`: `fc_quant = None` because "mtp.fc is stored as BF16 in NVFP4 checkpoints but is missing from hf_quant_config.json exclude_modules" (PR #38650)
2. GPTQ: `quantization_config.dynamic` `-:mtp` patterns → build all MTP layers unquantized

**Neither covers compressed-tensors.** For this checkpoint:

- `config.json` → `quantization_config.format: "pack-quantized"`, method `compressed-tensors`; the `ignore` list covers `model.visual.*`, `model.language_model.layers.*.linear_attn*`, `lm_head` — **no `mtp` entry**
- `model.safetensors.index.json` → 15 `mtp.*` tensors, **all dense** (plain `.weight` names, e.g. `mtp.fc.weight`, `mtp.layers.0.mlp.down_proj.weight`), all in a dedicated `model-mtp-bf16.safetensors` shard

So the quantizer left the MTP head unquantized **without declaring it in `ignore`**, vLLM builds the MTP Linears pack-quantized, and the dense names cannot resolve.

This is a cousin of #51581 (DFlash2 `_build_context_kv_buffers` slicing `.weight` on a pack-quantized target) — same family of draft/MTP structures assuming dense parameters on quantized targets.

## Suggested Fix

Extend the existing workaround family: when the target quant config is compressed-tensors (pack-quantized) and the checkpoint's MTP tensors are dense — detectable either from the safetensors index (plain `mtp.*.weight` names, no packed variants) or from a dedicated bf16 MTP shard — build the MTP predictor unquantized, mirroring the `modelopt_fp4` path for `fc` and the GPTQ `dynamic` path for the layers.

Happy to provide the full boot log or test a fix branch — the checkpoint and repro are on hand.
