title: [Feature]: [ROCm][AITER][Hy4] Enable gfx950 MXFP8 MoE and dense linear backends
body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

`tencent/Hy4-preview-FP8` runs on gfx950 through the ROCm support added in #57526, but its ModelOpt MXFP8 operations currently use Triton even when `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`:
```text
Using RocmDotScaledMxfp8LinearKernel for MXFP8 GEMM
Using 'TRITON_MXFP8' MxFp8 MoE backend.
```
This feature request tracks two independent AITER enablement categories. 

cc: @akii96 (I know you're focused on gfx942, but wanted to keep you in the loop)

### 1. MXFP8 MoE enablement
vLLM already provides `AiterMxfp8Experts`, but its compatibility check rejects Hy4.
The current AITER implementation requires:
- `SWIGLUOAI_UNINTERLEAVE`
- SwiGLU alpha `1.702`
- SwiGLU beta `1.0`
Hy4 instead uses clamped SwiGLU:
```text
gate = clamp(gate, max=limit)
up   = clamp(up, -limit, limit)
out  = silu(gate) * up
```
The published checkpoint sets `swiglu_limit=10.0`.

#### AITER work
- Support Hy4’s gate/up layout and clamped SwiGLU semantics in the gfx950 MXFP8 fused-MoE kernel.
- Preserve native 1×32 E8M0 weights/scales.
- Support Hy4 routing, expert masks and tensor-parallel execution.
- Add correctness tests against a BF16/dequantized reference.

#### vLLM work
- Represent Hy4’s activation semantics accurately in `FusedMoEConfig`.
- Update `AiterMxfp8Experts.is_supported_config`.
- Forward activation, clamp and gate-layout arguments to AITER.
- Verify automatic selection and explicit `--moe-backend aiter`.
- Preserve `TRITON_MXFP8` fallback.
- Add Hy4 MXFP8 MoE unit and end-to-end coverage.

### 2. MXFP8 dense linear/GEMM enablement
Hy4’s dense projections use ModelOpt MXFP8:
- E4M3 values
- E8M0 scales
- 1×32 scaling blocks
- BF16 output
This is not format-compatible with AITER’s conventional FP8 128×128 block-scale GEMMs. vLLM therefore selects `RocmDotScaledMxfp8LinearKernel`.

#### AITER work
- Add a gfx950 dense MXFP8 GEMM accepting the 1×32 E8M0 format.
- Support dynamic `M`, weight pre-shuffling, split-K and caller-owned output buffers.
- Add runtime configuration lookup, shape logging and a gfx950 tuner.
- Add correctness tests against dequantized BF16.

#### vLLM work
- Add an AITER-backed `Mxfp8LinearKernel`.
- Register it in `_POSSIBLE_MXFP8_KERNELS[PlatformEnum.ROCM]` ahead of Triton when supported.
- Implement gfx950, AITER and scale-layout capability checks.
- Add weight/scale preprocessing and pre-shuffling.
- Support `torch.compile` and full/piecewise cudagraph capture.
- Preserve Triton and emulation fallbacks.
- Add kernel-selection and end-to-end tests.


### Alternatives

- Continue using `RocmDotScaledMxfp8LinearKernel` and `TRITON_MXFP8`.
- Dequantize MXFP8 weights to BF16, with additional memory and performance cost.
- Generic AITER A8W8 block-scale kernels are not a valid substitute because their scale format differs from ModelOpt MXFP8.

title: [Spec Decode][dflash] Drafter KV group is never identified, so prefix-cache reuse is silently disabled for the Mamba groups
body:
AI-authored (disclosed): produced and verified on our live CMP 170HX cluster; the account owner is a user, not a vLLM dev.

### Summary

With `method="dflash"` the drafter's KV cache group is never identified, so the consumer falls back to treating **every** group as a draft group -- including the Mamba/GDN groups -- and prefix-cache reuse across requests is silently disabled for those layers. The warning is printed on every start:

```
Speculative decoding (method=dflash) is enabled but no KV cache group could be
identified as the draft model's, so every group -- including Mamba groups [0, 1, 2, 3]
-- will be treated as a draft group. A Mamba group cannot satisfy the widened lookup
window that implies, so prefix-cache reuse across requests will be disabled ...
```

`_uses_trailing_mtp_layers()` (the positional fallback generalized in #55390) is gated on `spec_config.method == "mtp"`. `dflash` drafts reuse the target's decoder-layer architecture, so their attention spec is indistinguishable from the target's and the spec-driven rule cannot find them either.

### Measured consequence -- corrected

**Correction (2026-09-16, see the validation comment below):** this section originally attributed the
36.4 s prefix-child TTFT to the missing draft-group annotation. That attribution is wrong. With the
annotation patch applied (`xiaoba17/vllm@40681e0c9d`) the same 35-36 s reproduces and the engine's
prefix-cache counters are byte-identical; the annotation fix is correct and worth carrying, but it does
not gate this symptom.

What does gate it is the **Mamba checkpoint retention policy** plus prefill chunk granularity. On the
same box, same payload: `--prefix-cache-retention-interval 832` takes the 51.8k prefix child from
35.15 s to 5.83 s (+74,880 reused tokens = 10 x 7,488), and `--max-num-batched-tokens 1664` takes it to
1.47 s (= an exact re-send) for ~13 % extra on the cold parent prefill. The default
`prefix_cache_retention_interval=0` keeps only semantic replay boundaries, so a child that extends a
cached parent resumes from a much earlier checkpoint. For reference, an **identical** re-send resumes
in 1.5 s in every configuration -- which is why the original comparison looked like an annotation
problem.

### Ask

Extend the trailing-layer positional fallback (with the `_groups_partition_layers_exactly` guard added in #55390) to `method == "dflash"`, or state why it cannot apply there. If dflash drafts are guaranteed to register their KV layers after every target layer the same way MTP drafts do, the rule should transfer; if they are not, some other annotation path is needed, because the flag-all fallback quietly costs the Mamba-group reuse in any dflash deployment.

### Environment / evidence

- vLLM v0.13.0 line (fork image `vllm/vllm-backport:cmp170hx`, sha256 `2d27fe8655b0c57b953dc3dff72034df0a98abf2a1ff07387e48f6a0af886a2a`), V2 GPU model runner.
- Reproducible on every start; no special flags beyond the ones above. Raw server logs, per-request TTFT/JSONL and the harness are kept on the machine and available on request.

---
AI-authored contribution (omp agent). The account owner is a user running these models in production: they reported the failure, asked for the fix, and run it live today. They are not a vLLM developer and do not vouch for the code -- please verify it independently (logs, configs and image digests on request). Thanks for the maintainer work, and apologies for the review load that AI-written reports add; if you would rather not get them, say so and we will stop. If our fix causes trouble, we will keep driving it.

title: [RFC] RL Test Consolidation: File Ownership, Coverage Docstrings, and CI Integration
body:
## Summary

This is a follow-up to **[RFC #45585: RL CI Matrix for vLLM: Behavioral + Physical + Protocol Coverage](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/45585)**.

We propose keeping its three functional categories:

1. **State transitions**
2. **Information retrieval**
3. **Consistency**

The change is how those categories map to **existing test files, new tests, and CI execution**. RL-related coverage already exists in entrypoints, engines, workers, allocators, model loaders, model-specific tests, and kernels. Consolidation should account for that coverage before adding or moving suites.

Specifically:

- Keep component-level regressions next to the component they test.
- Consolidate duplicate tests at the same interface/layer.
- Use `tests/entrypoints/serve/dev/rlhf/` for RL HTTP contracts and cross-component lifecycle tests.
- Document category scope and existing coverage locations in the **`rlhf/__init__.py` module docstring**, and explain each test module's contract and boundaries in its own **module docstring**. No new test README is proposed.
- Give each test/configuration an explicit CI execution owner, with appropriate GPU count, backend, and platform selection.
- Amend the existing PRs rather than replacing them with a new umbrella implementation PR.

This issue proposes the reorganization; the file moves, test changes, and CI changes below are not implemented by opening this RFC.

## Relationship to existing RFCs

#45585 remains the umbrella motivation and behavioral/physical/protocol coverage framework. This proposal revises its blanket migration approach and updates the implementation plan against coverage that has since landed.

It does not replace the product contracts in the related RFCs:

- #48311 — Engine Sleep/Wake/Drain Lifecycle for RL
- #48310 — Sleep/Wake Correctness for RL
- #48312 — Weight Reload Correctness for RL
- #48306 — RL Information Retrieval: APIs & Introspection
- #42259 — Logprobs/Logits Semantics and Determinism
- #51476 — DP pause/sleep correctness and layering

Those RFCs define the relevant semantics. This issue defines where their regression coverage belongs, how the current test PRs should be adjusted, and how CI should execute it. Proposed semantics must not be treated as already implemented contracts.

## Why revisit the file mapping?

The original breakdown was largely one topic/file/PR at a time. The broad categories still make sense, but the repository now has overlapping coverage at different layers.

Examples:

- `test_mem.py` covers more than allocator flags: it includes CUDA graphs, offline sleep/reload, LoRA, async deep sleep, and FP8 KV cache.
- `test_weight_transfer_llm.py` uses a mock transfer engine to test the LLM API contract; it does not replace real IPC/NCCL transfer tests.
- `test_reload.py` already changes checkpoints and checks their effect, including quantized and distributed configurations.
- Engine and DP suites already cover pause/resume, late requests, drain, and race/deadlock regressions.
- Routed-experts tests exist at frontend, model-executor, and kernel layers.

Moving every one of these into an HTTP test directory would obscure ownership. Adding a new HTTP test for every existing lower-level case would increase cost without necessarily adding useful coverage.

The inventory below is based on a repository source audit and targeted upstream-main checks. It is a coverage inventory, **not a claim that every listed configuration currently passes CI**.

## Current PR status

Snapshot at filing (2026-09-05). Short head SHAs identify the versions inspected; PR bodies and historical test results may describe earlier revisions.

| Area | PR | Status | Inspected head | Current scope |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Sleep/wake | #54930 | Open, draft | `c573143585ce` | HTTP sleep/wake suite parameterized over MRV1/MRV2 |
| Pause/resume | #52144 | Merged | `bf2c4252763e` | HTTP pause modes, request lifecycle, idempotency, validation, cache behavior |
| Weight update + metrics | #53541 | Open, non-draft | `accc4d3f0e1c` | Transfer tests, reload smoke, metrics, and new frontend state/version machinery |
| Weight checker | #51350 | Open, non-draft | `7252f6670c65` | Checksum/reset/compare feature and tests, including distributed reload verification |
| Response schema + weight info | #52864 | Open, non-draft | `8314de984014` | Structured sleep responses and current weight-version HTTP contract |
| Routed experts | #52902 | Open, draft | `df0f2194f653` | Latest diff: TP2×DP2 token-in/token-out capture and reduced-model OpenAI frontend coverage |
| CPU lifecycle-state coverage | No dedicated PR in this breakdown | Proposed gap audit | — | Extend production-module tests after subtracting existing engine/worker/DP coverage |

## Proposed ownership rules

1. **Place tests near their direct subject.** Allocator, worker, loader, and kernel invariants normally stay in their component suites.
2. **Merge duplication within a layer.** Two HTTP tests checking the same endpoint behavior are candidates for consolidation. A worker error-path test and an HTTP lifecycle test can be complementary.
3. **Review mixed files by test group.** A file containing allocator and offline-LLM cases must not be moved wholesale based on its name.
4. **Preserve execution coverage when moving tests.** Preserve frontend variants, eager/graph coverage, supported platforms, and resource requirements.
5. **Test the production state owner.** Do not create an independent test-only state machine just to populate a planned file.
6. **Use the cheapest effective level.** Exhaustive input validation and local invariants belong in unit tests; retain a small E2E set for actual cross-layer behavior.

### Existing coverage and proposed disposition

All paths below are repository-relative. “Keep” means retain the test's primary implementation location and reference it from the RL coverage docstrings.

| Category | Existing file | Coverage | Proposed disposition |
|---|---|---|---|
| State transitions | `tests/entrypoints/serve/dev/test_sleep.py` | HTTP flags, metrics, staged wake | Merge into `rlhf/state_transitions/test_sleep_wake.py`; remove old file only after coverage parity |
| State transitions | `tests/entrypoints/serve/dev/rlhf/state_transitions/test_pause_resume.py` | HTTP pause/resume contract | Keep |
| State transitions | `tests/v1/engine/test_async_llm.py` | Engine pause modes, queued cancellation, multiple requests | Keep; avoid duplicating its complete matrix at HTTP level |
| State transitions | `tests/v1/distributed/test_async_llm_dp.py` | DP/EP pause, late requests/drain, staggered ranks, barrier regressions; upstream also has wait/device-idle cases | Keep in distributed CI; reference exact relevant test functions |
| State transitions | `tests/v1/worker/test_sleep_mode_backend.py` | Backend factory, capabilities, backend state | Keep; this is not engine lifecycle-state coverage |
| State transitions | `tests/basic_correctness/test_mem.py` | Allocator/discard/graph and offline sleep/reload | Keep initially; any later split separates allocator from offline-LLM groups and preserves assertions |
| State transitions | `tests/models/language/generation/test_gdn_sleep_wake.py` | Hybrid state-cache regression after wake | Keep model-specific ownership and hybrid-model selection |
| State transitions | `tests/entrypoints/weight_transfer/test_weight_transfer_llm.py` | LLM API delegation through mock transport, version behavior | Keep |
| State transitions | `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_worker_weight_transfer.py` | Session guards, delegation, error cleanup | Keep and extend only for missing behavior |
| State transitions | `tests/distributed/test_weight_transfer.py` | IPC/NCCL/sparse transport, trainer/client, metadata validation | Keep |
| State transitions | `tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_reload.py` | Actual A/B checkpoint reload, quantization, KV scales, aliases/buffers/storage | Keep and extend here instead of duplicating weaker reload tests |
| Consistency | `tests/entrypoints/openai/test_return_routed_experts.py` | OpenAI frontend capture response | Retain lightweight frontend smoke; share validation helpers if useful |
| Consistency | `tests/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/test_return_routed_experts.py` | Token-in/token-out capture response | Retain single-GPU smoke; add multi-GPU coverage separately |
| Consistency | `tests/model_executor/test_routed_experts_capture.py` | EPLB/DP/TP capture, MRV2 output, KV-group selection | Keep |
| Consistency | `tests/kernels/moe/test_routed_experts_capture_monolithic.py` | Backend-specific BF16/FP8/NVFP4 capture | Keep in supported-hardware kernel jobs |
| Consistency | `tests/v1/sample/test_logprobs.py`, `test_logprobs_e2e.py`, and `tests/v1/determinism/` | General logprobs/determinism | Keep; RL adds lifecycle-specific checks only |

Frontend routed-experts smoke may instead be physically consolidated if maintainers prefer. The acceptance condition is unchanged: preserve the independently runnable frontend contracts, remove duplicate copies, and update CI ownership. This RFC's default is to keep them near their frontends.

## Coverage documentation through docstrings

### Package docstring

Add a concise, documentation-only `tests/entrypoints/serve/dev/rlhf/__init__.py` describing:

- The three categories and their behavioral scope.
- RL HTTP/lifecycle modules maintained under this package.
- Existing component coverage outside this package, with repository-relative paths and representative function/class names.
- The distinction between local coverage and referenced coverage.
- Links to #45585 and this follow-up RFC.

It must not import the referenced suites, initialize GPU dependencies, or change test collection.

### Test-module docstrings

Each affected test module should explain:

- The production interface/contract it tests.
- The observable failure or regression it guards.
- Important coverage already owned by another test module.
- Non-obvious execution requirements or matrix boundaries.

For example, the sleep/wake module could document the following intended boundary:

```python
"""HTTP sleep/wake lifecycle coverage for RL rollout.

Checks request gating during partial wake and successful generation after
memory and weights are restored. Resource-only and long-cycle cases are
selected separately from the small lifecycle smoke suite.

Related coverage:
    tests/basic_correctness/test_mem.py: allocator and offline sleep/reload.
    tests/v1/distributed/test_async_llm_dp.py: DP pause/drain regressions.
    tests/models/language/generation/test_gdn_sleep_wake.py: hybrid state cache.
"""
```

The final wording must describe assertions actually implemented by the module.

Keep volatile PR status and outstanding work in this RFC, rather than embedding “done” claims in Python files. Docstrings record stable scope and ownership; CI configuration remains authoritative for execution. Update affected cross-references in the same change as a move or rename. No symlinks, wrapper imports, or new README are needed.

## Target RL HTTP/lifecycle modules

Under `tests/entrypoints/serve/dev/rlhf/`:

| Subpackage | Module | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| Package | `__init__.py` | Category scope and coverage-location index |
| Package | `conftest.py` | Shared fixtures and narrowly reusable HTTP/lifecycle helpers |
| State transitions | `test_pause_resume.py` | Existing minimal HTTP request-lifecycle contract |
| State transitions | `test_sleep_wake.py` | HTTP gating, staged/full wake, restored generation |
| State transitions | `test_weight_update.py` | Configured real transfer, error contract, version/cache effects |
| State transitions | `test_weight_update_metrics.py` | Actual transaction metrics, after metric semantics are agreed |
| State transitions | `test_weight_checker.py` | Checker API and corruption/recovery verification |
| State transitions | `test_rl_step.py` (proposed) | Small compound lifecycle across interfaces |
| Information retrieval | `test_response_schema.py` | Response fields/types and rejected-input behavior |
| Information retrieval | `test_weight_info.py` | Current `weight_version` query/update contract |
| Consistency | `test_routed_experts.py` | Lifecycle/cache-related routing correctness beyond frontend smoke |

CPU engine-state tests should extend nearby engine suites, or use a narrowly scoped engine test module if no existing suite fits. Worker session tests remain in the existing worker module. We do not require the original `rlhf/test_state_machine*.py` layout.

## Planned changes to existing PRs

### #54930 — Sleep/wake

- Move the suite to `state_transitions/` and consolidate the old HTTP sleep test with explicit coverage parity.
- Replace “request was not successful” checks with precise pending/rejected/completed semantics.
- For partial wake, observe that the **same request** does not complete prematurely and does complete after full wake; propagate background exceptions and join all threads.
- Cover both tag orders where supported. A fresh successful request after wake is not sufficient to prove the earlier request survived.
- Separate level-2 flag/resource checks from recovery tests. A level-2 recovery test must restore weights before generation; a shared fixture cannot treat wake alone as weight restoration.
- Verify cache effects directly, rather than only checking that a repeated prompt generates.
- Merge redundant flag/cycle cases; keep representative runner and graph coverage.
- Separate long-cycle resource checks from smoke. Put dedicated performance benchmarks under the benchmark infrastructure rather than making general CI depend on machine-specific latency limits.
- Use exact idempotency/error contracts instead of accepting unrelated status codes such as both 200 and 400.

### #52144 — Pause/resume

Keep the merged suite and its focused contract. Amend helpers only through a coordinated infrastructure change.

Changes motivated by #51476 should track the relevant implementation contract. Do not change admission expectations solely because a proposed semantic change exists. Also distinguish engine completion from the client's receipt of the final streaming chunk when synchronizing assertions.

### #53541 — Weight update and metrics

Separate the test increment from product-design changes:

1. Real HTTP transfer and protocol tests.
2. Metrics implementation/semantics and associated tests.
3. Any additional state-management feature, only after demonstrating a gap in the existing engine/worker ownership.

Required test changes:

- Success tests use a configured/initialized backend and require success; HTTP 500 is not a successful protocol outcome.
- Invalid-order tests have explicit expected responses and state-preservation/recovery checks.
- Provide deterministic compatible A/B weights in CI. Core transfer coverage must not silently disappear because `VLLM_TEST_MODEL_ALT` is unset.
- Compare warm-updated B with a B reference, or another controlled numerical oracle; “text changed” alone does not establish correct transfer.
- Warm the relevant cache under A, update to B, and verify cache coherence and B results.
- Remove or relocate the reload smoke that only calls initialize/finalize without loading replacement weights. Reuse `test_reload.py` for actual model/quantization reload coverage.
- Exercise real metric transitions: active 0→1→0, successful counter increments, histogram observation count, and the agreed failure behavior.
- Define multi-API-process and DP metric/state ownership; frontend-local state and a fixed engine label need explicit justification.

There is also a cross-PR contract conflict: #52864 tests the existing `weight_version` response, while #53541 introduces `weight_gen/weight_label` and expands `/weight_info`. Resolve the API design first. Weakening schema tests to accept both is not the resolution. This proposal defaults to the upstream `weight_version` contract; any additional counter has separate semantics.

### #51350 — Weight checker

Keep this as a feature PR with its own focused tests.

- Align documentation and tests with the latest checksum/reset/compare baseline lifecycle, including compare's one-shot behavior.
- Ensure tests independently establish/consume their baseline and restore mutated weights.
- Use small unit tests for supported tensor types, hashing/coverage policy, and key merging.
- Verify the complete rank-qualified key inventory and negative cases such as missing ranks/tensors or changed values.
- Retain distributed reset→reload→compare; add real-transfer restoration as a distinct integration path.
- Schedule TP2×DP2×EP on an explicitly provisioned four-GPU job.

### #52864 — Schema and weight information

Keep the current scope. Use router-level CPU tests with a fake engine client for exhaustive field/input validation where practical, plus a small real-engine E2E set.

A schema matrix does not need to multiply every case by runner and parallelism. Successful transfer's version-commit behavior belongs in weight-update/compound lifecycle coverage.

### #52902 — Routed experts

Reconcile the PR description and reported results with the latest diff before expanding it.

The inspected version primarily checks capture shape/range across frontends/models and TP2×DP2. That should not be described as complete routing-replay correctness.

- Preserve cheap single-GPU frontend smoke when adding distributed/model cases.
- Add exact token/row alignment, cache-hit recovery, mixed-batch isolation, and lifecycle-related stale-routing checks.
- Shape/range alone cannot detect a valid-range all-zero capture; use a controlled/reference routing oracle where applicable.
- Repeated deterministic generation is not a test of consuming captured routes for replay. Add actual replay validation only through an available supported path; otherwise track it as a gap.
- Keep backend-specific checks near kernel tests and explicitly select supported hardware.
- Reduced-geometry dummy models establish code-path coverage, not real-checkpoint numerical correctness.
- Preserve graph coverage explicitly; a shared harness that forces eager cannot establish graph behavior.

### Shared infrastructure

Resolve the differing `server()` signatures/defaults across these PRs in one coordinated change. Prefer the repository's existing server utilities where they fit. Make model, environment, sleep enablement, execution mode, port handling, logging, and process cleanup explicit.

Do not collapse transport exceptions into a generic unsuccessful response for behavioral assertions. Reuse servers only when state is restored reliably; destructive weight changes need restoration or isolation.

## CI integration

Keep the three functional categories, and split execution within them by cost and resource requirements.

| Execution group | Scope | Resource policy |
|---|---|---|
| CPU/unit | Router contracts, actual engine/worker invariants, checker small-tensor behavior | Verify collection and execution without GPU dependencies |
| State transitions smoke | Core pause/sleep behavior, real IPC, minimal compound step | One GPU where topology permits; critical MRV1/MRV2 compatibility paths |
| Information retrieval smoke | Schema/version; small real-engine cross-check | CPU plus a small one-GPU E2E subset |
| Consistency smoke | Small-MoE capture/alignment and lifecycle correctness | One GPU, selected eager/graph scenarios |
| Distributed | NCCL, TP, DP/EP, rank completeness | Explicit two/four-GPU topology, including trainer resources |
| Hardware/extended | Supported quantization/kernel paths, long cycles, larger models | Dedicated hardware and explicit optional/scheduled selection |

Operational requirements:

- The existing entrypoints API-server job recursively collects `entrypoints/serve`. Its upstream four-way sharding does not provide four GPUs to an individual test.
- If dedicated RL jobs take ownership, exclude those tests from the former recursive job in the same change, including applicable AMD mirrors.
- Existing component jobs should remain the primary owners of their suites. The RL docstrings reference them without causing duplicate collection.
- Update source-file dependencies as well as pytest commands when moving tests.
- Use supported markers and explicit job selection. Adding a `nightly` marker alone does not schedule a job.
- Record passed, skipped, and deselected configurations separately. An advertised critical lane that skips its only transfer/hardware case is not established coverage.
- Avoid a full model × runner × backend × parallelism Cartesian product. Select combinations that exercise materially different paths.

## Remaining implementation work and order

- [ ] Agree on the file-ownership table and the docstring-based coverage index.
- [ ] Coordinate shared harness changes across the open PRs.
- [ ] Amend #54930 and consolidate the old HTTP sleep test without losing coverage.
- [ ] Separate and strengthen #53541; resolve version/metrics/state ownership with #52864.
- [ ] Audit CPU lifecycle gaps against existing engine, worker, and upstream DP tests; add only missing production behavior.
- [ ] Add a minimal complete RL-step test, then two consecutive steps.
- [ ] Complete #51350's checker contract and assign its distributed execution lane.
- [ ] Amend #52902 with precise capture-versus-replay scope and preserve frontend smoke.
- [ ] Add or reuse physical edge-case regressions after checking prior work in #45585.
- [ ] Wire CI ownership/resource selection and verify collection after every migration.
- [ ] Extend model/backend-specific coverage only where the inventory identifies an uncovered path.

A representative level-2 compound step is:

```text
rollout with A
→ pause/quiesce according to the implemented contract
→ sleep(level=2)
→ wake(weights)
→ transfer B and finish(weight_version=B)
→ wake(kv_cache), restore scheduling as required
→ rollout and compare with B reference
→ repeat for the next version
```

Assert request liveness, restored output/logprobs, committed version, and cache coherence. Metrics/checker assertions can be added as their features land; they need not block the initial compound test.

Coordinate physical tests with the earlier contributions linked in #45585. Its discussion also contains ownership of parallel-sampling abort-count/parent-child cleanup work; this reorganization should not duplicate that feature work.

## Acceptance criteria and feedback requested

Consolidation is complete when:

- Every claimed behavior has an identifiable test implementation and CI execution path.
- File moves preserve relevant platforms, frontends, and execution modes.
- Same-layer duplicates are removed; complementary component tests remain discoverable.
- Package and module docstrings describe implemented scope and point to existing coverage.
- Core real-transfer and lifecycle tests run in their designated lanes with meaningful oracles.
- PR descriptions match the current diff and separate source-audited coverage from actually executed validation.

Feedback requested: agreement on the ownership/migration table, frontend routed-experts placement, and resource-based CI partitioning before implementing the reorganization.

**Validation for this RFC:** source/diff review and targeted upstream-main/CI inspection only. No code changes or GPU test runs are claimed.

title: [Performance]: GLM-5.3-Flash on H100: auto-selected FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM90 is 36-70% slower than FLASH_ATTN_MLA_SPARSE
body:
### Your current environment

<details>
<summary>vllm collect-env (abridged)</summary>

```
OS                           : Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS (x86_64)
PyTorch version              : 2.13.0+cu130
CUDA runtime version         : 13.0.88
GPU                          : 8x NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3 (single node, TP=8)
Nvidia driver version        : 595.71.05
vLLM Version                 : 0.28.1rc1.dev580+g385dce36b (git sha: 385dce36b)
Docker image                 : vllm/vllm-openai:glm53-flash @ sha256:819ec9c063412e5730d1b0e82046ba540d1bf991f3c4f661a849aae8a0c52374
[pip3] flashinfer-python==0.6.18
[pip3] torch==2.13.0+cu130
[pip3] triton==3.7.1
```
</details>

### 🐛 Describe the bug

**Summary:** For `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash` on H100 the auto-selected sparse-MLA attention backend is `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM90` (log: `Using FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM90 attention backend out of potential backends: ['FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM90', 'FLASH_ATTN_MLA_SPARSE']`). It is **~36% slower at concurrency 1 and ~70% slower at concurrency 8** than the other candidate, `FLASH_ATTN_MLA_SPARSE`, measured with `vllm bench serve` on the same server flags. MTP draft acceptance is identical across the two, so the gap is per-step attention cost, not speculative-decoding behaviour. Forcing `--attention-backend FLASH_ATTN_MLA_SPARSE` recovers it.

**How we found it:** we had been serving from an image built on 2026-08-26 from the `glm-release` branch (base `487ecf187`, FlashInfer 0.6.17). That build logs `Using FLASH_ATTN_MLA_SPARSE attention backend out of potential backends: ['FLASH_ATTN_MLA_SPARSE', 'FLASHMLA_SPARSE']`. After moving to the current `vllm/vllm-openai:glm53-flash` (nightly `385dce36b`, FlashInfer 0.6.18) with identical flags, the backend line changed to `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM90` and single-stream throughput dropped by roughly a third. The preference appears to come from #53906 (`031c899d` "[Model] Use FlashInfer for GLM-5.3-Flash NoPE MLA", `e34f7f71` "[Kernel] Use FlashInfer rc10 for NoPE MLA") and is gated on the FlashInfer version, so the 0.6.17 -> 0.6.18 bump flipped the kernel without any flag change.

**Server launch (both runs identical except the one flag):**

```bash
docker run --gpus all --ipc=host -p 8000:8000 \
  -v /path/to/hf-cache:/root/.cache/huggingface \
  -e VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=3600 \
  vllm/vllm-openai:glm53-flash \
  zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash \
  --served-model-name zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":5}' \
  --tool-call-parser glm47 --enable-auto-tool-choice --reasoning-parser glm45 \
  --max-model-len 262144 --max-num-seqs 512
  # "FA3" rows add:  --attention-backend FLASH_ATTN_MLA_SPARSE
```

**Benchmark (run inside the same container):**

```bash
vllm bench serve --backend openai-chat --endpoint /v1/chat/completions --base-url http://localhost:8000 \
  --model zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash --served-model-name zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash \
  --dataset-name sonnet --dataset-path /vllm-workspace/benchmarks/sonnet.txt \
  --sonnet-input-len 300 --sonnet-output-len 256 --sonnet-prefix-len 100 \
  --num-prompts 20 --num-warmups 2 --max-concurrency {1,8} --ignore-eos --disable-shuffle --temperature 0 --seed 0
# "random" rows: --dataset-name random --random-input-len 300 --random-output-len 256
```

| dataset | max-concurrency | backend | output tok/s | mean TPOT | mean ITL | median E2E (256 tok) | MTP accept len / rate |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| sonnet | 1 | `FLASH_ATTN_MLA_SPARSE` (forced) | **368.8** | 2.28 ms | 10.9 ms | 698 ms | 4.89 / 77.8% |
| sonnet | 1 | `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM90` (default) | 237.0 | 3.83 ms | 18.3 ms | 1064 ms | 4.89 / 77.7% |
| sonnet | 8 | `FLASH_ATTN_MLA_SPARSE` (forced) | **754.1** | 5.00 ms | 23.9 ms | 1914 ms | 4.90 / 77.9% |
| sonnet | 8 | `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM90` (default) | 229.8 | 17.4 ms | 82.9 ms | 5470 ms | 4.87 / 77.3% |
| random | 1 | `FLASH_ATTN_MLA_SPARSE` (forced) | **249.3** | 3.59 ms | 10.9 ms | 1006 ms | 3.08 / 41.7% |
| random | 1 | `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM90` (default) | 162.9 | 5.78 ms | 17.0 ms | 1570 ms | 2.97 / 39.5% |

(sonnet is a best case for MTP on this model, random a worst case; the ratio between backends is the same in both.) Same picture with `--enable-expert-parallel` (recipe TEP strategy) and with the Hopper recipe override `--no-enable-flashinfer-autotune`.

**Expected:** the auto-selected backend should not be materially slower than an available alternative on the same hardware; or the recipe should document `--attention-backend FLASH_ATTN_MLA_SPARSE` for Hopper.

**Related:** forcing `FLASH_ATTN_MLA_SPARSE` on this nightly floods the log with `Error: Failed to initialize the TMA descriptor 1` from zero-extent descriptors (outputs correct; 0 such messages with the default backend). Filed separately: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/56563.

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Bug]: moe_permute can divide by zero with no tokens
body:
﻿### Your current environment

vLLM source at commit `0908116dd9e27766efdd46f37a108c5a6b7ade53`; Ubuntu in WSL, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu132, CUDA 13.2, NVIDIA RTX 2000 Ada.

### Describe the bug

Calling `moe_permute` with zero tokens and an `expert_map` reaches `preprocessTopkIdLauncher` with `size = 0`. It sets `block = 0`, then divides by `block` when calculating the CUDA grid size.

Expected: return empty outputs and zero expert offsets without launching sorting or permutation work.

Reproduction:

```python
import torch
from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.moe_permute_unpermute import moe_permute

hidden = torch.empty((0, 128), device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
topk_ids = torch.empty((0, 2), device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32)
expert_map = torch.arange(8, device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32)
moe_permute(hidden, None, topk_ids, 8, expert_map=expert_map)
```

The zero-block calculation is in `csrc/libtorch_stable/moe/permute_unpermute_kernels/moe_permute_unpermute_kernel.cu:174-175`.

title: [RFC]: fp8 KV cache gives little to no memory benefit on Mamba/GDN hybrid models
body:
**TL;DR**
- `--kv-cache-dtype fp8` roughly doubles KV cache capacity on attention-only models (measured 2.00x), but on Mamba/GDN + attention hybrids it gives 1.84x at 32k context and 1.00x (no gain) at short context.
- Root cause is the known hybrid page-pinning behavior (#37121, #40696): the Mamba state is not quantized by `--kv-cache-dtype` and all groups share one uniform page, so the bf16 Mamba page pins bytes-per-block and the fp8 attention page cannot shrink the pool.
- Fix is parity work: quantize the Mamba state too (SGLang already does this at int8) and/or decouple per-group page size (SGLang/TRT-LLM/llama.cpp already use separate pools). This RFC contributes the fp8-capacity characterization plus wiring a fix into vLLM.

### Motivation.

fp8 KV cache is advertised as a ~2x capacity/concurrency lever. On Mamba/attention hybrids (Falcon-H1, Qwen3-Next, Granite-4, Jamba, Nemotron-H) that lever is mostly or entirely dead, and there is no caveat in the docs. Numbers below are from vLLM's own `get_kv_cache_configs`/`get_kv_cache_capacity` (offline, no forward pass; `gpu_memory_utilization=0.85`, `max_model_len=32768`, default `block_size`, A10G). For Qwen2.5-3B and Falcon-H1 the offline bf16 result reproduces the live-served `GPU KV cache size` exactly, which validates the method; gpt-oss-20b is offline-computed and not anchored to a live run.

| model | bf16 KV tokens | fp8 KV tokens | ratio |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen2.5-3B (attention only, live-anchored) | 334,256 | 668,512 | **2.00x** |
| gpt-oss-20b (sliding-window + full, offline/unanchored) | 562,283 | 1,124,567 | **2.00x** |
| Falcon-H1-1.5B (Mamba + attention, live-anchored) | 603,229 | 1,111,381 | **1.84x** |

Falcon-H1 by context length: 512 tok 1.00x, 1024 tok 1.00x, 2048 tok 1.51x, 8192 tok 1.76x, 32768 tok 1.84x. Sliding window alone does not cause this (gpt-oss gets a clean 2.00x); the effect requires a non-attention group co-resident in the pool.

The mechanism is already filed. #37121 reports the ~7x KV memory over-estimation on hybrids: the attention block size is inflated up to the larger Mamba page, and the Mamba state is padded to match, so both grow to a common page. #40696 reports the prefix-caching consequence of the same block-size pinning. This RFC adds the fp8-capacity consequence and proposes the fix.

Why fp8 fails to help, concretely:
1. `get_mamba_state_dtype_from_config` returns bf16 regardless of `--kv-cache-dtype`, so the Mamba page is a fixed ~1.59 MB.
2. `get_uniform_page_size` asserts one page across all groups, and `_align_hybrid_block_size` (`vllm/platforms/interface.py`) enforces `attention_page >= mamba_page` by inflating the attention `block_size` (Falcon-H1: 1568 tokens at bf16, 3120 at fp8). The per-token attention page halves exactly under fp8 (1024 -> 512 B), so the block size roughly doubles (it lands one alignment step short of 2x), leaving the product pinned to the Mamba page.
3. Once pages are unified, `num_blocks` is effectively `available_memory // (uniform_page * num_groups)` (in code, `available_memory // bytes_per_block` where `bytes_per_block` is the max over groups of the summed page size). That uniform page is 1,605,632 B (bf16) vs 1,597,440 B (fp8) — essentially unchanged, so `num_blocks` moves only 405 -> 407. fp8's only gain comes from the larger block, dragged below 2x by the never-shrinking Mamba group and coarse block quantization (a short request fits in one attention block either way — the 1.00x rows).

### Proposed Change.

Two independent levers; either helps, together they recover the full 2x. Neither is novel — both exist in other engines — so the deliverable is the vLLM implementation plus the characterization above.

1. **Quantize the Mamba state alongside attention KV.** vLLM already exposes `--mamba-cache-dtype` / `--mamba-ssm-cache-dtype`, but the allowed values are only `auto/float32/float16/bfloat16` (no fp8 or int8), so today the state cannot be shrunk at all. This is the natural insertion point. SGLang ships state quantization at int8 (`--enable-int8-mamba-checkpoint`, `Int8CheckpointStore`, cited as ~2x prefix capacity), and Quamba2 (arXiv:2503.22879) quantizes the ssm_state at int8. Not yet done anywhere: fp8, and the conv_state (not just ssm_state). The recurrent path is the most quantization-sensitive component (Q-S5, arXiv:2406.09477), so this must ship with its own accuracy check (perplexity + one downstream task), not on an assumption of safety. Larger change: needs a quantized Mamba kernel path.

2. **Decouple per-group page size.** Relax the single-uniform-page invariant so an attention group keeps its smaller fp8 page instead of being inflated to the Mamba page; the pool tracks per-group bytes. This is what SGLang (separate `MambaPool`), TensorRT-LLM (separate cache managers), and llama.cpp (`llama_memory_hybrid`) already do via separate pools; academic cover in Jenga (SOSP 2025) and AVMP (preprint, arXiv:2605.22416). KV-cache-manager change only, no kernels.

Suggested phasing: (2) first as a self-contained KV-cache-manager PR that removes the pinning for the attention group (recovers most of the long-context gain, kernel-free). (1) as a follow-up that also shrinks the Mamba group, gated on the accuracy check. The characterization/probe can land as a test that asserts fp8 recovers ~2x on a small hybrid.

Out of scope: the sliding-window in-flight admission reserve (#54703, different mechanism) and block-pool logging (#54840).

### Feedback Period.

One week.

### CC List.

@heheda12345 @tdoublep

### Any Other Things.

Honest severity: the 1.00x rows are at short context, where KV is not the bottleneck, so the practical impact there is small. The impact that matters is long context, where fp8 under-delivers by ~8-16% on Mamba hybrids (1.84x vs 2.00x at 32k). Real and fixable, on a growing model class; not a crash or correctness bug.

Limitations of the measurement: one anchor hybrid (Falcon-H1) plus two attention-only controls. The mechanism is architecture-level (any non-quantized co-resident group pins the shared page), so it should generalize across Qwen3-Next/Granite-4/Jamba/Nemotron-H, but that is asserted, not yet measured per-model.

Reproduction (offline, no GPU forward pass, so it dodges any fp8 attention-kernel issues): build a `VllmConfig` via `EngineArgs.create_engine_config()`, construct per-layer `KVCacheSpec`s (Mamba shapes from `get_mamba_state_{shape,dtype}_from_config`), run `_align_hybrid_block_size` for the resolved backend, then call `get_kv_cache_configs` with a hypothetical `available_memory` and read `get_kv_cache_capacity`. bf16 reproduces live-served KV tokens exactly, which validates the fp8 numbers.

Not claimed as novel: the state-vs-KV asymmetry (Marconi, MLSys 2025), page decoupling (SGLang/TRT-LLM/llama.cpp, AVMP, Jenga), or int8 Mamba-state quantization (SGLang, Quamba2). The unpublished pieces are the fp8-capacity characterization on hybrids and, if pursued, fp8 + conv_state quantization with an accuracy frontier.

title: [Bug]: Resumable session that stops while preempted is dropped from every queue, and folds at num_computed_tokens=0
body:
### Your current environment

Scheduler-level reproduction on CPU, no model or GPU needed. Reproduces on main at `2bc902eb0f7d3e3e171002e456daee254497b46b`.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

With async scheduling, a resumable (streaming-input) request can be preempted while a step is still in flight. That step's output is delivered as stale output (deliver mode). If it contains a stop token, the request stops while in `PREEMPTED` state, and then:

1. **The session is removed from every queue and never scheduled again.**
2. **If the next chunk is already queued, the fold runs with `num_computed_tokens == 0` and truncates the whole token list,** leaving `num_prompt_tokens` and `all_token_ids` inconsistent.

Trigger: async scheduling, KV-pressure preemption of a streaming session whose in-flight step returns a stop token. Connectors that require KV delivery preempt in drop mode, so they are not affected.

#### Reproduction

Run from the repo root with `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python repro.py`:

```python
from tests.v1.core.utils import EOS_TOKEN_ID, create_requests, create_scheduler
from vllm.v1.outputs import ModelRunnerOutput


def mro(rid, toks):
    return ModelRunnerOutput(req_ids=[rid], req_id_to_index={rid: 0},
        sampled_token_ids=[toks], logprobs=None,
        prompt_logprobs_dict={rid: None}, pooler_output=[])


for with_next_chunk in (False, True):
    s = create_scheduler(async_scheduling=True)
    req = create_requests(1, num_tokens=10, max_tokens=8, req_ids=["r"])[0]
    req.resumable = True
    s.add_request(req)
    s0 = s.schedule()                      # prefill, in flight
    s1 = s.schedule()                      # decode on placeholder, in flight
    if with_next_chunk:
        nxt = create_requests(1, num_tokens=5, max_tokens=8, req_ids=["r"])[0]
        nxt.resumable = True
        s.add_request(nxt)                 # queued on streaming_queue
    s.running.remove(req)
    s._preempt_request(req, 0.0)           # e.g. KV pressure; deliver-mode stale
    s.update_from_output(s0, mro("r", [EOS_TOKEN_ID]))   # stale output hits EOS
    queues = sum(r is req for q in (s.running, s.waiting, s.skipped_waiting) for r in q)
    print(f"next_chunk_queued={with_next_chunk}: status={req.status.name} "
          f"in_queues={queues} C={req.num_computed_tokens} "
          f"num_prompt_tokens={req.num_prompt_tokens} "
          f"len(all_token_ids)={len(req.all_token_ids)}")
```

Output:

```
next_chunk_queued=False: status=WAITING_FOR_STREAMING_REQ in_queues=0 C=0 num_prompt_tokens=10 len(all_token_ids)=11
next_chunk_queued=True: status=WAITING in_queues=0 C=0 num_prompt_tokens=15 len(all_token_ids)=5
```

Expected: the session stays in exactly one queue, and after the fold `all_token_ids` holds the old prompt, the kept output tokens and the new chunk, with `num_prompt_tokens == len(all_token_ids)`.

#### Cause 1: the re-enqueued session is removed again

- `_preempt_request` sets `num_computed_tokens = 0` and puts the request in `waiting` ([L1561](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/2bc902eb0f7d3e3e171002e456daee254497b46b/vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py#L1561), [L1581](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/2bc902eb0f7d3e3e171002e456daee254497b46b/vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py#L1581)).
- The stale output stops the request with `status_before_stop == PREEMPTED` ([L2101](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/2bc902eb0f7d3e3e171002e456daee254497b46b/vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py#L2101)).
- `_handle_stopped_request` sets `WAITING_FOR_STREAMING_REQ` (or `WAITING` after a fold) and re-enqueues it ([L2407](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/2bc902eb0f7d3e3e171002e456daee254497b46b/vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py#L2407), [L2410](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/2bc902eb0f7d3e3e171002e456daee254497b46b/vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py#L2410)).
- Because the pre-stop status was not `RUNNING`, it is added to `stopped_preempted_reqs` ([L2175](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/2bc902eb0f7d3e3e171002e456daee254497b46b/vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py#L2175)), and both queues then drop it ([L2232-L2233](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/2bc902eb0f7d3e3e171002e456daee254497b46b/vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py#L2232-L2233)). `remove_requests` removes every occurrence ([request_queue.py L112](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/2bc902eb0f7d3e3e171002e456daee254497b46b/vllm/v1/core/sched/request_queue.py#L112), [L182](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/2bc902eb0f7d3e3e171002e456daee254497b46b/vllm/v1/core/sched/request_queue.py#L182)), so the entry just added goes too.

That cleanup assumes a request stopping while preempted is finished, which does not hold for resumable requests. A `WAITING_FOR_STREAMING_REQ` session is only scheduled again by staying in `skipped_waiting` ([L890-L897](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/2bc902eb0f7d3e3e171002e456daee254497b46b/vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py#L890-L897), [L3104-L3106](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/2bc902eb0f7d3e3e171002e456daee254497b46b/vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py#L3104-L3106)): when the next chunk arrives, `add_request` only calls `_update_request_as_session` and does not enqueue ([L2546](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/2bc902eb0f7d3e3e171002e456daee254497b46b/vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py#L2546)). The session hangs.

As far as I can tell from the code, the no-queued-chunk case follows from the `skipped_waiting` removal added in #48245. Before it, only `waiting` was cleaned and the re-enqueued `skipped_waiting` entry survived. I did not run the pre-#48245 code.

#### Cause 2: the fold uses `num_computed_tokens` as the keep boundary

`_update_request_as_session` keeps `all_token_ids[num_prompt_tokens:num_computed_tokens]` and deletes `all_token_ids[num_computed_tokens:]` ([L1628-L1631](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/2bc902eb0f7d3e3e171002e456daee254497b46b/vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py#L1628-L1631)). After preemption `num_computed_tokens == 0`, so the slice is empty and `del all_token_ids[0:]` removes the prompt as well. `prompt_token_ids` is a separate list ([request.py L150](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/2bc902eb0f7d3e3e171002e456daee254497b46b/vllm/v1/request.py#L150)) and is only extended, so `num_prompt_tokens` ([L1649](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/2bc902eb0f7d3e3e171002e456daee254497b46b/vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py#L1649)) no longer matches `all_token_ids`. The previous turn's output is lost.

`num_computed_tokens` is used both as "positions with KV" and as "tokens to keep". These coincide for a running request but not after preemption, where every token is still valid and only needs recomputing.

#### Possible fix directions

- Apply the `stopped_preempted_reqs` queue cleanup only to requests that actually finished, or re-enqueue resumable requests after it.
- In the fold, choose the kept tokens by position (keep `[num_prompt_tokens, num_tokens - 1)`, dropping the final sampled token as today) and clamp `num_computed_tokens` to that boundary instead of using it as the boundary.

#### Related

- Fix: #58778.
- #58668 is a separate bug in the same fold: a speculative step that stops on an accepted draft leaves `num_computed_tokens` too high. It does not affect this issue.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to find and reproduce this.

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Searched existing issues and PRs (open and closed) for this path; none found.

title: [Bug]: DeepSeek-V4-Flash + DFlash speculator fails at startup (fp8_ds_mla draft KV dtype; 16384 vs 4096 hidden states)
body:
### Your current environment

vLLM `main` @ 73a78e6f1f, 2× B300 (SM100), TP2 + expert parallel. Reproduced with `--load-format dummy` (the failures are at startup, before any weights matter).

### 🐛 Describe the bug

`DeepSeek-V4-Flash` + the `RedHatAI/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-speculator.dflash` DFlash drafter fails at startup on current `main`, in one of two ways depending on the drafter's KV cache dtype.

**1. fp8 target KV cache (default draft KV dtype): no attention backend for the drafter**

```bash
vllm serve RedHatAI/DeepSeek-V4-Flash --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 --trust-remote-code \
  --max-model-len 131072 --tensor-parallel-size 2 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --block-size 256 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --load-format dummy --enforce-eager \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dflash","model":"RedHatAI/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-speculator.dflash","num_speculative_tokens":7}'
```

The drafter's sliding-window layers inherit the target's `fp8_ds_mla` KV cache dtype, which no non-MLA backend supports:

```
ValueError: No valid attention backend found for cuda with AttentionSelectorConfig(head_size=256, dtype=torch.bfloat16, kv_cache_dtype=fp8_ds_mla, block_size=256, use_mla=False, ..., has_sliding_window=True, ...). Reasons: {FLASHINFER: [kv_cache_dtype not supported], FLASH_ATTN: [kv_cache_dtype not supported, FP8 KV cache requires FA3 on SM90, FA4 with head_size=512 on SM90, or FA4 on SM100], TRITON_ATTN: [kv_cache_dtype not supported], FLEX_ATTENTION: [kv_cache_dtype not supported], TURBOQUANT: [kv_cache_dtype not supported, sliding window not supported]}.
```

(Forcing `"attention_backend": "FLASH_ATTN"` in the speculative config fails the same way: `kv_cache_dtype not supported`.)

**2. bf16 draft KV cache: hidden-state width mismatch in `propose`**

Same command, with `"attention_backend":"FLASH_ATTN","kv_cache_dtype":"auto"` added to the speculative config. The backend check passes, and the profile run then fails:

```
File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py", line 947, in profile_run
File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py", line 887, in _dummy_run
File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/dflash/speculator.py", line 376, in propose
    self.hidden_states[:num_target_tokens].copy_(hidden_states[:num_target_tokens])
RuntimeError: The size of tensor a (16384) must match the size of tensor b (4096) at non-singleton dimension 1
```

`aux_hidden_states` is empty here, so `propose` falls back to the target's final hidden states. For DeepSeek-V4 those are 16384 wide (4 hyper-connection streams × 4096), while the drafter's buffer is 4096 wide. It looks like DeepSeek-V4 doesn't expose aux hidden states for DFlash, similar to what #55682 adds for GLM-5.3-Flash.

**Expected:** DeepSeek-V4-Flash + its DFlash speculator starts. Suggested fixes: pick a draft KV cache dtype the draft's backend supports instead of inheriting `fp8_ds_mla`, and capture the aux hidden states DFlash expects from DeepSeek-V4.

For reference, `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-DSpark` (bundled DSpark drafter) starts fine on the same setup.

Found while testing KV cache grouping for #58638. AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to reproduce and write this up; I reviewed it.

title: [Bug]: DeepSeek V4 buffers long string tool arguments until </parameter>
body:
### Your current environment

This is reproducible in the parser without a model or accelerator.

- Reproduced on vLLM `v0.25.1` (`752a3a504485790a2e8491cacbb35c137339ad34`).
- Confirmed by source inspection on current `main` at `f1178f3a06fa30a0cc282376924210cedad08c44`: `deepseek_v4_config()` still sets `arg_structural_chars=frozenset(">")`, and `_compute_arg_delta()` still skips converter calls when a raw delta does not contain one of those characters.
- Python 3.12.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

DeepSeek V4 tool calls do not incrementally stream the body of a single long string parameter. The stream emits the function name and the opening JSON prefix, then remains silent for the entire parameter body. When the DSML `</parameter>` closing tag arrives, the accumulated body is emitted as one large `delta.tool_calls[0].function.arguments` fragment.

This is the same user-visible failure mode discussed in #43267, but it affects the DeepSeek V4 parser added in #45877 after #43267 was closed. #46351 added schema-aware support for streaming prefix-stable string values in the shared ParserEngine, but the DeepSeek V4 configuration prevents that path from running for ordinary parameter-body deltas.

#### Minimal parser-only reproduction

The following uses no model weights or accelerator:

```python
import json
from unittest.mock import MagicMock

from vllm.entrypoints.openai.chat_completion.protocol import (
    ChatCompletionToolsParam,
    FunctionDefinition,
)
from vllm.tool_parsers.deepseekv4_engine_tool_parser import (
    DeepSeekV4EngineToolParser,
)

tokenizer = MagicMock()
tokenizer.get_vocab.return_value = {}
tool = ChatCompletionToolsParam(
    type="function",
    function=FunctionDefinition(
        name="emit_text",
        parameters={
            "type": "object",
            "properties": {"text": {"type": "string"}},
            "required": ["text"],
        },
    ),
)
request = MagicMock()
request.tools = [tool]
request.tool_choice = "auto"
parser = DeepSeekV4EngineToolParser(tokenizer, tools=[tool])

header = (
    '<｜DSML｜tool_calls>\n'
    '<｜DSML｜invoke name="emit_text">\n'
    '<｜DSML｜parameter name="text" string="true">'
)
body = "A" * 4096
tail = (
    '</｜DSML｜parameter>\n'
    '</｜DSML｜invoke>\n'
    '</｜DSML｜tool_calls>'
)
chunks = [header] + [body[i : i + 32] for i in range(0, len(body), 32)] + [tail]

previous = ""
argument_deltas = []
for index, delta_text in enumerate(chunks):
    current = previous + delta_text
    delta = parser.extract_tool_calls_streaming(
        previous_text=previous,
        current_text=current,
        delta_text=delta_text,
        previous_token_ids=[],
        current_token_ids=[],
        delta_token_ids=[1],
        request=request,
    )
    previous = current
    if delta:
        for tool_call in delta.tool_calls:
            if tool_call.function and tool_call.function.arguments is not None:
                argument_deltas.append((index, tool_call.function.arguments))

print([(index, len(value)) for index, value in argument_deltas])
print("pre-close non-empty deltas:", sum(
    bool(value) for index, value in argument_deltas if index < len(chunks) - 1
))
print("valid reconstruction:", json.loads("".join(
    value for _, value in argument_deltas
)) == {"text": body})
```

Observed output:

```text
[(0, 10), (129, 4104)]
pre-close non-empty deltas: 1
valid reconstruction: True
```

The only pre-close fragment is the JSON prefix `{"text": "`. All 4096 body characters are withheld and emitted with the closing tag.

Expected behavior: multiple non-empty `function.arguments` deltas should contain parameter body text before `</parameter>`, while their concatenation remains valid JSON after the tool call completes.

#### Root cause

`vllm/parser/deepseek_v4.py` configures:

```python
arg_converter=_dsml_arg_converter,
arg_structural_chars=frozenset(">"),
```

`ParserEngine._compute_arg_delta()` then returns early for every body-only delta:

```python
structural = self._arg_structural_chars
if structural is not None and structural.isdisjoint(raw_delta):
    return None
```

The opening parameter tag contains `>`, so the converter emits `{"text": "`. Typical string body deltas contain no `>`, so they are accumulated without conversion. The closing tag contains `>`, which finally triggers conversion of the full accumulated body.

As a diagnostic control, setting `arg_structural_chars=None` for the same parser input produces 130 non-empty argument deltas (maximum 32 characters) before/finally at close, with exact JSON reconstruction. That demonstrates the filtering condition is the immediate cause, although simply removing it may make the regex-based converter repeatedly scan the full accumulated argument and should be evaluated for long-argument complexity.

#### Real endpoint confirmation

A deterministic `stream=true`, `tool_choice="auto"` request to a DeepSeek V4 Flash service produced:

```text
2.433s  function name: emit_text
2.531s  arguments: {"text": "        (10 characters)
12.893s arguments: <entire body>       (861 characters)
12.942s arguments: "}                  (2 characters)
12.992s finish_reason: tool_calls
```

There were no argument-body deltas for 10.36 seconds. The reconstructed arguments were valid JSON. `tool_choice="auto"` is intentional so the request exercises the DeepSeek V4 parser rather than the generic required/named-tool path.

A regression test should specifically assert that a single long schema-typed string parameter emits more than one body delta before `</parameter>`. The existing mixed-parameter incremental test can pass because each subsequent parameter header contains `>` and flushes the preceding value.

title: [Bug]: FlashInfer sampler JIT crashes engine startup when nvcc isn't discoverable (default precompiled/wheel install) — no fallback to native sampler
body:
### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py ```text ============================== System Info ============================== OS : Ubuntu 26.04 LTS (x86_64) GCC version : (Ubuntu 15.2.0-16ubuntu1) 15.2.0 Libc version : glibc-2.43 ============================== PyTorch Info ============================== PyTorch version : 2.11.0+cu130 Is debug build : False CUDA used to build PyTorch : 13.0 ============================== Python Environment ============================== Python version : 3.12.13 (main, Jul 18 2026, 17:02:19) [Clang 22.1.3 ] (64-bit runtime) Python platform : Linux-6.18.33.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2-x86_64-with-glibc2.43 ============================== CUDA / GPU Info ============================== Is CUDA available : True CUDA runtime version : Could not collect GPU models and configuration : GPU 0: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4060 Ti Nvidia driver version : 596.49 ============================== Versions of relevant libraries ============================== [pip3] flashinfer-python==0.6.15.post1 [pip3] nvidia-cuda-nvcc==13.3.73 [pip3] nvidia-cuda-nvrtc==13.0.88 [pip3] nvidia-cuda-runtime==13.0.96 [pip3] torch==2.11.0 [pip3] triton==3.6.0 [pip3] transformers==5.14.1 ============================== vLLM Info ============================== vLLM Version : 0.23.1rc1.dev1392+g910cc8543 (git sha: 910cc8543) vLLM Build Flags: CUDA Archs: Not Set; ROCm: Disabled; XPU: Disabled ============================== Environment Variables ============================== VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0 VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0 PYTORCH_NVML_BASED_CUDA_CHECK=1 ``` (The two `VLLM_*` env vars above are the workarounds I now run with; the crash below reproduces with both unset. collect_env output trimmed for length — full version available on request.)
Install: `VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1 uv pip install --editable .` at commit 910cc8543 on WSL2. **No system CUDA toolkit** — no `/usr/local/cuda`, no nvcc on PATH — which is the normal state for wheel-based installs (and the documented setup for WSL2, which uses the Windows driver via passthrough). ### 🐛 Describe the bug With a default config, the FlashInfer top-k/top-p sampler is auto-selected ("Using FlashInfer for top-p & top-k sampling"), then engine startup crashes when FlashInfer JIT-compiles its sampling module: ```text File ".../site-packages/flashinfer/jit/cpp_ext.py", line 61, in get_cuda_path raise RuntimeError( RuntimeError: Could not find nvcc and default cuda_home='/usr/local/cuda' doesn't exist RuntimeError: Engine core initialization failed. See root cause above. ``` It reproduces in **both** sampler code paths: - **V1 model runner:** during `profile_run` → `_dummy_sampler_run` (`vllm/v1/sample/ops/topk_topp_sampler.py:504` → `flashinfer.sampling.top_k_top_p_sampling_from_logits`) - **V2 model runner:** during `compile_or_warm_up_model` → `warmup_kernels` → `sample_tokens` (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/sample/sampler.py:234` → same call) Minimal repro on any machine without a discoverable toolkit: ```python from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams if __name__ == "__main__": llm = LLM(model="facebook/opt-125m") out = llm.generate(["Hello, my name is"], SamplingParams(max_tokens=20)) print(out[0].outputs[0].text) ``` Workaround: `VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0` — inference then works normally via the native sampler. **Two observations:** 1. **The failure escapes vLLM's existing gate.** `flashinfer_sampler_supported()` (`vllm/v1/sample/ops/topk_topp_sampler.py`) already implements the right policy for unsupported configs: warn once and fall back to native, or raise a clear error if the user explicitly forced `VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=1`. But it only checks platform and compute capability — not whether FlashInfer can actually build or load its kernels. So a default install crashes at engine init with an error pointing at `/usr/local/cuda`, which wheel users have no reason to have. 2. **nvcc is actually present, just undiscoverable.** The wheel install pulls in `nvidia-cuda-nvcc==13.3.73` as a pip package, so a compiler exists inside `site-packages` — but FlashInfer's `get_cuda_path()` only consults `CUDA_HOME` and `/usr/local/cuda`. (Compare #44305, where CUDA_HOME pointed into the pip `nvidia/` tree and nvcc WAS found.) Related but distinct: #44305 (closed; Blackwell, nvcc found but toolkit headers incompatible), #26642 (old FlashInfer 0.4.0). Also mentioned briefly in my comment on #47292. Happy to submit a PR. My preferred direction: extend `flashinfer_sampler_supported()` to verify sampling-kernel availability (prebuilt cubin/jit-cache, or a usable toolkit for JIT — possibly including the pip-installed nvcc per observation 2) using the existing warn-and-fallback / raise-if-forced structure. Open to guidance on whether the pip-nvcc discovery belongs in vLLM or upstream in FlashInfer. **Full tracebacks:**
V1 model runner (default settings) ```text ERROR [core.py:1330] EngineCore failed to start. ERROR [core.py:1330] Traceback (most recent call last): File "vllm/v1/engine/core.py", line 1299, in run_engine_core engine_core = EngineCoreProc(*args, engine_index=dp_rank, **kwargs) File "vllm/v1/engine/core.py", line 136, in __init__ kv_cache_config = self._initialize_kv_caches(vllm_config) File "vllm/v1/engine/core.py", line 286, in _initialize_kv_caches available_gpu_memory = self.model_executor.determine_available_memory() File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py", line 488, in determine_available_memory self.model_runner.profile_run() File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py", line 6430, in profile_run output = self._dummy_sampler_run(last_hidden_states) File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py", line 6210, in _dummy_sampler_run sampler_output = self.sampler( File "vllm/v1/sample/sampler.py", line 286, in sample random_sampled, processed_logprobs = self.topk_topp_sampler( File "vllm/v1/sample/ops/topk_topp_sampler.py", line 174, in forward_cuda return flashinfer_sample(logits.contiguous(), k, p, generators), None File "vllm/v1/sample/ops/topk_topp_sampler.py", line 504, in flashinfer_sample next_token_ids = flashinfer.sampling.top_k_top_p_sampling_from_logits( File "flashinfer/sampling.py", line 1550, in top_k_top_p_sampling_from_logits masked_logits = top_k_mask_logits(logits, top_k) File "flashinfer/sampling.py", line 68, in get_sampling_module module = gen_sampling_module().build_and_load() File "flashinfer/jit/cpp_ext.py", line 61, in get_cuda_path raise RuntimeError( RuntimeError: Could not find nvcc and default cuda_home='/usr/local/cuda' doesn't exist ```
V2 model runner (VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 VLLM_WSL2_ENABLE_PIN_MEMORY=1) ```text ERROR [core.py:1330] EngineCore failed to start. ERROR [core.py:1330] Traceback (most recent call last): File "vllm/v1/engine/core.py", line 324, in _initialize_kv_caches self.model_executor.initialize_from_config(kv_cache_configs) File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py", line 779, in compile_or_warm_up_model warmup_kernels(self.model_runner, self.execute_model, self.sample_tokens) File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu/warmup.py", line 283, in warmup_kernels worker_sample_tokens(grammar_output) File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py", line 1454, in sample_tokens sampler_output, num_sampled, num_rejected = self.sample( File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu/sample/sampler.py", line 234, in sample sampled = flashinfer_sample(processed_logits, top_k, top_p).to(torch.int64) File "vllm/v1/sample/ops/topk_topp_sampler.py", line 504, in flashinfer_sample next_token_ids = flashinfer.sampling.top_k_top_p_sampling_from_logits( File "flashinfer/sampling.py", line 68, in get_sampling_module module = gen_sampling_module().build_and_load() File "flashinfer/jit/cpp_ext.py", line 61, in get_cuda_path raise RuntimeError( RuntimeError: Could not find nvcc and default cuda_home='/usr/local/cuda' doesn't exist ```

title: [Docs] Feedback for `/en/stable/serving/data_parallel_deployment/` load balancing with respect to vllm-router
body:
### 📚 The doc issue

In data parallel deployments, it is not well documented that vllm-router is capable to route requests to specific data-parallel engines within a vllm deployment via `--intra-node-data-parallel-size`.

This can effectively leverage session-affinity routing with data-parallel deployments in the presence of a conversational or agentic workload where a request's context is reused by the same client over and over.

### Suggest a potential alternative/fix

It does not fit well with the current load balancing classification (internal, hybrid, external) because it looks like this is specific to vllm-router, but it would be handy to explicitly mention that it is possible to route requests to specific engines within a single HTTP endpoint and demonstrate it with an example using `vllm-router --intra-node-data-parallel-size N`.

title: [Bug]: v0.30.0 ships transformers 5.17, Pixtral-based models (LightOnOCR, Mistral3) fail with ImportError PixtralRotaryEmbedding
body:
### Your current environment

- `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.30.0` (`sha256:8a69ffad015f138d7170c4ddc429e230a3bc1c1719f67e14324749df200a4b90`), unmodified
- vLLM 0.30.0, transformers 5.17.0 (as shipped in the image), torch 2.13.0+cu130
- 2× NVIDIA H200 NVL, driver 580.178.04

### 🐛 Describe the bug

The official v0.30.0 image ships transformers 5.17.0, but v0.30.0's `pixtral.py` still imports the pre-5.17 name `PixtralRotaryEmbedding` (renamed to `PixtralVisionRotaryEmbedding` in huggingface/transformers#48105). Every model that goes through `pixtral.py` fails at model inspection, so the server never starts. In v0.30.0 that is `lightonocr.py`, `mistral3.py`, `llava.py` and `vision.py`.

`requirements/common.txt` in v0.30.0 only has `transformers >= 5.10.4` with no upper bound, so the same thing happens with a fresh `pip install vllm==0.30.0`.

Minimal repro, no GPU needed:

```bash
docker run --rm --entrypoint python3 vllm/vllm-openai:v0.30.0 \
  -c "import vllm.model_executor.models.pixtral"
```

```
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/vllm/model_executor/models/pixtral.py", line 19, in <module>
    from transformers.models.pixtral.modeling_pixtral import (
ImportError: cannot import name 'PixtralRotaryEmbedding' from 'transformers.models.pixtral.modeling_pixtral' (/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/transformers/models/pixtral/modeling_pixtral.py). Did you mean: 'PixtralVisionRotaryEmbedding'?
```

`vllm serve lightonai/LightOnOCR-2-1B-bbox` then fails with:

```
pydantic_core._pydantic_core.ValidationError: 1 validation error for ModelConfig
  Value error, Model architectures ['LightOnOCRForConditionalGeneration'] failed to be inspected.
```

This is already fixed on `main` by #56108 (merged 2026-09-16, gates the import on `transformers >= 5.17.0.dev0`), but v0.30.0 was cut before that. Could #56108's `pixtral.py` change be backported to a v0.30.1? Alternatively, cap `transformers < 5.17` for the 0.30 line. Our workaround for now is staying on v0.29.0 for LightOnOCR.
