title: [Bug]: Dynamic SD (num_speculative_tokens_per_batch_size) + MTP on V2 runner crashes with ZeroDivisionError in SpeculatorCudaGraphManager._init_candidates
body:
### Your current environment

- vLLM nightly `0.28.1rc1.dev628+g2a02f6efe` (docker `vllm/vllm-openai`), `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`
- 2× NVIDIA GB10 (DGX Spark), TP=2 across two nodes
- Model: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next NVFP4 (`qwen4_exp`), MTP drafter (`mtp_num_hidden_layers: 1`)
- `compilation_config={"mode":0,"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}`, `max_num_seqs=16`

### 🐛 Describe the bug

Enabling Dynamic SD (`num_speculative_tokens_per_batch_size`) with an MTP drafter on the V2 model runner crashes during KV-cache init, before the server starts.

```json
{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":4,"disable_eagle_block_drop":true,
 "num_speculative_tokens_per_batch_size":[[1,4,4],[5,8,3],[9,12,2],[13,16,1]]}
```

The schedule validates fine (`build_dynamic_sd_schedule_lookup` → `[0,4,4,4,4,3,3,3,3,2,2,2,2,1,1,1,1]`). With the static config (`num_speculative_tokens: 3`, no schedule) the same deployment runs normally.

```
File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py", line 712, in initialize_kv_cache
    self.speculator.init_cudagraph_manager(cudagraph_mode)
File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/autoregressive/speculator.py", line 143, in init_cudagraph_manager
    self.decode_cudagraph_manager = SpeculatorCudaGraphManager(
File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu/cudagraph_utils.py", line 186, in __init__
    self._init_candidates()
File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu/cudagraph_utils.py", line 280, in _init_candidates
    rounded_num_tokens = round_up(num_tokens, decode_query_len)
File "vllm/utils/math_utils.py", line 22, in round_up
    return ((x + y - 1) // y) * y
ZeroDivisionError: integer division or modulo by zero
```

**Likely cause.** `SpeculatorCudaGraphManager` is built with `decode_query_len=1` for draft positions > 0. When `uses_dynamic_speculative_decoding()` is true, `_init_candidates` derives per-k query lengths as

```python
num_new_sampled_tokens_per_step = self.decode_query_len - self.vllm_config.num_speculative_tokens
decode_query_lens = {num_spec + num_new_sampled_tokens_per_step for num_spec in dense_schedule[1:]}
```

That is correct for the target model (`decode_query_len = k+1`), but for the drafter it gives `1 − 4 = −3`. The lengths for k=4,3,2,1 then come out as 1, 0, −1, −2, and `round_up(..., 0)` divides by zero. The draft-decode manager should probably skip the dynamic-SD tiers, since each draft step is always 1 token, or compute them from its own query length.

Any schedule that contains a k lower than `num_speculative_tokens` should hit this with an autoregressive (MTP/EAGLE) drafter on the V2 runner.

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] I searched existing issues and didn't find this.

title: [RFC]: Shared JSON Schema structure for structured-output checks and transformations
body:
This RFC describes the target design. Illustrative interfaces below are not implemented APIs.

## Motivation

The core problem is that vLLM's pre-compilation JSON Schema checks and configuration-driven transformations lack a shared schema-aware structural model. Several recurse through arbitrary dictionaries and lists, so they can mistake property names or literal JSON values for schema keywords, or treat an unreferenced `$defs` entry as an active constraint. Some type-specific checks also require an explicit `type`, although JSON Schema assertions can apply without one. Patching these cases one walker at a time is whack-a-mole: the next keyword or consumer can repeat the same mistake. These consumers need one shared account of schema boundaries, reference reachability, and type applicability.

Concrete motivating cases include:

- A property named `patternProperties`, or the same key inside `const`, incorrectly triggers the [Guidance feature gate](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/fa94450b743766d466021a40e5b5f5f5746c92b9/vllm/v1/structured_output/backend_guidance.py#L50-L73) ([bug #58694](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/58694)).
- With `disable_additional_properties=True`, the [Guidance transformation](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/fa94450b743766d466021a40e5b5f5f5746c92b9/vllm/v1/structured_output/backend_guidance.py#L37-L48) inserts `additionalProperties: false` into an object inside `const`, changing the allowed value ([bug #58695](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/58695)).
- String assertions can bypass xgrammar checks when `type` is omitted; [#57550](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/57550) tracks this bug, and open [#57592](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57592) proposes a scoped fix with related traversal changes.
- An unreferenced `$defs` entry can change backend selection even though it does not constrain the generated value (also reproduced in [bug #58694](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/58694)).

For a concrete Guidance case, this valid schema has a property **named** `patternProperties`; it has no `patternProperties` keyword:

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "patternProperties": {"type": "string"},
    "n": {"type": "number", "multipleOf": 3}
  },
  "required": ["patternProperties", "n"],
  "additionalProperties": false
}
```

On upstream `main` at `fa94450b74` (September 25, 2026), the Guidance gate reports it unsupported and `auto` selects Outlines. The original schema rejects `{"patternProperties":"x","n":7}`, while the resulting Outlines regex accepts it; the Guidance matcher rejects it.

Separately, with `disable_additional_properties=True`, Guidance inserts `additionalProperties: false` into a literal object under `const` or `enum` when that object has a `properties` member. Its matcher then accepts the changed literal, which the original schema rejects. These are local request-validation and matcher/regex reproductions, without model generation.

The proposal is a shared **schema-document layer** used by checks and transformations. Backend grammar compilers remain responsible for producing grammars.

## Proposed Change

The target is a shared schema document used by backend checks and configuration transformations before grammar compilation. The [fork-only Draft demo PR](https://github.com/equiluxe/vllm/pull/1) is a proof of concept that makes the design discussable through a code diff. It does not propose that diff as the fix and is marked **Do Not Merge**. The contract below defines the intended behavior, including requirements the prototype does not implement.

The shared document has these contracts. Each code excerpt is from the [fork-only Draft demo PR](https://github.com/equiluxe/vllm/pull/1) at commit `a83751a1` and illustrates only the stated part of the target design.

#### Schema/data boundary

`properties` is a name-to-schema map, `allOf` is a list of schemas, and `additionalProperties` holds a schema. `const`, `enum`, and `default` hold ordinary JSON values. Structural traversal visits nodes inside recognized schema-bearing keywords; it does not treat a property named `patternProperties` or an object inside `const` as a schema.

Keyword roles depend on the dialect of each schema resource, not on a single universal keyword table. The document obtains that dialect from `$schema` or a documented caller default; an embedded `$id` resource may declare another dialect. Ordinary unknown fields remain opaque and preserved. If a declared dialect requires a vocabulary this layer cannot interpret, capability analysis reports incomplete.

The demo recurses into recognized schema-bearing keywords and stores other values without parsing them as schemas. [Code](https://github.com/equiluxe/vllm/blob/a83751a1a89082ffe11642918405fe6a66a7d833/vllm/v1/structured_output/schema_document.py#L200-L210):

```python
elif keyword in _SCHEMA_SINGLE:
    subschemas[keyword] = _parse_node(value)
else:
    values[keyword] = _copy_value(value)
```

The demo uses a fixed `2020-12` keyword table and does not inspect `$schema`. It also treats legacy `additionalItems` as schema-bearing under `2020-12`, although [that dialect replaced it with `items`](https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/json-schema-core#section-10.3.1.2) and treats it as an unknown keyword; dialect-specific roles remain target work.

#### Lossless representation

Boolean schemas and generic schema objects preserve the original child-container shapes. There is no second independently mutable raw tree. Without a transformation, `SchemaDocument.parse(schema, dialect).export() == schema` for JSON-valued inputs. Parsing does not mutate caller input or silently treat malformed structural values as absent. A present but invalid keyword value is not treated as an omitted keyword by derived analysis, even though structural parsing is separate from full schema-validity checking. Transformations use immutable nodes or controlled edits that keep keyword order, source locations/indexes, and derived caches consistent. Existing accepted dialect and legacy forms, including tuple-valued `items`, need an explicit normalization or round-trip contract.

The demo exports boolean nodes directly and reconstructs object keywords in their original order. [Code](https://github.com/equiluxe/vllm/blob/a83751a1a89082ffe11642918405fe6a66a7d833/vllm/v1/structured_output/schema_document.py#L213-L230):

```python
if isinstance(node, BoolSchema):
    return node.value
exported: dict[str, Any] = {}
for keyword in node.order:
    if keyword in node.values:
        exported[keyword] = _copy_value(node.values[keyword])
```

This demonstrates the representation for the prototype's accepted forms; compatibility across existing dialects and legacy forms has not been established. The demo exposes mutable keyword dictionaries, so edits outside its narrow transformation method can leave export order or derived caches stale.

#### Two traversals

`walk_all_schema_nodes()` includes definitions and schema-valued annotations for structural inspection and controlled whole-document edits. `walk_potential_constraints()` starts at the root and follows only edges that may affect the generated instance under the relevant dialect, plus resolved references. Schema-bearing does not imply instance-applicable: Draft 2020-12 [`contentSchema`](https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/json-schema-validation#section-8.5) is a content annotation by default, and [`then`/`else`](https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/json-schema-core#section-10.2.2) have no effect without `if` in the same schema object. An unused `$defs` schema is preserved without changing semantic capability checks. Reachability is conservative, not a satisfiability proof.

References remain edges, with cycle tracking and explicit coverage for local pointers, `$id` scopes, and anchors. Dialect-specific reference rules, including [Draft-07's treatment of `$ref` siblings](https://json-schema.org/draft-07/json-schema-core#section-8.3), govern which edges apply. Unresolved or unsupported cases are reported as incomplete; remote schemas are not fetched automatically. Source locations support diagnostics such as `#/properties/code`; the full pointer index can be built only when references or diagnostics require it.

The demo's capability walk skips unused definitions, follows local references, and tracks visited nodes. [Code](https://github.com/equiluxe/vllm/blob/a83751a1a89082ffe11642918405fe6a66a7d833/vllm/v1/structured_output/schema_document.py#L349-L367):

```python
visited.add(id(node))
yield node
if isinstance(node, GeneralSchema):
    _push_children(pending, node, include_definitions=False)
    target = self._local_reference(node)
    if target is not None:
        pending.append(self.nodes[target])
```

The demo resolves only root-local JSON Pointers; `$id` scopes, anchors, and remote references remain incomplete. It also follows `contentSchema` and orphan `then`/`else` as if they could constrain the generated value; the target walk must distinguish these edges. A pointer-yielding walk exists, but the backend gates do not yet return source locations.

#### Derived assertions

The document keeps explicit `type` separate from type-specific assertions. A schema such as `{"pattern": "^[a-z]+$", "maxLength": 3}` still constrains string instances while allowing non-strings. A backend checks string features unless string is definitely excluded; it does not infer or insert `type: string`. One schema node owns the data and exposes numeric, string, array, and object behavior; these do not require four separately allocated views or another mutable tree. Scalar, list-valued, and omitted types use the same applicability rules. Backend profiles own their capability rules; no general entailment solver is required.

In the demo, omitted `type` leaves string instances possible, so the [Xgrammar check](https://github.com/equiluxe/vllm/blob/a83751a1a89082ffe11642918405fe6a66a7d833/vllm/v1/structured_output/backend_xgrammar.py#L265-L281) can inspect string-specific keywords without inserting a type. [Code](https://github.com/equiluxe/vllm/blob/a83751a1a89082ffe11642918405fe6a66a7d833/vllm/v1/structured_output/schema_document.py#L68-L71):

```python
def may_be_string(self) -> bool:
    types = self._explicit_types
    return types is None or "string" in types
```

The demo currently treats an explicit invalid `"type": null` as if `type` were omitted. The target distinguishes absence from an invalid value and reports invalidity or incomplete analysis under its validation policy.

#### Safe preparation

Transformations edit eligible schema nodes in a new document; they never edit literal JSON values such as `{"const": {"properties": {"status": "ok"}}}`. Guidance's `disable_additional_properties=True` may add `additionalProperties: false` to an object schema, but this is a configuration-driven semantic rewrite, not necessarily a monotone restriction. For example, `{"not":{"properties":{"x":{"const":1}}}}` rejects `{"x":1,"extra":2}`; adding `additionalProperties: false` inside `not` makes that value valid. `if` and `oneOf` also have non-monotone cases. Which contexts the configuration rewrites is an explicit compatibility decision, not something structural traversal decides automatically.

Each candidate backend starts from the unmodified parsed document. Conceptually, it prepares its own copy, checks that prepared schema and configuration, and, if selected, compiles that same prepared schema and configuration.

The demo copies the document and visits only `GeneralSchema` nodes, including definitions; literal JSON inside `const` and `enum` remains opaque. [Code](https://github.com/equiluxe/vllm/blob/a83751a1a89082ffe11642918405fe6a66a7d833/vllm/v1/structured_output/schema_document.py#L391-L410):

```python
prepared = SchemaDocument(deepcopy(self.root), self.dialect)
pending = [prepared.root]
nodes: list[GeneralSchema] = []
while pending:
    node = pending.pop()
    if isinstance(node, GeneralSchema):
        nodes.append(node)
        _push_children(pending, node, include_definitions=True)
```

[Guidance applies](https://github.com/equiluxe/vllm/blob/a83751a1a89082ffe11642918405fe6a66a7d833/vllm/v1/structured_output/backend_guidance.py#L62-L71) its `additionalProperties` change to these nodes. The demo does not select eligible contexts within that set, so `not`, `if`, and schema-valued annotations can also be rewritten. Candidate preparation, capability checks, and actual compilation do not yet share one end-to-end prepared result.

#### Routing boundary

A check reports a reason, schema location, backend, and one of **known unsupported**, **analysis incomplete**, or **no known issue**. A definite unsupported feature remains reportable even if another branch is incomplete; otherwise incomplete analysis must not become **no known issue**. The last state is not proof of complete backend support.

Routing handles incomplete analysis explicitly and preserves existing validation/fallback behavior unless a separate policy change is reviewed. Ordinary JSON, tool parameters, and structural-tag inner schemas use this schema path while retaining their outer protocol handling. Parsing and analysis run during preparation/compilation, outside the per-token masking path.

The demo's feature gate still returns a Boolean, so this contract is not implemented. [Code](https://github.com/equiluxe/vllm/blob/a83751a1a89082ffe11642918405fe6a66a7d833/vllm/v1/structured_output/backend_guidance.py#L41-L51):

```python
document = SchemaDocument.parse(schema)
return any(
    isinstance(node, GeneralSchema) and node.pattern_properties is not None
    for node in document.walk_potential_constraint_nodes()
)
```

When traversal reaches an unsupported reference form, it raises `IncompleteSchemaAnalysis`; routing does not yet handle a distinct incomplete result or return a reason and location. `False` means no known issue in this gate, not proof of backend support. Tool and structural-tag paths are also outside this demo.

Backend grammar compilation, runtime matcher state, a full instance validator, exact satisfiability/type inference, and a new default fallback order are outside this proposal. Benchmark preparation against today's path on representative schemas: parsing, traversal, candidate-specific rewrites, export, and allocations, especially when multiple backend candidates inspect one schema. Measure that separately from grammar compilation before deciding whether caching is useful.

### Adoption

Adoption does not require a complete JSON Schema parser up front. Start with the smallest schema-aware reader needed by one consumer: recognize the schema-bearing positions and application edges it uses, leave the caller's schema untouched, and report **analysis incomplete** for dialects, references, or structures it cannot safely analyze. Extend coverage only as consumers need it. Each small, consumer-backed PR should state the behavior it changes or preserves, protect unrelated backend routing and accepted schema forms, and include targeted regressions. Independent bug fixes can be reviewed while the shared interface is discussed. The exact order, dependencies, and code split belong in those PRs; this RFC defines the shared end state and its compatibility boundaries.

For example, first compare a narrow Guidance check against the existing check **in tests only**, so serving still uses the old decision. Test unchanged cases for equivalence and give each intended behavior change its own regression. A later PR can switch that one consumer while preserving the old decision whenever analysis is incomplete (illustrative pseudocode, not a proposed API):

```python
# First PR: compare only schemas expected to keep the current decision.
for unchanged_schema in unchanged_cases:
    analysis = analyze_guidance_subset(unchanged_schema)
    if analysis.status != ANALYSIS_INCOMPLETE:
        assert (analysis.status == KNOWN_UNSUPPORTED) == legacy_guidance_gate(
            unchanged_schema
        )

# Later PR: migrate one consumer; leave global routing policy unchanged.
analysis = analyze_guidance_subset(schema)
if analysis.status == ANALYSIS_INCOMPLETE:
    return legacy_guidance_gate(schema)
return analysis.status == KNOWN_UNSUPPORTED
```

An incomplete result never means "supported"; it preserves the existing decision until that schema form is covered. This keeps each structural addition reviewable without changing every backend, schema entry point, or fallback rule at once.

### Test contracts and real backend behavior

Use an independent validator on the **original schema**, not our AST, as the semantic oracle. For a supported test case with no configuration-driven schema rewrite:

```python
original = deepcopy(schema)
document = SchemaDocument.parse(schema, dialect=DRAFT_2020_12)
assert document.export() == original
assert schema == original

Draft202012Validator.check_schema(original)
oracle = Draft202012Validator(original)  # independent of our parser
matcher = compile_via_vllm(document, backend, config=no_schema_rewrite_config)
for value in ["abc", "abcd", "ABC", 123, None]:
    expected = oracle.is_valid(value)
    assert accepts_complete_json(matcher, value) == expected
```

`accepts_complete_json` creates fresh matcher state and checks the whole serialized value **and legal termination/EOS**, not just prefix acceptance. This is test pseudocode, not a production validation layer.

The test plan includes:

- Structural round trips and non-mutation: boolean schemas, property names, opaque data, unknown fields, nested schemas, escaped pointers, and cycles. Dialect cases include 2020-12 `additionalItems`, Draft-07/2020-12 `$ref` sibling behavior, and invalid explicit keyword values distinct from omission.
- Constraint traversal: unused definitions, schema-valued content annotations, orphan `then`/`else`, active conditional branches, and referenced definitions.
- Curated cases from the [JSON Schema Test Suite](https://github.com/json-schema-org/JSON-Schema-Test-Suite), targeted positive/negative regressions, and bounded generated instances. Pin dialect, backend versions, serialization policy, and `format` assertion behavior; [python-jsonschema does not enforce formats by default](https://python-jsonschema.readthedocs.io/en/stable/validate/).
- Separate transformation contracts: equivalence for lossless operations; independently specified acceptance and rejection effects for configuration-driven rewrites, including preservation of literal values and non-monotone `not`/`if`/`oneOf` contexts.
- Integration checks for explicit/automatic backends, actual routing and compilation, and supported JSON/tool/tag entry points. Output-affecting fixes also need model smoke tests; length-truncated output is not a successful schema-valid generation.

Unsupported cases should test diagnostics and routing, not demand universal backend acceptance. Differential tests increase confidence but do not prove correctness for arbitrary schemas, and compilation success alone does not prove that all assertions are enforced.

### Alternatives and tradeoffs

- **Only share a walker:** sufficient for read-only checks, but transformations and export also need a common structure contract. A walker remains a reasonable alternative if it preserves the same schema/data boundary and offers a safe transformation interface.
- **Rely only on backend compilation:** avoids duplicated checks, but cannot address vLLM's own data traversal/transformation bugs or compilers that warn and ignore constraints. Prefer reliable backend-native diagnostics wherever available.
- **Build a complete semantic AST:** more uniform in theory, but expands review scope and duplicates backend work. General/boolean nodes with derived behavior for actual consumers cover the proposed contract. Evaluate existing dialect/reference utilities before implementing a new resolver.

The main costs are another representation, dialect/reference maintenance, and preparation overhead. The preparation benchmark above makes these costs visible alongside routing and correctness changes.

### Feedback requested

1. Is a structural document/AST justified by the check **and transformation** use cases, or would a schema-aware visitor with a safe transformation interface be a better shared contract?
2. Which dialect/legacy forms and reference behaviors must this layer support? How should routing handle incomplete analysis when backend-native validation cannot cover it?
3. Which capability rules belong in vLLM, and which should be replaced by backend-native diagnostics?
4. Which schema contexts should `disable_additional_properties` rewrite, given that a rewrite below `not`, `if`, or `oneOf` can admit values the original schema rejects?

## Feedback Period

September 25 through October 2, 2026 (at least one week). Discussion can continue until the core scope questions have received maintainer feedback.

## CC List

Structured-output maintainers and authors of overlapping changes are invited to comment. No one is explicitly mentioned in this issue.

## Any Other Things

- [#48416](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48416) established scalar/list type handling. Preserve that behavior and its tests when extracting shared analysis.
- [#57592](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57592) overlaps omitted-type handling, schema-aware traversal, and local references; coordinate and reuse its work rather than submit a competing fix. [#57594](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57594) updates a backend capability gate; that remains backend policy, not parser behavior. Recheck overlapping work before each implementation PR.
- xgrammar already has an internal schema parser ([v0.2.7 source](https://github.com/mlc-ai/xgrammar/blob/v0.2.7/cpp/json_schema_converter.cc)). This proposal does not replace it. Prefer upstream diagnostics for unsupported or dropped constraints, and remove vLLM compatibility rules when a supported dependency provides a tested replacement. That upstream work need not block vLLM-local structural fixes.

AI assistance: this RFC was prepared with OpenAI Codex. The pinned local reproductions above are reported as such; no production AST implementation is claimed.

title: [Feature/Design]: UVA weight offload on quantized MoE — pin_memory() power-of-two rounding wastes ~35% host RAM, and MXFP4 process_weights_after_loading silently un-offloads layers via replace_parameter
body:
## Summary

Two independent host-memory problems make `--offload-backend uva` on quantized MoE checkpoints fail at scales where the arithmetic says they should fit. Both were hit bringing up `XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.6-Pro-RL` (1.02T, MXFP4 experts, 527 GiB on disk) on a single DGX Station GB300 (250 GiB HBM visible, 494 GiB Grace host RAM, coherent C2C). Both have working local patches; I'm opening this as a design question rather than a PR because the right fix touches `offloader/uva.py` and the quantization `process_weights_after_loading` contract, and maintainers should pick the shape.

Image: `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-d05da62e` (0.29.1rc1.dev422). Both code paths are unchanged on `main` as of today (`uva.py` L115 `cpu_data.pin_memory()`; `mxfp4.py` L358–361 `replace_parameter`).

## Problem 1: `pin_memory()` rounds every offloaded tensor up to a power of two

`UVAOffloader.wrap_modules` pins each offloaded parameter with `torch.Tensor.pin_memory()`, which goes through the CachingHostAllocator and rounds each allocation to the next power of two. For MiMo-Pro's per-layer expert tensors: `w13_weight` is 4.5 GiB → 8 GiB pinned, `w2_weight` 2.25 GiB → 4 GiB. Requesting `--cpu-offload-gb 305` consumed ~504 GiB of host memory and the kernel OOM-killed the EngineCore during load (host 494 GiB). Measured with a small probe that pins tensors of the real shapes and reads `Mlocked`/`Shmem` from `/proc/meminfo` before and after.

That's a ~33–45% host-RAM tax on exactly the workload UVA offload exists for, and it's invisible: the log reports "Total CPU offloaded parameters: 305 GiB" while the host holds far more.

**Local fix that works:** register the existing contiguous CPU tensor in place with `cudaHostRegister(ptr, nbytes, cudaHostRegisterPortable)` via ctypes (exact size), and keep a reference so it's never unregistered. With that, 321.75 GiB offloaded pins 321.75 GiB; the full model loads with 126 GiB host free. Read bandwidth through the resulting CUDA view was 336 GB/s vs 355 GB/s for the `pin_memory()` path on this box — a wash.

**Design question:** is an in-place `cudaHostRegister` path acceptable in `uva.py` (env-gated, or automatic above some size threshold), or would you rather expose a way to allocate exact-size pinned memory (e.g. `cudaHostAlloc` + `torch.from_blob`) so the caching allocator isn't involved at all? I can send either as a PR.

## Problem 2: `Mxfp4MoEMethod.process_weights_after_loading` un-offloads every layer via `replace_parameter`

On the Marlin/TRT-LLM MXFP4 path, `process_weights_after_loading` shuffles/re-packs the expert weights and installs the result with `replace_parameter(layer, "w13_weight", w13)` (and w2, and both scale tensors). `replace_parameter` registers the new tensor as a fresh `nn.Parameter`. The new tensor lives wherever the shuffle produced it (HBM), so the UVA view the offloader installed is dropped and the layer silently comes back onto the GPU: +7.17 GiB HBM per MoE layer on MiMo-Pro. With 46 of 69 MoE layers offloaded the box runs out of HBM after a handful of layers — the failure is a CUDA OOM inside `process_weights_after_loading`, nowhere near the offloader, so it's hard to attribute.

**Local fix that works:** when the existing parameter carries the offloader's `_vllm_is_uva_offloaded` marker and the new tensor has the same byte size, byte-copy the new contents into the existing pinned storage through a `uint8` view and re-view it to the new dtype/shape, preserving the UVA view; fall back to `replace_parameter` (with a warning) if the size changed. Verified: 5/5 greedy prompts token-exact between offloaded and non-offloaded runs of the same weights (8- and 16-layer truncations), and the full model serves correctly.

**Design question:** should `replace_parameter` itself become offload-aware (check the marker, copy in place), so every quant method benefits, or should quant methods that re-pack weights call a new helper? The former is one function; the latter is a per-backend audit (`mxfp4.py` is the one I hit; `fp8.py`, `nvfp4`, `compressed_tensors` likely have the same shape).

## Repro

```
vllm serve XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.6-Pro-RL --trust-remote-code --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
  --moe-backend marlin \
  --offload-backend uva --cpu-offload-gb 320 \
  --cpu-offload-params routed_experts.w13_weight routed_experts.w2_weight \
  --max-model-len 262144 --max-num-seqs 8 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.96
```
Problem 1 shows as a host OOM-kill during load on a 494 GiB host; problem 2 shows as `torch.OutOfMemoryError` in `Mxfp4MoEMethod.process_weights_after_loading` once problem 1 is worked around. With both local patches this serves at 30 tok/s C1 / 56 tok/s aggregate at C8.

Write-up with per-boot receipts: https://al-engr.com/gb300-mimo-v26-pro-testing.html. Happy to send PRs once there's a preferred shape, and to test on this hardware.

title: [Bug]: cutlass_scaled_mm_supports_block_fp8 excludes SM89 (Ada Lovelace) despite native FP8 tensor core support
body:
### Your current environment

**Environment:**
- GPU: NVIDIA RTX 6000 Ada Generation (SM 8.9)
- vLLM: 0.29.0
- CUDA: 13.4
- Model: Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 (block-quantized FP8, 128×128 blocks)

### 🐛 Describe the bug

**Description:**
cutlass_block_fp8_supported() returns False on Ada Lovelace (SM89), causing block-quantized FP8 checkpoints to fall through the kernel priority list in _POSSIBLE_FP8_BLOCK_KERNELS all the way to MarlinFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel — bypassing CUTLASS entirely, even though:

Non-block FP8 CUTLASS is supported on this card: cutlass_fp8_supported() == True
Ada Lovelace has native FP8 tensor core hardware, and vLLM's own docs state FP8 W8A8 is officially supported on "Hopper and Ada Lovelace" (https://docs.vllm.ai/en/stable/features/quantization/fp8/)

Bisecting ops.cutlass_scaled_mm_supports_block_fp8() directly shows a hard floor at SM90:
- 80 -> False
- 86 -> False
- 89 -> False
- 90 -> True
- 100 -> True

**Question:** Is this a genuine CUTLASS-library-level limitation (e.g. block-scaled grouped GEMM requiring Hopper-specific TMA multicast at the collective-builder level, similar to the SM_120/SM_121 CUTLASS MoE gap in #43507), or is SM89 support for block-scaled CUTLASS GEMM simply not yet wired up in vLLM's compiled extension?

If it's the latter, this is a meaningful gap for anyone running block-quantized FP8 checkpoints (increasingly common — DeepSeek-style 128×128 block scales) on Ada workstation cards (RTX 6000 Ada, L40S, RTX 4090), since it silently falls back to Marlin's weight-only dequant path rather than using the card's native FP8 compute.

**Repro:**
```
from vllm import _custom_ops as ops
for cap in [80, 86, 89, 90, 100]:
    print(cap, ops.cutlass_scaled_mm_supports_block_fp8(cap))
```


### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [RFC]: Request level text and derender output on `/inference/v1/generate`
body:
### Motivation.

The disaggregated serving path in vLLM is render → generate → derender. `/render` turns an OpenAI request into a `GenerateRequest` (#36166). `/inference/v1/generate` runs it on the GPU tier and returns token IDs (#22817, #24261).
`/v1/chat/completions/derender` and `/v1/completions/derender` turn the result back into an OpenAI response (#42729).
This works well for batch and RL traffic where the caller already holds the complete `GenerateResponse`.

Latency sensitive interactive traffic in prefill/decode (P/D) deployments is a poor fit. Streaming derender (#47161) is a stateless per chunk translator, so every SSE chunk from generate costs the client another HTTP round trip:

- One `POST` per chunk with the client echoing `stream_state` back on each call.
- On the parsing path the full `chat_request` is re-sent with every chunk.
- Parser state is rebuilt by replaying all output tokens each chunk. #50550 documents this as O(n³) character work over a generation and defers caching it.

All of this lands on the TPOT critical path and for parsed output the cost grows with response length. A benchmark
of the streaming derender PRs measured it (1×A100-40G, Qwen3-8B, hermes + qwen3 parsers, main plus #50550, https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/56851#issuecomment-5685698033). At matched load, detokenize and parse on the derender tier cost ~9× the in-process CPU, and E2E p50 rose 15% on multi-thousand-token reasoning outputs. Tokens-in / text-out in a single call already works on the main server (`/v1/completions` accepts token IDs in `prompt`). The gap is specific to deployments whose wire format is `GenerateRequest`.

**Tokenizer availability is per pool. Detokenization is already per request.** Only one of these is a launch time decision:

| | Granularity | Where it's decided today |
|---|---|---|
| Tokenizer loaded | per pool, at launch | `--tokens-only` sets `skip_tokenizer_init` |
| Detokenize this request | per request | `SamplingParams.detokenize`, default `True`. `GenerateRequest.sampling_params` is a full `SamplingParams`, so it's on the wire today. |

The only thing that makes detokenization look launch level is `--tokens-only` overriding the request value. A generate server launched with `--enable-scale-out` and without `--tokens-only` already runs a `FastIncrementalDetokenizer` for every request. The handler then builds the response from `output.token_ids` only and throws `output.text` away.

**P/D makes request level the natural grain:**

- **Only the terminal leg's output reaches the client.** Proxies run the prefill leg with `max_tokens=1` and keep only `kv_transfer_params`. Decode recomputes the last prompt token to sample the first output token itself.
- **Decode already has everything detokenization needs.** `GenerateRequest.token_ids` carries the full prompt and the detokenizer primes its `DecodeStream` from it. No detokenizer state crosses the P→D boundary.
- **State lives with the live request.** `RequestState` owns the detokenizer and is popped on finish and on abort/disconnect. There's no session registry or eviction. That's the property #47161 couldn't get on the stateless derender tier which has no live request to hang state on.
- **No new pool flavor.** P/D fleets already run prefill and decode pools with different launch configs. Prefill pools stay `--tokens-only`. Decode pools load a tokenizer.

This also continues #22817's original design, which says *"We can make `Detokenization` step optional in the `AsyncLLM`"* and sketches a service mapping `GenerateRequest` → `ChatCompletionResponse`.

### Proposed Change.

#### 1. A request-level `output_mode` field

Add a top level field to `GenerateRequest`:

```python
output_mode: Literal["tokens", "text", "derender"] = "tokens"
```

It's a new field rather than a reuse of `sampling_params.detokenize`. That field defaults to `True`, so keying response content off it would change every existing response on tokenizer loaded servers. It's also an engine field and response shape is a serving concern.

| Level | Response adds | Equivalent today | Server needs |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tokens` (default) | nothing, unchanged behavior | `/inference/v1/generate` | nothing |
| `text` | detokenized `text`, resolved logprob tokens | `/v1/completions/derender` | tokenizer |
| `derender` | `content`, `reasoning`, `tool_calls` | `/v1/chat/completions/derender` | tokenizer, parser config, per request parser context |

#### 2. Response shape (proposed, see open question 1)

One response class per level with `GenerateResponse` as a union discriminated on `output_mode` (open question 1, suggested by @DarkLight1337):

```python
class GenerateTokensResponse(GenerateResponseBase):
    output_mode: Literal["tokens"] = "tokens"
    choices: list[GenerateTokensChoice]

class GenerateTextResponse(GenerateResponseBase):
    output_mode: Literal["text"]
    choices: list[GenerateTextChoice]

class GenerateDerenderResponse(GenerateResponseBase):
    output_mode: Literal["derender"]
    choices: list[GenerateDerenderChoice]

GenerateResponse = Annotated[
    Annotated[GenerateTokensResponse, Tag("tokens")]
    | Annotated[GenerateTextResponse, Tag("text")]
    | Annotated[GenerateDerenderResponse, Tag("derender")],
    Discriminator(output_mode_or_tokens),  # missing tag -> "tokens"
]
```

The choices follow the same pattern:

| Level | Choice adds | Stream choice adds | `logprobs` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tokens` | nothing | nothing | token ID form (#57574) |
| `text` | `text: str` | `text: str` (delta) | resolved token strings (section 5) |
| `derender` | `message: ChatMessage` | `delta: DeltaMessage` | resolved token strings (section 5) |

- **Shared fields stay in the base classes.** `GenerateResponseBase` holds `request_id`, `usage`, `prompt_token_ids`, `mm_placeholders`, `metrics`, `kv_transfer_params` and `ec_transfer_params`. The choice base holds `index`, `finish_reason`, `token_ids`, `routed_experts` and `sampling_mask`. The stream response and stream choices split the same way.
- **The response echoes `output_mode`.** It's what the union discriminates on and it makes every response and stream chunk self-describing. For existing clients this is one new field on `tokens` responses and nothing else changes.
- **A missing `output_mode` means `tokens`.** `GenerateResponse` is also parsed as input by `/derender` (`DerenderChatRequest.generate_response`) and existing clients don't send the field. A plain discriminated union rejects a missing tag, so the discriminator is a callable that falls back to `"tokens"`. The trade-off is that the OpenAPI schema shows a `oneOf` without a discriminator mapping.
- **Mode-specific fields are required, not optional.** `text` is `str` on a text choice and `message` is `ChatMessage` on a derender choice, so callers don't need `None` checks. It also removes the need to exclude unset `text` / `message` / `delta` fields by hand, since the `tokens` classes don't have them.
- **`logprobs` is typed per level.** That answers the question of `choice.logprobs` changing type with `output_mode`. Each level declares its own type.
- **`derender` doesn't carry the raw `text`** which matches `/derender`. `message` / `delta` are the same types `/derender` and `/v1/chat/completions` emit, so the parity check compares field for field.
- **Python code that constructs `GenerateResponse` moves to `GenerateTokensResponse`** because `GenerateResponse` becomes a type alias rather than a class.

Example decode-leg request and stream chunk:

```json
{"token_ids": [151644, 872, ...], "sampling_params": {"max_tokens": 512},
 "stream": true, "output_mode": "text", "kv_transfer_params": {...}}
```

```json
{"request_id": "...", "output_mode": "text",
 "choices": [{"index": 0, "token_ids": [9707], "text": " Hello"}]}
```
#### 3. Parser context for the `derender` level (proposed, see open question 2)

Parsers are built per request from context `GenerateRequest` doesn't carry today: `tools`, `tool_choice`, `chat_template_kwargs`. Batch `/derender` solves this by taking the post `adjust_request`
`ChatCompletionRequest`. The proposal mirrors it:

```python
chat_request: ChatCompletionRequest | None = None  # used only when output_mode="derender"
```

- It's sent once per request, not once per chunk as with streaming derender.
- It reuses the batch derender path (`OnlineDerenderer.derender_chat`) and its parity tests with stop string handling added (section 9). That path runs on the renderer's executor which has `renderer_num_workers` threads, default `1`. It runs once per request and decode pools do no prompt tokenization, so contention is low but the pool size caps concurrent `derender` calls.
- Without `chat_request`, a server with a reasoning or tool parser configured returns **400** (section 6). Batch `/derender` falls back to plain detokenization instead which can mix reasoning or tool call markup into `message.content`. Streaming derender already fails closed for parser configured models. Clients that want plain text use `text`. On a server with no parser, `derender` without `chat_request` puts the plain text in `message.content`.

#### 4. Streaming

- **`text`**: `text` carries each chunk's delta from the request's existing incremental detokenizer (`RequestOutputKind.DELTA`). No extra state.
- **`derender`**: one `Parser` per choice, created when the request starts and kept for its lifetime, the same way `/v1/chat/completions` streams today. There's no replay, no `stream_state` and no per chunk `chat_request`.
- **End of stream**: at `text` and `derender` levels, the stream emits a chunk whenever the engine output carries new text or a `finish_reason`, even with no new token IDs. That covers the final output the engine produces on `/abort_requests` which has no token IDs but can flush text held back for stop string matching. The generate stream skips outputs with no new token IDs today (on `main`, #53187 only keeps them while prompt metadata is pending), so `tokens` streams already drop a finish only chunk. #47933 (open) fixes that for `tokens` by emitting the terminal chunk when `finish_reason` is set. Phase 1 builds on it and also emits chunks that carry only new text.

#### 5. Logprobs

At `text` and `derender` levels, logprob entries carry decoded token strings and `bytes`, as `/derender` produces, instead of the `token_id:N` placeholders generate emits today. The tokens level shape follows #57574.

Dense logprobs are the expensive case. At `top_logprobs=20` the benchmark measured 355 µs per logprob-bearing token and 0.83 of a frontend core within 1.2× of the GPU's token rate. On a tokenizer loaded server that cost is already paid at the `tokens` level: `LogprobsProcessor` decodes every top-k token whenever `sampling_params.detokenize` is true and generate then discards the strings. Clients that want wide logprobs off the decode host send `output_mode="tokens"` with `detokenize: false` (which rules out `stop` strings) or use a `--tokens-only` pool. The Phase 1 docs should say so.

#### 6. Validation (fail loud)

- `output_mode != "tokens"` on a server without a tokenizer → **400**. Today's no-op detokenizer returns `""`, so a naive implementation would return empty text with a 200 for any request routed to a `--tokens-only` pool.
- `output_mode != "tokens"` with `sampling_params.detokenize` explicitly `false` → **400**.
- `chat_request` set without `output_mode="derender"` → **400**, rather than silently ignoring it.
- `output_mode="derender"` without `chat_request` on a server with a reasoning or tool parser configured → **400**, rather than falling back to plain text that may contain reasoning or tool call markup.

**Rollout note:** `GenerateRequest` is a plain pydantic `BaseModel`, so servers without this change ignore `output_mode` and return tokens only with a 200. Clients should check that `output_mode` in the response matches the request. Older servers don't return it.

#### 7. Role agnostic P/D usage

The field has no behavior tied to pod role or `kv_transfer_params`. The same decode pod may serve some requests decode only and others after a remote prefill, so role keyed behavior would differ across those paths. Orchestrators set `output_mode` and `chat_request` on the terminal leg only. If they reach a tokenizer free prefill pool anyway, the 400 above surfaces the misconfiguration.

For llm-d: the coordinator builds the prefill request from scratch, so it needs no change. The NIXL v2 sidecar reuses the client body for prefill and overrides a fixed set of fields (`stream`, token limits, `kv_transfer_params`). It would need to reset `output_mode` and drop `chat_request` on the prefill request, keeping both for decode. Resetting only `output_mode` leaves `chat_request` on a `tokens` request, which section 6 rejects.

#### 8. Decoupling `--tokens-only`

A decode pool needs the generate API surface *with* a tokenizer. `--tokens-only` currently does four jobs:

| Job | Where | Proposal |
|---|---|---|
| Skip tokenizer init | [arg_utils](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/362a64b21d5038691c929521478b63dcb4828e58/vllm/engine/arg_utils.py#L2385-L2386) | keep |
| Force `detokenize=False` | [factories](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/362a64b21d5038691c929521478b63dcb4828e58/vllm/entrypoints/scale_out/factories.py#L61) → [serving](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/362a64b21d5038691c929521478b63dcb4828e58/vllm/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/serving.py#L249-L250) | keep |
| Register `/abort_requests` | [api_router](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/362a64b21d5038691c929521478b63dcb4828e58/vllm/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/api_router.py#L77) | also register when generate is served on a tokenizer loaded server (open question 4) |
| Imply scale-out endpoints | [factories](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/362a64b21d5038691c929521478b63dcb4828e58/vllm/entrypoints/scale_out/factories.py#L73) | keep |

A decode pool then runs `--enable-scale-out` with a tokenizer and without `--tokens-only`.

#### 9. Parity and shared code

The inline path and `/derender` must produce identical output or clients get different text depending on deployment.

- Both go through the same `Parser` code, with no parallel copy.
- Extend the round-trip parity test (#48617, streaming added in #57922) to assert `generate(output_mode=X)` matches `derender(generate(output_mode="tokens"))` for `text` and `derender`, batch and streaming.
- Streaming derender drops logprobs on `main`, so the streaming logprob checks depend on #55029.
- **Stop strings.** Inline levels follow the engine's stop handling, like `/v1/completions` and `/v1/chat/completions`: a matched stop string is cut from the text unless `include_stop_str_in_output` is set. Token IDs keep every generated token, so decoding them in `/derender` brings the stop string back, plus anything after it in the same token. For requests with `stop`, the test asserts inline output matches the coupled endpoint and that `/derender` output starts with the inline text and differs only after it. The `tokens` leg has to run on a tokenizer-loaded server, since `--tokens-only` rejects `stop` with a 400 (#57058). `OnlineDerenderer.derender_chat` re-decodes token IDs, so the Phase 2 inline path has to apply the stop truncation before parsing.
- **End of stream.** Tests cover a final chunk carrying only buffered text or only a `finish_reason`, including after `/abort_requests` (section 4).

#### 10. Rust frontend

The Rust frontend serves generate over HTTP and gRPC and both need the change. The protocol should be agreed here once and mirrored in both with the Rust frontend owners.

**HTTP.** `rust/src/server/src/routes/inference/generate/types.rs` mirrors `GenerateRequest` / `GenerateResponse`. It takes `output_mode`, `chat_request`, `text`, `message` and `delta` to also mirror the per level response types. For example, with a `#[serde(tag = "output_mode")]` enum that defaults to `tokens` when the tag is missing. The proto keeps optional fields. A proto `oneof` doesn't fit because every level carries `token_ids`.

**gRPC.** `rust/proto/inference.proto` (`Inference.Generate` / `GenerateStream`, enabled with `--grpc-port`) already serves most of the `text` level. It accepts `token_ids` and `kv_transfer_params` and returns decoded `text` on every `SequenceOutput` because `ResponseOptions.output_text` defaults to `true`. That's the reverse of HTTP generate where `tokens` is the default. gRPC shapes responses with per-field `ResponseOptions` flags rather than one mode, so the levels map onto flags:

| Level | gRPC today | Change |
|---|---|---|
| `tokens` | `output_text: false`, `output_token_ids: true` | none |
| `text` | `output_text: true` (default) | resolved logprob tokens |
| `derender` | not supported | `DerenderOptions` on `ResponseOptions`, `ParsedOutput` on `SequenceOutput` |

Proposed additions. All are new fields or messages, so they're wire compatible:

```proto
message ResponseOptions {
  ...
  // Set for the derender level. output_text stays independent.
  // Set it false to drop the raw text.
  optional DerenderOptions derender = 9;
}

message DerenderOptions {
  // Post-adjust_request ChatCompletionRequest (open question 2).
  google.protobuf.Struct chat_request = 1;
}

message SequenceOutput {
  ...
  // Set for the derender level. The full message in Generate, a delta in GenerateStream.
  optional ParsedOutput parsed = 11;
}

message ParsedOutput {
  optional string content = 1;
  optional string reasoning = 2;
  repeated ToolCall tool_calls = 3;
}

message ToolCall {
  uint32 index = 1;
  string id = 2;         // first delta for this index only when streaming
  string name = 3;       // first delta for this index only when streaming
  string arguments = 4;  // full JSON in Generate, a fragment in GenerateStream
}
```

- **Logprobs.** Sampled and candidate logprobs carry token IDs only. `CandidateTokenInfo.TokenInfo` already has `text = 4` and `token_bytes = 5` commented out. The `text` level fills them and adds the same for the sampled token, matching section 5.
- **Finish reason.** `FinishInfo.FinishReason` gains `TOOL_CALLS` for the `finish_reason` rewrite `/derender` does when tool calls were emitted.
- **Parser context.** `chat_request` travels as `google.protobuf.Struct`, the same way `kv_transfer_params` does, until open question 2 settles its shape.
- **Validation.** Section 6's 400s become `INVALID_ARGUMENT`. The no-tokenizer case doesn't come up because the Rust frontend doesn't support `--tokens-only` or `--skip-tokenizer-init` yet and always loads a tokenizer.
- **Streaming.** `GenerateStream` stays server streaming. Parsing runs with the request, so the client has nothing to send after it and bidirectional streaming isn't needed (Alternatives, item 7). `GenerateStream` forwards every decoded event without filtering on new token IDs, so the end of stream gap in section 4 may not apply here. The section 9 tests should confirm it.
- **Parity.** The `derender` level on both Rust surfaces uses the Rust parsers in `rust/src/parser` and depends on the Rust `/derender` work, which has stalled: #53223 closed unmerged on 2026-09-17 and the draft follow-ups #53418 / #53419 haven't moved since 2026-09-10. The Rust `derender` level needs someone to pick that stack back up. The section 9 parity tests also run against the Rust frontend so Rust and Python produce the same output.
- **Release.** The proto change ships with a `vllm-proto` version bump in the same PR, checked by `cargo-semver-checks` (see `rust/proto/README.md`).
- **Out of scope.** `vllm serve --grpc` uses the external `smg-grpc-servicer` package with its own proto.

#### 11. Phasing

| Phase | Scope | PR(s)
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `output_mode` field, `text` level (batch and streaming), logprob resolution, validation, `/abort_requests` decoupling, docs, latency benchmarks (section 12) | #58588 |
| 2 | `derender` level, batch: `chat_request` context, `message` on the choice, reusing `OnlineDerenderer.derender_chat` | |
| 3 | `derender` level, streaming: request-scoped parsers, `delta` on stream choices, parity CI extension, latency benchmarks (section 12) | |
| — | Rust frontend mirror, tracked with the Rust frontend owners | |

#### 12. Latency benchmarks

The CPU numbers above don't cover latency. The Phase 1 and Phase 3 PRs report TTFT and TPOT for:

- inline `text` / `derender` against generate plus streaming derender, across concurrency levels and response lengths.
- `tokens` requests on the same pod, with and without `text` or `derender` traffic mixed in.

#### Alternatives considered

1. **Streaming derender as-is (#47161).** Keeps the GPU tier tokenizer free but puts a round trip and echoed state on every chunk, plus replay for parsed output. It stays the right tool for stateless postprocessing (RL, batch, gateways that own postprocessing). This RFC complements it and doesn't replace it.
2. **The gateway composes generate + derender.** The per chunk hop moves from client to gateway rather than going away. Holding state in the gateway instead means reimplementing postprocessing there.
3. **Server-side derender sessions keyed by `request_id`.** Rejected in #47161 (Option B) over session lifecycle, eviction and memory. The derender tier has no live request to attach state to. The generate server does.
4. **Token IDs on `/v1/chat/completions`.** Complementary, not a replacement. Chat only takes token IDs through `kv_transfer_params["prompt_token_ids"]` (#48145) and #55771 proposes a first class `prompt_token_ids` field. That serves routers that already use the OpenAI format and tokenize to pick a replica. It doesn't serve orchestrators on the generate format because a render produced `GenerateRequest` carries resolved `SamplingParams` that don't map back onto OpenAI request fields without resolving. They would therefore have to support two wire formats. The reverse holds too. `output_mode` doesn't help OpenAI format routers because they'd need a `/render` hop, `--enable-scale-out` on the engines and a wrap into `chat.completion`, even at the `derender` level.
5. **Run the coupled OpenAI server on decode pools.** Decode pods leave the generate protocol with the same
   two format problem as (4).
6. **Reuse `sampling_params.detokenize` as the switch.** It defaults to `True`, so every existing response on a
   tokenizer loaded server would grow text and token only clients would pay for detokenization by default.
7. **gRPC bidirectional streaming derender** (suggested by @andylolu2 on slack). The client opens one bidi stream to the derender tier, sends the parser context once, then forwards each generate chunk. The parser lives on the stream until it closes. That removes the echoed `stream_state`, the per chunk `chat_request` and replay. It also answers the lifecycle and eviction objections behind (3) because state lasts exactly as long as the stream. It doesn't remove the hop though. Every chunk still passes from the generate stream through the derender stream on the TPOT path and clients would need gRPC next to the HTTP generate format. If a derender replica fails mid stream, the parser state goes with it and the client has to reconnect and replay. A WebSocket would give the same stream lifetime on the HTTP stack. This complements the RFC rather than replacing it. It fits #57571 as an alternative to the parser cache for consumers that want a tokenizer free GPU tier.

#### Costs and risks

- **CPU on the decode host.** Detokenization and parsing run in the API server process, not the engine core. They don't block the scheduler but they use host CPU. `text` adds little on a tokenizer loaded server because detokenization already runs there today. Parsing and logprob resolution are the new work. In the benchmark, with the GPU saturated, the in-process frontend stayed under 0.25 of a core for chat, reasoning and tool-calling traffic (24–144 µs per token), at least 3.5× headroom over the GPU's token rate. That was one A100 and a faster GPU narrows the gap.
  `--api-server-count` scales the frontend if it becomes the limit. Dense logprobs are the exception (section 5). Opt-in per request bounds the cost to the traffic that asks for it.
- **Parser config drift.** Decode pools need the same `--reasoning-parser`, `--tool-call-parser` and `--enable-auto-tool-choice` as the render tier. That's the same obligation the derender tier already has.
- **Two call sites for postprocessing.** Mitigated by shared `Parser` code and the parity CI in section 9.
- **Security.** The inline path postprocesses engine produced tokens bounded by the request's resolved limits. It doesn't accept caller supplied output token IDs the way `/derender` does, so it doesn't need `/derender`'s explicit bounds checks. `chat_request` is caller supplied and needs the same validation as on the chat and derender endpoints.

#### Open questions

1. ~**Response shape.**~ RESOLVED. An extended generate format with `text` / `message` / `delta` (proposed) or return `ChatCompletionResponse` / `ChatCompletionStreamResponse` directly for `output_mode="derender"`? The latter is a drop-in for existing `/derender` consumers but the endpoint's response schema would then depend on a request field and the generate only fields would need a home. *Feedback so far:*
   - @nilig supports extending the generate response format (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/56851#issuecomment-5692634586).
   - @DarkLight1337 prefers separate response classes per `output_mode` for type checking (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/56851#issuecomment-5794326266).
2. **Parser context.** Embed the post-`adjust_request` `chat_request` (proposed), or have `/render` emit a slim derender context (`tools`, `tool_choice`, `chat_template_kwargs`, plus `adjust_request`-derived state) that clients pass through? The slim form is smaller but first needs a settled answer to the open `adjust_request` question from #42729. *Feedback so far:*
   - #42729 now proposes re-running `adjust_request` on the derender side. Once that's settled it answers this one too.
3. **Naming.** `output_mode` with `tokens | text | derender`, or something else?
4. **`/abort_requests`.** Register it whenever generate is served, add a separate flag or leave it tied to `--tokens-only`? *Feedback so far:*
   - @nilig wants it whenever generate is served, including on decode pools that load a tokenizer (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/56851#issuecomment-5692634586).
   - #55521 adds a general `/abort_requests` on every `vllm serve` server, where an empty or missing `request_ids` aborts all in-flight requests. The scale-out route returns 400 for a missing `request_ids`. If #55521 lands, the two routes clash on `--tokens-only` servers and the semantics need to be reconciled. That would also answer this question.
5. **Completions shaped parsing.** Is `text` enough for completions shaped clients or does anyone need reasoning/tool parsing on completions? Parsing on `/v1/completions/derender` is chat-only today. *Feedback so far:*
   - @shimib's logprob-heavy traffic is completions shaped and needs `text` plus resolved logprobs, not parsing (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/56851#issuecomment-5685698033).
   - #42729 records that completions don't parse, which matches @shimib's feedback. #57922 documented it in `derenderer.md`.

### Feedback Period.

_No response_

### CC List.

@chaunceyjiang @DarkLight1337 @vMaroon @NickLucche @nilig @njhill @robertgshaw2-redhat @sagearc @BugenZhao

### Any Other Things.

**Related work**
- #47161 / #50550: streaming derender and its parse path. Complementary to this RFC (Alternatives, item 1).
- #47313: adds `stop_reason` to generate response choices. It touches the same protocol and serving files, and the matched stop string would let `/derender` cut its text there too (section 9).
- #36983 / #51641: `delta_text` and `delta_token_ids` desync when stop strings are buffered. Streaming `text` inherits this and should use the fix.
- #53223 / #53418 / #53419: Rust `/derender` endpoints. #53223 closed unmerged and the drafts have stalled (section 10).
- #47933: emits the terminal `finish_reason` chunk on `tokens` streams, including after an abort (section 4).
- #55029: resolved logprobs on streaming derender chunks. The streaming logprob parity checks in section 9 need it.

**Related bug: #57052.** Stop strings break on the scale-out token path in two ways. On `--tokens-only` servers `stop` was silently ignored and generation ran to EOS or `max_tokens` with a 200. #57058 fixed that and the server now returns 400. On the derender side the stop text leaks back into the output because `/derender` re-decodes every token ID (section 9). That part is still open. Once decode pools run with a tokenizer, `stop` works there too.

**Out of scope**
- Skipping detokenization for `output_mode="tokens"` on tokenizer loaded servers where today it runs and its output is discarded. It's a worthwhile performance follow up but it changes existing behavior (`stop` strings need detok).
- Any change to `/derender` itself.

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Bug]: Explicit scalar CUDA graph maximum can drop a required uniform-decode shape
body:
### Your current environment

The configuration-level reproducer below does not require a GPU.

- vLLM `main`: `76ba32160a501e5e8aadb5e1820c51c765714220`
- Also observed with vLLM 0.28.0: `2cf0a6915ce544dc493a0990f2ea38d81601128a`
- Python 3.12.3, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130
- Runtime validation: two NVIDIA DGX Spark systems (GB10), driver 580.173.02,
  CUDA 13.0, Ubuntu 24.04.4 aarch64

### Describe the bug

When `CompilationConfig.max_cudagraph_capture_size` is set explicitly but
`cudagraph_capture_sizes` is left unset, `_set_cudagraph_sizes()` builds the
default stepped grid and silently truncates the scalar maximum to the largest
grid entry.

For static speculative decoding with `max_num_seqs=6` and six speculative
tokens, the widest uniform decode batch is:

```text
6 requests * (1 sampled token + 6 speculative tokens) = 42 tokens
```

Setting `max_cudagraph_capture_size=42` currently produces a capture list that
ends at 40 and changes the resolved maximum to 40. The model-runner-v2 CUDA
graph manager rounds the 40-token candidate to the seven-token query width,
gets 42, then rejects it because 42 exceeds the resolved maximum of 40. The C6
verification step therefore dispatches eager.

#### Minimal reproducer

```python
from types import SimpleNamespace
from unittest.mock import MagicMock

from vllm.config import (
    CompilationConfig,
    CUDAGraphMode,
    ParallelConfig,
    SchedulerConfig,
    VllmConfig,
)

compilation_config = CompilationConfig(
    cudagraph_mode=CUDAGraphMode.FULL_AND_PIECEWISE,
    max_cudagraph_capture_size=42,
)
config = MagicMock(spec=VllmConfig)
config.compilation_config = compilation_config
config.scheduler_config = SchedulerConfig.default_factory(
    max_num_seqs=6,
    max_num_batched_tokens=8192,
)
config.parallel_config = ParallelConfig()
config.model_config = MagicMock(enforce_eager=False)
config.performance_mode = None
config.diffusion_config = None
config.speculative_config = SimpleNamespace(
    num_speculative_tokens=6,
    num_speculative_tokens_per_batch_size=None,
    uses_dynamic_speculative_decoding=lambda: False,
)
config.num_speculative_tokens = VllmConfig.num_speculative_tokens.fget(config)
config.uniform_decode_query_len = VllmConfig.uniform_decode_query_len.fget(config)

VllmConfig._set_cudagraph_sizes(config)
print(compilation_config.max_cudagraph_capture_size)
print(compilation_config.cudagraph_capture_sizes)
```

Actual output on current `main`:

```text
WARNING ... Truncating max_cudagraph_capture_size to 40
40
[1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 24, 32, 40]
```

Expected output:

```text
42
[1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 24, 32, 40, 42]
```

The expectation is not that every scalar maximum must necessarily become a
capture size. It is that a schedulable uniform decode shape that fits within an
explicit scalar bound is not discarded merely because it is off the inferred
8/16-token stride. An explicit `cudagraph_capture_sizes` list should remain
authoritative.

### Measured serving impact

We reproduced this with DeepSeek V4 Flash Vision, DSpark static K=6,
`max_num_seqs=6`, and an otherwise matched two-node/two-rank configuration.
Five p256/C6 trials were run in each lane:

| C6 median | Inferred list ending at 40 | Exact 42 included |
|---|---:|---:|
| Decode/request | 30.4 tok/s | 27.0 tok/s |
| Aggregate throughput | 25.3 tok/s | 133.3 tok/s |
| TTFT | 26.016 s | 0.839 s |

Adding the 42-token capture removes the eager verification step, improving
aggregate throughput by 5.27x and reducing TTFT by 96.8%. Startup shape probes
also completed 47/47 in 30 seconds, compared with 85 seconds before the fix.

### Related work and duplicate check

- #50488 added uniform-decode shapes when vLLM computes the default scalar
  ceiling; #54418 subsequently kept those defaults within the platform memory
  ceiling. The explicit scalar branch still does not populate
  `uniform_decode_sizes`.
- Open PR #37865 addresses the same externally visible truncation by appending
  every explicit scalar maximum to the inferred grid. It is currently stale
  and conflicted. A narrower alternative is to append only the widest
  schedulable uniform-decode shape when it fits within the scalar maximum,
  leaving unrelated scalar bounds and explicit capture-size lists unchanged.

Because #37865 overlaps this bug, I am not opening a competing PR without
maintainer/author coordination. I have a rebased two-file patch and regression
test ready if the narrower semantics are preferred.

This investigation and candidate patch used OpenAI Codex assistance. The
reproducer and measurements were run on the systems described above.

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and open PRs for
  `max_cudagraph_capture_size`, uniform decode, off-stride capture sizes, and
  speculative CUDA graphs.

title: [Bug]: guidance backend rejects tool-calling structural tags (KeyError: 'triggers') — strict/required/named tool_choice broken
body:
### Your current environment

Verified on the official `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.28.0` Docker image (llguidance 1.7.6, xgrammar 0.2.3) and on the current nightly image (`vllm 0.28.1rc1.dev337+g27a94d1ce`, built 2026-09-03) — same failure, same line. The failure happens at request validation time, so it is model-, GPU- and traffic-independent.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

With `--structured-outputs-config '{"backend": "guidance"}'`, any tool-calling request that produces a structural tag is rejected before the first token with:

```
vllm.exceptions.VLLMValidationError: Invalid grammar specification: 'triggers'
```

This affects every request where the tool parser emits a structural tag, i.e. with a hermes-style parser:

- `tool_choice="auto"` with at least one `strict: true` tool,
- `tool_choice="required"`,
- named tool choice.

OpenAI-SDK clients commonly set `strict: true` on tools (pydantic-ai does it by default), so in practice tool calling is broken for those clients whenever the guidance backend is selected. Non-streaming requests get an HTTP 400; streaming requests get an in-stream error payload after the 200.

**Cause**: tool parsers build structural tags in the new xgrammar-style format, `{"type": "structural_tag", "format": {...}}` (via `vllm/tool_parsers/structural_tag_registry.py`), but `serialize_guidance_grammar` in `vllm/v1/structured_output/backend_guidance.py` only understands the legacy `{"triggers": [...], "structures": [...]}` shape and immediately does `s_tag["triggers"]` → `KeyError`, wrapped by `validate_guidance_grammar`. `backend_xgrammar.py` handles both formats (it branches on `"structures" in s_tag`); the guidance backend was never updated when the new format was introduced.

### Minimal reproduction (no GPU, no weights)

```python
import json
from vllm.entrypoints.openai.chat_completion.protocol import ChatCompletionToolsParam
from vllm.tool_parsers.structural_tag_registry import get_model_structural_tag
from vllm.v1.structured_output.backend_guidance import serialize_guidance_grammar
from vllm.v1.structured_output.backend_types import StructuredOutputOptions

tools = [ChatCompletionToolsParam(**{
    "type": "function",
    "function": {
        "name": "get_weather",
        "strict": True,
        "parameters": {"type": "object",
                       "properties": {"city": {"type": "string"}},
                       "required": ["city"]},
    },
})]

st = get_model_structural_tag("hermes", tools, "auto", False)
serialize_guidance_grammar(StructuredOutputOptions.STRUCTURAL_TAG, json.dumps(st.model_dump()))
```

```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/tmp/r.py", line 21, in <module>
    serialize_guidance_grammar(StructuredOutputOptions.STRUCTURAL_TAG, spec)
  File ".../vllm/v1/structured_output/backend_guidance.py", line 267, in serialize_guidance_grammar
    triggers: list[str] = s_tag["triggers"]
                          ~~~~~^^^^^^^^^^^^
KeyError: 'triggers'
```

### Server-level reproduction

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser hermes \
  --structured-outputs-config '{"backend": "guidance"}'
```

```bash
curl -s http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{
  "model": "Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B",
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "What is the weather in Paris?"}],
  "tools": [{"type": "function", "function": {"name": "get_weather", "strict": true,
    "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"city": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["city"]}}}],
  "tool_choice": "auto"
}'
```

→ `{"error":{"message":"Invalid grammar specification: 'triggers'", ...}}` (the same request without `"strict": true` works). `tool_choice="required"` and named tool choice fail identically, even without `strict`.

### Related finding

While fixing this we noticed the legacy path has a second problem: it passes the output of `LLMatcher.grammar_from_json_schema` (a serialized `{"grammars": [...]}` envelope) as `llguidance.StructTag.grammar`, which llguidance silently interprets as an empty JSON schema — so tool-call arguments were effectively unconstrained even when the legacy format worked.

I have a fix that translates the new-format structural tags (`triggered_tags`, `tags_with_separator`, `any_text`, as emitted by the tool-parser registry) into llguidance grammars and rejects unsupported shapes with a clear error; it has been running in production for us. PR coming shortly, with the legacy-path schema fix as a separate commit (easy to split out if preferred).

title: [Performance]: MoE decode ~15% slower on SM12x since #56876 (DeepGEMM contiguous-layout alignment 128 instead of 64)
body:
### Report of performance regression

Since #56876 moved DeepGEMM to vllm-project/DeepGEMM `e1f418c2`, `get_theoretical_mk_alignment_for_contiguous_layout` returns 128 on SM12x. DeepGEMM 2.6.1 (`8b1392b9`) returned 64 when each expert gets at most 64 rows. The fork's SM120 port (vllm-project/DeepGEMM#4) left that rule unwired. vLLM pads the contiguous MoE layout with this alignment, so decode pads twice as many rows and the grouped GEMMs run with `BLOCK_M=128`.

DGX Spark (GB10, SM121), Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8, DFlash (7 speculative tokens), TP1, vLLM main 70fc359d (official cu130 aarch64 wheel). Server-side time per decode step:

| | 1 request | 16 requests |
|---|---|---|
| main | 56.6 ms | 173.7 ms |
| main + diff below | 50.2 ms | 146.5 ms |
| c81ace18 build (before #56876) | 50.5 ms | 149.0 ms |

With nsys at 16 requests, the MoE grouped GEMMs and the SiLU-mul/quant kernels account for 23.5 of the 23.7 ms difference. Greedy output is identical with and without the diff.

### Proposal to improve performance

Port the SM12x rule from deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM#447 into vllm-project/DeepGEMM and bump the pin, or restore it in vLLM's wrapper. This is equivalent to the patch measured above:

```diff
--- a/vllm/utils/deep_gemm.py
+++ b/vllm/utils/deep_gemm.py
@@ -382,6 +382,13 @@ def get_theoretical_mk_alignment_for_contiguous_layout(
     _lazy_init()
     if _get_theoretical_mk_alignment_for_contiguous_layout_impl is None:
         return _missing()
+    if current_platform.is_device_capability_family(120):
+        # vllm-project/DeepGEMM returns 128 on SM12x; 2.6.1 used 64 when each
+        # expert gets at most 64 rows.
+        per_group_m = expected_m
+        if expected_m is not None and num_groups:
+            per_group_m = cdiv(expected_m, num_groups)
+        return 64 if per_group_m is not None and per_group_m <= 64 else 128
     if num_groups is None:
         return _get_theoretical_mk_alignment_for_contiguous_layout_impl(expected_m)
     if num_groups <= 0:
```

From reading the code only (not measured): on SM10x the fork returns a fixed 256 regardless of `expected_m`, so the alignment no longer shrinks below 128, where 2.6.1 went down to 32 for small per-expert M. Small-batch decode on B200/GB200 may be affected the same way.

I'm not planning to open a PR for this, so it's free for anyone to pick up.

title: [Performance]: multimodal preprocessing is single-threaded per API server; a wider thread pool does not help (GIL) — process pool for _mm_executor?
body:
### Proposal to improve performance

**Summary.** For a VLM serving one image per request, the renderer's single-worker multimodal executor (`vllm/renderers/base.py`, `_mm_executor = ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=1)`, "must stay single-worker per #38418") is a hard wall in front of the engine, and a wider *thread* pool barely moves it: with the cache disabled (so #38418 does not apply) I widened it on a B300 host — **2 threads: +20 % render throughput (14.0 → 16.8 pages/s); 6 threads: −70 % (→ 4 pages/s), GPU starved**. The GIL, not the cache, is the constraint. Proposal: run multimodal preprocessing in a **process pool**, sized by a config value, default 1 worker as today.

### Report of performance regression

Not a regression between versions — a measurement of the executor's shape at `v0.29.0`.

**Setup.** Qwen3.5-VL-class 4B model (custom weights), 1 × B300, 8 vCPU (Modal), `--max-num-seqs 16 --max-num-queued-reqs 216 --mm-processor-cache-gb 0 --no-enable-prefix-caching --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":1}'`, `mm_processor_kwargs max_pixels=3145728`. Client: 300 simultaneous chat completions each carrying one inline 1275×1650 PNG (218 KB, ~2.1 k prompt tokens), `max_tokens = min_tokens = 1024`; then an open loop of 20 requests/s for 60 s with 16-token decodes, so the GPU drains faster than the render and the render alone sets the rate. "Pre-engine wait" is `time_to_first_token − time_in_model_prefill − time_in_queue` from the `llm_request` trace span (the time between `arrival_time` and the engine seeing the request — i.e. the renderer). A plugin replaced `_mm_executor` after `BaseRenderer.__init__` with a K-worker `ThreadPoolExecutor` (re-binding `_process_multimodal_async` / `_clear_mm_cache_async` via `make_async`) and set `set_default_torch_num_threads()`'s default to `8 // K` (also tried 8 per worker — same result).

| MM executor workers (torch intra-op threads each) | 300 at once: served p50 / p99 | pre-engine wait p50 / max | engine queue (`time_in_queue`) max | container CPU p50 (of 8 cores) | GPU util p50 | 20 rps × 60 s: pages/s served |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **1 (8)** — today | 17.5 s / 28.5 s | 8.0 s / 14.5 s | 9.8 s | 1.4 (6.7 in the steady run) | 58 % | **14.0** |
| 2 (4) | 17.4 s / 28.3 s | 6.7 s / 11.7 s | 12.1 s | 1.4 (6.9 in the steady run) | 57 % | **16.8** (1200/1200 served, 0 refused; p50 8.8 s vs 13.3 s) |
| 6 (1) | **29.7 s / 57.1 s** | **27.3 s / 54.2 s** | **0** | 4.4 | 60 % | **4.2** |
| 6 (8) | — | — | 0 | 3.7 | 15 % | **3.8** |

Outputs at temperature 0 were byte-identical across configurations (30 requests, image by URL and inline); no errors or crashes in any configuration — thread-safety was not the problem.

**Reading.** Two threads help a little (the second thread overlaps the first's GIL-free tensor ops). With six render threads the engine's queue never forms and GPU utilisation drops: the renderer got *slower* in aggregate, and CPU utilisation fell rather than rose. That is the GIL-convoy signature: the HF processor's torch/numpy ops release and re-acquire the GIL per op, and with K render threads plus the event loop contending, every re-acquire waits a scheduling round, so a render that takes ~70 ms alone takes seconds abreast. The single worker's ~6.7 busy cores are its own intra-op threads (which is also why going from 8 to 16 vCPUs changed nothing for the single worker in an earlier run: the ops do not scale past ~8 threads).

**Why the cache guard is not the limit here.** #38418 (closing #38375) guards the multimodal processor *cache* — the LRU/SHM sender/receiver caches are not thread-safe and assume P0's insertion order at P1 — and #49524 kept `_mm_executor` single-worker for that reason. With `--mm-processor-cache-gb 0`, `processor_cache_from_config` returns `None`, the engine core builds no receiver cache, and (with prefix caching off) `_process_mm_uuids` names every item per request; nothing is shared between requests. The remaining path is already thread-safe (`maybe_make_thread_pool`'s tokenizer copies, `AtomicCounter`). So a wider thread pool is *safe* in this configuration — it is just not faster.

**What would help.**
1. A `ProcessPoolExecutor` (or a small pool of forked/spawned preprocessing workers) for the CPU-bound part of `_process_multimodal`, sized by a config value (default 1 = today's behaviour), refused when the processor cache is enabled (the existing #38418 rule). The processed `MultiModalKwargs` would cross a process boundary once more (they already cross to the engine core), so the cost is one extra serialization of `pixel_values` per request — small against the ~70 ms render, and the GIL is per process.
2.
